229	### 2. Screen recordings with the cursor as data
230	
231	**Pitch.** The recorder stops burning the pointer and click rings into the picture. Beside the movie it saves the cursor's path and image and every click. If the creator opts in, it also saves the shortcuts pressed. When the recording lands:
232	
233	- zoom actions already sit on the action lane at each click and each burst of typing;
234	- the cursor is its own layer, which can be made bigger, restyled, smoothed or hidden when idle, and gets click ripples;
235	- each shortcut appears as a Keyboard keys overlay;
236	- long typing stretches can be sped up.
237	
238	All of it is ordinary actions, clips and graphics that the creator can drag or delete. Recordings made before this ships, and imported screen videos, behave as today.
239	
240	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** The polished-screencast category rests on cursor data:
241	
242	- Screen Studio zooms where clicks happened [S2] and edits the cursor after recording [S3];
243	- Prequel stores the pointer as data [S19];
244	- Cap [S16], FocuSee [S18], Tella [S11] and Camtasia [S8] [S9] do the same.
245	
246	Frame Job's recorder stores none of it, so Frame Job loses its own home segment to a recorder that costs about $29 a month [S7]. This bet brings Frame Job level on polish. It pulls ahead because those recorders are shallow editors and Frame Job is a full one. Its auto zooms are actions on a real timeline, next to grading, the audio chain, captions and graphics, and an agent can re-plan them ("zoom only on the clicks in the settings pane").
247	
248	Being free is not unique by itself. OpenScreen is a free, MIT-licensed Screen Studio alternative with about 40,000 stars, archived after v1.5.0 [S23], and Cap sells a $58 lifetime licence [S17].
249	
250	**Builds on.** `RecordingSetup.swift`, which sets `showsCursor` and `showMouseClicks` today; `add_zoom_action` (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`); `add_speed_ramp`; the Keyboard keys graphic template; the recorder panel's grants; `recipe_layer.rs`; `MediaConsolidator` and relink.
251	
252	**Effort.** L.
253	
254	**Risks and what comes first.**
255	- Spec §11 (`recording.md`) decides three things this bet reverses: the cursor and click ring are taken as drawn and nothing is reconstructed; callouts stay out; a recording is ordinary media, with no source kind and no schema bump. The owner amends §11 first, as CAM-1 did for the camera.
256	- Shortcuts need the Input Monitoring grant, which `RecorderStatusItem.swift` deliberately avoids today. Key capture should be opt-in and record only modifier shortcuts by default. It must never record secure fields, and it must show plainly when it is on.
257	- The cursor must follow the screen clip's own transform and zoom actions. It has to be drawn as part of that clip's layer, or the two have to be nested with the zooms on the nest. A sprite on another track would drift.
258	- `NSCursor.currentSystem` is marked deprecated in macOS 27.0 in Apple's availability metadata, so a replacement is needed.
259	- The sidecar cannot be regenerated, so Consolidate and Relink must carry it.
260	- Timing can anchor on the screen's first-frame time, which the camera spike measured within 0.5 ms. Issue #370 is a microphone-offset problem and is not inherited.
261	- Motion blur on zooms needs sub-frame sampling and is out of scope.
262	- Code from AGPL-licensed recorders is not carried over, the same rule as for Concat.
263	
264	### 3. Make Vertical Version
265	
266	**Pitch.** File ▸ Make Vertical Version… writes a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac. It does this with ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. In a screen recording made after bet 2, it follows the cursor instead. Captions re-lay for the short side, and graphics re-layout from the canvas size. A shot that cannot be cropped gets Add Blurred Background.
267	
268	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes. OpusClip [C11], CapCut [C4], Premiere [P21], Final Cut Pro for iPad [P17], Riverside [C9], Kapwing [C20] and Screen Studio [S1] all ship it, and auto-repurposing is the most-wanted creator AI feature in one survey [D2]. Frame Job pulls ahead on terms. CapCut moved Auto Reframe behind Pro in April 2026 [C4]. Here it is free and local, and the result is editable pan actions rather than a render. If the owner chooses linked versions (one cut, with a framing per shape), Frame Job is ahead of every rival, because their vertical copies drift from the master.
269	
270	**Builds on.** `fill_scale` (`edit_fit.rs`); Add Blurred Background (`edit_background.rs`); word captions sized to the shorter side (`CaptionStyle.swift`); graphics that read `ctx.canvas`; actions (`edit_action.rs`); nests (`edit_nest.rs`); `set_canvas` (`edit_canvas.rs`); File ▸ Duplicate; the E9 Vision spike in `tools/proof/effects_spike/`.
271	
272	**Effort.** M as a regenerated copy. L for linked versions, which need a canvas per version, framing overrides per clip and a format bump.
273	
274	**Risks and what comes first.**
275	- Spec §1 lists auto-reframe as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it first. The reason given there, heavy pixel work outside the one-pass compositor, no longer applies: the analysis runs offline and its output is actions.
276	- No two actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. A clip that already carries an action (a zoom, a grade, a ramp) needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas freezes at the size it was nested at.
277	- `set_canvas` does not rescale action end states. A screencast's existing zoom actions keep their 16:9 targets, and the planner must rewrite them.
278	- `MediaCacheLane` is a width-2 lane for audio decodes, so video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows.
279	- The planner should use face, human and saliency rectangles with tracking, not masks: the E9 spike found that foreground masks flicker on video.
280	- Two people in frame, a speaker leaving the frame, and shot changes inside one flattened clip each need a rule.
281	
282	### 4. Find Clips
283	
284	**Pitch.** Clip ▸ Find Clips…, run on an episode, a VOD or a finished edit, lists 10 to 30 candidates of 20 to 60 seconds. Each candidate shows:
285	
286	- in and out points snapped to sentence ends;
287	- its length;
288	- a one-line reason, such as "laughter after the punchline";
289	- a preview.
290	
291	There is no virality score. Make Short turns the checked candidates into vertical projects through bet 3. Each short is word-captioned, has fillers removed where a cloud transcript exists, and is queued for export.
292	
293	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Long-to-short is what OpusClip [C10] [C12], Riverside [C9], Submagic [C14] and Kapwing [C20] sell, all metered by credits. YouTube's own free tool covers only 10 countries and 7 languages [D9]. Frame Job pulls ahead in three ways:
294	
295	- **Local signals.** Laughter, applause and cheering from Sound Analysis, the 10 ms loudness, speech spans and sentence ends are all measured on the Mac.
296	- **The creator's own key.** Ranking runs on the creator's Claude key, with no per-minute credits.
297	- **Real timelines.** Each candidate opens as an editable timeline.
298	
299	A stated reason for each moment, rather than a score, answers the documented complaint that clippers cut in the wrong place [D16].
300	
301	**Builds on.** `get_transcript` (timeline ticks); `ClipLoudness.swift` and the per-media loudness cache; `media_speech.rs`; `detect_fillers` and `ripple_delete_ranges`; caption Restyle with Replace; the Export Queue; the Assistant helper (`agent/`) and its price table; `set_range`.
302	
303	**Effort.** M on top of bet 3. Without bet 3 it produces horizontal clips only.
304	
305	**Risks and what comes first.**
306	- Ranking quality is the whole product.
307	- On-device FoundationModels has a 4,096-token context and needs Apple Intelligence turned on. It is a chunked, weaker fallback, not an equal path.
308	- Speaker labels exist only on AssemblyAI transcripts requested with speakers.
309	- No op copies a timeline range into a new project: `new_project` takes a path, and Duplicate copies everything. One is needed.
310	- Sound Analysis (`SNClassifySoundRequest` `.version1`, 303 labels on macOS 26.5.1, laughter, applause and cheering among them) is noisy on game audio and music beds.
311	- Long transcripts cost tokens, so show an estimate range before running.
312	
313	### 5. Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file
314	
315	**Pitch.** The creator brings two to four cameras and a mic per person, lines them up with Synchronize Audio, and chooses Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking, judging each mic's speech spans against that mic's own noise floor. It uses the wide shot during crosstalk and holds a minimum shot length. The whole switch is one undo step, and every cut is an ordinary split the creator can roll or re-pick. OBS multitrack files and multichannel recorder files import every audio track, not only the first.
316	
317	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Automatic switching is sold as AutoPod for about $29 a month [D14], as Resolve SmartSwitch in Studio [P8], and inside hand-off or metered tools such as Eddie [C32] and Descript. Premiere users have asked for it for years [D13], and video podcasts are the fastest-growing creator format [D10] [D11] [D12]. Frame Job already owns the hard audio half: drift-corrected sync, cached speech spans, the loudness cache, Match Audio, Enhance Voice, the leveller, a −16 LUFS target and stems. Adding the picture half makes it a free podcast editor. An agent can also re-run the switch with new rules, such as "cut to wide whenever both laugh".
318	
319	**Builds on.** `AudioSync*.swift` (alignment as `move_clip` and `set_speed`); `SileroVAD.swift` and `media_speech.rs`; `audio_duck_speech.rs`; `ClipLoudness.swift`; `set_enabled` (a clip with its picture disabled is not decoded, per `nest.rs` `shows_video`); `ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`; `core/src/container.rs` and every `CompositionBuilder.firstTrack` audio caller.
320	
321	**Effort.** M for speaker switching on stacked tracks plus every audio track. L for a multicam clip with an angle grid and live overrides.
322	
323	**Risks and what comes first.**
324	- Spec §1 lists multicam as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it, either narrowly (stacked tracks) or fully.
325	- Reading every audio track touches every `firstTrack(.audio)` caller: the builder, Silence, the isolation, ramp, voice and reverse renderers, and the transcription extract. It needs a format bump.
326	- Splitting linked picture and sound halves of three angles every 8 s for two hours gives about 5,400 clips, which is over the 4,096 cap. The switch should cut picture only and keep the mics whole.
327	- Mic bleed can mislead the switch, and one-mic shows need Vision mouth activity instead.
328	- Transitions decode both angles. Decoding three or four 4K angles has not been measured (see the next tier).
329	- Zoom and Riverside already deliver one file per participant, so the multitrack fix chiefly serves OBS and multichannel WAV.
330	
331	### 6. Camera cutout and layouts
332	
333	**Pitch.** The creator ticks Remove Background on a camera clip. Vision segments the person on the Mac, rendered in the background the way Reverse is. A Layout pop-up switches the camera at the playhead, with an animated move, between:
334	
335	- corner bubble (circle or rounded);
336	- side by side;
337	- stacked for vertical;
338	- camera full;
339	- screen only.
340	
341	"Hide camera while silent" fades the camera out during pauses. Text Behind Subject follows from cutout: a title sits between the person and their background.
342	
343	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** This is mostly catch-up. Screen Studio 4 (cutout in beta) [S6], Cap 0.6 [S16], Tella [S11], Prequel [S19] and Loom [S13] shipped camera cutout or layouts in September and October 2026. Final Cut Pro [P14], Premiere [P2] and Resolve [P8] ship one-click subject masks. Frame Job's recorded camera is fixed in the bottom-right corner. It pulls ahead only in combination: layouts are actions any agent can write, the camera gets Frame Job's grading and LUT engine, and with bet 2 the whole screencast polish lives inside a full editor.
344	
345	**Builds on.** Issue #124 and its E9 Vision spike; `ReverseRenderer`, `ReverseCache`, `BackgroundRender` and `MediaCacheLedger`; matte tracks (`recipe_matte.rs`); actions over transform, crop, corner radius and shadow; Add Background; the speech spans of the microphone media.
346	
347	**Effort.** L.
348	
349	**Risks and what comes first.**
350	- Edge quality on hair is a risk. Balanced person masks are 512×384 and likely need a refinement pass. Accurate masks run at 1.7× realtime and take 1.7 GiB per minute.
351	- Non-person masks flicker on video, so non-person cutout is for stills only.
352	- A mask on a Luma matte track has no link to the camera clip and drifts on trims, splits and speed changes. A per-layer mask with a format bump is the sound design.
353	- Issue #124's `texture(2)` binding is stale: looks now hold texture 2 and curves texture 3.
354	- The camera clip has no sound of its own, so hide-while-silent reads the microphone's spans through the microphone clip.
355	- Spec §1's ML non-goal, and issue #124's proposed decision D5, must enter §11 first.
356	- The 8-decoder budget is a warning, not a refusal. HLG projects need the mask in the right working space.

358	### The next tier
359	
360	- **Proposals: play an agent's multi-step edit before it lands (M; Recipes later, also M).** Only Frame Job can do this cheaply. Handles are immutable. The export pin already renders a project that is not the current one. `performGroupedEdit` already makes one undo step from many. An agent's turn becomes a side chain the creator plays and compares A/B with the current cut, then accepts as one named step or rejects. This answers the 44% who want to review or undo and the 37% who want to see what the agent does [D4]. It amends spec §11 AI-10, which accepted ten Undos for a ten-call turn. It matters most once bets 1 and 4 produce agent-driven batches. Recipes come after Proposals and need three things: tool allow-lists enforced by the gate, because a shared recipe is a prompt-injection path; cost shown as an estimate range, because `pricing.ts` prices a run after it happens; and prompts served from `mcp-proxy`, because `core/src/agent.rs` is generic code.
361	- **Punch in on cuts (S).** Alternates scale between about 100% and 112% across cuts within one take, centred on the face, with `set_video` x, y and scale as one grouped step. It is free and exact, and needs no disclosure. Ship it right after bet 1's first phase.
362	- **Source ranges, skimming, In and Out, favourite ranges (M).** `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` gain a source range, and `opTool` prints it into the MCP tools automatically. This is the precondition for placing a found moment and for a clean restore in bet 1. Add proxies only after a measurement shows a shortfall, under a recorded decision on a playback-only builder input.
363	- **Caption styles, brand kit and project templates (M).** Colour controls are safe under spec §11 W-10. Size and font changes need re-paging or a W-10 amendment. Per-word emphasis and emoji need a `model_words.rs` field and a format bump under W-2 and W-3. Whether emoji render correctly in HLG projects is unverified.
364	- **Publish polish slice (S).** A copyable 00:00 chapter list from chapter markers, checked against YouTube's rule [D21]; approximate platform safe-zone overlays [D24]; named platform export targets. Skip AI titles and thumbnails, which YouTube Studio is adding itself [C29].
365	- **Measure multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback (S).** Bet 5 and any claim to lead depend on it. It is a measurement, not performance work.
366	- **`search_media` over cached transcripts (S).** The useful slice of a footage index. Build the Vision and Sound Analysis analysis inside bets 3, 4 and 6.
367	- **Merge the in-app tutorials after TU4 (S).** Creators arriving from CapCut need onboarding. The merge needs TutorialTargets rows for the audio road map.
368	- **Optical-flow slow motion, spike first (S, then M).** `VTFrameProcessor` accepts only 64RGBAHalf on this Mac, and its handling of HDR encodings is untested. Interpolated smooth cuts across a jump cut stay a spike, not a commitment.
369	- **WebVTT import (S); translated captions later (M).** A later phase of a caption road map, not a bet.

371	## Not worth chasing
372	
373	| Item | Reason |
374	|---|---|
375	| Generative media: AI B-roll and video, avatars, voice clones, lip-synced dubbing | Nothing on the device can do it, so it means brokering credit-metered vendor APIs, the model Frame Job competes against. It carries disclosure risk [D25]. YouTube [C26] and Instagram [C28] now dub and translate for free. |
376	| Direct upload, scheduling, hosted share links, platform analytics | An open-source app with no backend cannot keep OAuth client secrets. A shared quota would cap all users together, and posting APIs need audits. Share links need a server. Bring-your-own storage is the only later form that fits. |
377	| Stock libraries; a template marketplace | These need licensing, curation and a backend. One developer cannot match CapCut's volume [C1] or MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro [P15]. Agent-written graphics and `.fjgraphic` packages are the counter. |
378	| Eye-contact correction, face retouching | Apple has no public API for these on recorded video. They would need cloud or custom generative face models, with likeness risk and a per-frame cost the one-pass compositor cannot absorb. |
379	| Cloud sync, collaboration, mobile or iPad apps, Windows | Each needs a backend or a second platform. |
380	| Remote guest recording, live multi-camera capture | This is Riverside's moat [C9] and needs WebRTC servers. Import the per-guest files instead, and switch between them with bet 5. |
381	| A virality score | Creators distrust scored clips [D16]. A stated reason per moment is honest and controllable. |
382	| A standalone on-device footage index | The major editors shipped footage search within a year [P1] [P13] [P9]. Vision gives only fixed labels, so free-text search needs a bundled model whose licence is unverified. Build slices inside bets 3, 4 and 6, plus `search_media`. |
383	| Script to cut: a listening teleprompter that assembles takes | Teleprompters are common [S19] [S16]. Script-first recording suits a minority. `SpeechEngine.swift` is file-based today. The valuable kernel, retake removal, belongs in bet 1. |
384	| Translated captions and soft subtitle tracks as a bet | Platforms translate themselves [C26] [C28]. ADA Title II needs same-language captions, which Frame Job already makes. Platforms take the sidecar SRT and VTT files Frame Job already writes. |
385	| A publish kit as a headline | YouTube Studio is adding AI titles and title and thumbnail tests [C29]. The on-device model's context cannot hold a long transcript, and Frame Job already meets the loudness targets. Only the S slice is worth doing. |
386	| More MCP surface or a second agent mode as the headline | MCP became expected in 2026 [C6] [C13] [C21] [P10]. Every creator job shipped as ops becomes an agent tool anyway. |
387	| Stabilisation, for now | Phones stabilise in camera, and stabilisation mainly serves handheld vlogs. It is feasible later as a cached render. |
388	| Live-compositor motion blur | It needs several sub-frame passes, which breaks the one-pass compositor. |
389	| A plugin system | It contradicts the closed effect vocabulary (spec §11 R5-1, G-1) that preview and export parity and the proof suite rest on. |
390	| Pro finishing as headline features (Dolby Vision, synthetic depth of field) | Resolve and Final Cut Pro own these [P9]. Frame Job's colour and HDR already lead every creator tool. |
391	| Analytics-driven idea features | The platforms hold the data [C23] [C29]. |

393	## Decisions for the owner
394	
395	1. **Lead segment.** Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
396	2. **Which spec §1 non-goals to lift, and how far.**
397	   - Auto-reframe: needed for bet 3.
398	   - Multicam: narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5).
399	   - ML and heavy pixel work: needed for camera cutout (issue #124's D5, bet 6).
400	   - Optical-flow retiming and motion blur: stay out until a spike.
401	   - A plugin system: stays out.
402	3. **Which spec §11 decisions to amend before code.**
403	   - TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1).
404	   - `recording.md`: cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and a schema bump (bet 2).
405	   - AI-10, for Proposals.
406	   - W-10, for inspector caption styling.
407	4. **Shortcut capture.** Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, with capture opt-in and limited to modifier shortcuts by default.
408	5. **Vertical versions.** A regenerated copy (M), or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
409	6. **Language models.** Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
410	7. **Cloud.** Confirm that bring-your-own key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
411	8. **Performance.** Allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
412	9. **Real use.** Cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
413	10. **Positioning.** Whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises [C5] [S7] [D19], metered credits [D7] [P7] and content-licence scares [D18].

1	# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)
2	
3	**Opened 2026-10-30** (AP0), when the owner answered the five choices below ("Yes, lift scopes,
4	and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the rest): AU-2…AU-4, and spec
5	§1's audio non-goal lifted. The brief
6	is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
7	`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
8	AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).
9	
10	## Goal
11	
12	Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
13	a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
14	turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
15	can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
16	then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
17	hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
18	buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
19	MCP mirror, as every control does today.
20	
21	## What it delivers first
22	
23	The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
24	loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
25	(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
26	Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
27	Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
28	−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
29	limiter and the target.
30	
31	## The owner's choices (answered 2026-10-30: all five as recommended)
32	
33	Recorded as AU-2 (choice 1), AU-3 (choices 4 and 5) and AU-4 (choices 2 and 3). The owner,
34	on the rest: "We'll address other questions as we progress. If builds can be run in multiple
35	lanes, do so."
36	
37	1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
38	   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
39	   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
40	2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
41	   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
42	3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
43	   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
44	   *Recommended.*
45	4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
46	   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,
47	   deterministic, testable against analytic responses. Apple's units only where Frame Job cannot
48	   write its own: ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`) and E8's voice effects, both rendered
49	   offline as speed-ramp audio is. AP0's spike S1 confirms or overturns this. *Recommended.*
50	5. **One fixed chain order, not a user-ordered list.** Channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch
51	   → isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, each stage off by
52	   default and inert when off. A closed vocabulary like every other effect (§11 R5-1), and the
53	   order an engineer would choose for voice. *Recommended.*
54	
55	Asked later, at the phase that needs them (each has a recommendation there): how the volume
56	line is edited (AP8), the split-edit model (AP9), track processing in the preview and the stem
57	format (AP10), and where speech spans live for ducking (AP11).
58	
59	## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)
60	
61	- **Working arrangement:** this worktree is the integration branch; each phase is built
62	  through litecode in a lane of its own, gated, committed, rebased onto the integration branch
63	  one at a time and gated again there, as codec-export (CX-11) and grading (GR-25) merged
64	  phase by phase. Merging into main is done from the main checkout.
65	- **Lanes (the owner's "multiple lanes"):** after AP0, at most three at once, split by the
66	  files they touch. **Lane A, the voice block:** AP1 → AP2 → AP3 → AP4 → AP5 → AP6, then AP8
67	  and AP14, which build on its stages. **Lane B, editing and playback:** AP9 → AP13 → AP7
68	  (the meter after AP1 has landed, since both read `Loudness.swift`). **Lane C, the mix:**
69	  AP11 → AP10 (after AP2 has landed: both work in the export's float gain stage) → AP12
70	  (after AP3). A lane whose next phase waits on another lane's phase waits; it never builds
71	  against an unlanded one.
72	- **Collisions between lanes:** each phase numbers its decisions in its own block (APn's
73	  AU-n0…, AU-2's note), and a format bump is provisional until its phase lands: the
74	  integrator renumbers it (and its `schema_vN.rs`) when another lane landed one first.
75	- **Agent parity:** every new property is a `set_audio` key, every new command a tool, every
76	  new answer readable through `get_project`.
77	- **Proof currency:** exports decoded to PCM and measured by the proof's own arithmetic
78	  (`phase5_proof.py`'s BS.1770 and 4× true-peak oversampler), synthetic fixtures with known
79	  answers, and the owner's samples where present. What only ears can judge is a row in
80	  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
81	- **Samples:** the owner records the survey's §6 list. A phase uses a sample when it exists and
82	  a synthetic fixture otherwise; no phase waits for one.
83	- **Persisted fields** carry serde defaults and bump the format (`core/CLAUDE.md`); an older
84	  project opens unchanged and sounds the same.
85	
86	## How it fits the tree (at `33eeed0`)
87	
88	- **The clip strip runs in a tap, before the fader.** `AudioTap.swift` (595) puts one
89	  `MTAudioProcessingTap` (PreEffects) on each composition audio track and schedules each clip's
90	  settings by span (`AudioDSPSpan`). `AudioDSP.swift` (**890, over the cap**) holds pan, the mono
91	  fold, the compressor (default threshold −18 dB) and noise reduction, real-time safe. Volume,
92	  fades and ducking come after the tap, as the core's envelope played as volume ramps
93	  (`core/src/audio.rs` 537, `audio_duck.rs` 136). **A new live stage sees the clip at its
94	  recorded level**, so a level-relative stage (limiter, gate) must be told the clip's gain.
95	- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** One tap per input, already used by
96	  the meter (`LevelMeter.swift` 400, which sums per-track peaks as an upper bound, not the mix).
97	  The export measures a 32-bit float mix and gains it in `ExporterAudioGain.swift` (179); its
98	  write pass still decodes 16-bit integers (#86).
99	- **Offline renders have a pattern.** Speed-ramp audio renders into `cache/ramp-audio/` through
100	  `RampAudioRenders` (a serial queue, owners, a wait in the export, dry while pending).
101	- **Loudness exists once.** `Loudness.swift` (**674, over the cap**) is BS.1770-4 for the
102	  export; `ExporterLoudness.swift` (211) its measurement pass.
103	- **The model.** `AudioProps` lives in `core/src/model_props.rs` (551), checked by
104	  `props_check.rs` (526) and clamped by `actions_clamp.rs` (386); pan, mono, compressor, noise
105	  reduction, duck and keep pitch are BASE-only (`InspectorBinding+Writes.swift`'s
106	  `structural(audio:)`), and only volume, mute and the fades animate.
107	- **Caches.** Peaks, sync features and speech (Silero VAD) per media, on the cache lane
108	  (`MediaCacheLane.swift`); a loudness cache would be a fifth beside them.
109	
110	## Phases
111	
112	| Phase | Survey items | What a person gets |
113	|---|---|---|
114	| AP0 | — | Scope lifted, the spike's answers, the files split |
115	| AP1 | A2, A8 (readout) | A clip's LUFS shown; Normalize to a loudness |
116	| AP2 | A1, A13 | A true-peak limiter; the export reaches its loudness; 24-bit |
117	| AP3 | A3, A7, B7 | EQ and high-pass, hum removal, channel selection |
118	| AP4 | A5, A6 | Gate/expander, de-esser |
119	| AP5 | A4, B4 | Voice isolation; de-reverb if isolation does it |
120	| AP6 | B1, B3, B8 | Enhance Voice; the leveller; clean-up when a voice-over lands |
121	| AP7 | A8 | Live LUFS and true-peak meter |
122	| AP8 | A9 | Every audio parameter animates; the volume line on the clip |
123	| AP9 | A10 | J- and L-cuts that keep sync; reversible Detach |
124	| AP10 | A12, A11 | Track faders, track and master processing, stems |
125	| AP11 | B2, B9 | Ducking by speech; fade and crossfade shapes |
126	| AP12 | B6 | Match one clip's level and tone to another |
127	| AP13 | B5 | Audio while scrubbing |
128	| AP14 | B10 | Voice effects (E8, #123) |
129	
130	AP1–AP6 are the voice block, in the order the owner's recording needs them. AP7 onward is the
131	mixing block and can be reordered freely; only AP12 needs AP3, and AP6 needs AP2–AP5.
132	
133	### AP0 — scope, the record, the tolls and the spike
134	
135	- **Decisions:** AU-2 (the scope, from choice 1), AU-3 (the chain, choices 4 and 5), AU-4 (the
136	  loudness defaults, choices 2 and 3). Spec §1's non-goal sentence rewritten; this road map
137	  opened.
138	- **Tolls, each a pure move landed and gated alone:** `AudioDSP.swift` cut at its MARKs (the
139	  compressor and noise reduction into their own files, the chain kept); `AudioTap.swift`'s
140	  schedule and parameters (its first two MARKs) out of the tap; `Loudness.swift` cut below the
141	  cap; `AudioProps` and its vocabulary out of `model_props.rs` into a new `model_audio.rs`.
142	- **Spike S, its rule fixed before its run, its record here:**
143	  - **S1 — own DSP or Apple units, live.** A biquad EQ and Frame Job's limiter against
144	    `AVAudioUnitEQ`, `AUNBandEQ` and `AUPeakLimiter` driven inside the tap: byte-identical
145	    exports run twice, preview against export, CPU per track at eight stages, latency.
146	  - **S2 — voice isolation.** `AUSoundIsolation` rendered offline over the owner's recording:
147	    speed against real time, latency, determinism across runs, the pause floor and the speech
148	    band against the shipped noise reducer, and whether it reduces reverberation (B4's
149	    question), on a reverberant sample if one exists.
150	  - **S3 — tracks and the master in the preview.** Whether one composition audio track ever
151	    carries two timeline tracks; the error of a track chain run per composition track during an
152	    overlap (zero for linear stages, measured for dynamics); the options for a preview master
153	    limiter (none and say so, per-track, or an offline premix); rebuilding the true mix from the
154	    taps for a LUFS meter.
155	  - **S4 — a loudness cache.** K-weighted 100 ms block energies per media: size, build time on
156	    a 20-minute file, and integrated LUFS over any window against `Loudness.swift` measuring an
157	    export of the same window (agreement within 0.1 LU).
158	- **Acceptance:** `make gate` after each toll; the spike's verdicts recorded here.
159	
160	### AP1 — loudness you can see and target (A2, A8's readout)
161	
162	- A per-media loudness cache (`cache/loudness/<id>.bin`, S4's format) on the cache lane after
163	  peaks, current by `CacheStamp` like the others.
164	- The Volume section reads the clip's integrated loudness (gated, over the window that plays)
165	  and its true peak beside the Gain row.
166	- Normalize gains a **Loudness** mode: a target in LUFS, each clip of a selection to the same
167	  target, which is what "match these clips" means. Until AP2, a clip whose peak would pass the
168	  ceiling stops short and says where it landed, as the volume ceiling does today.
169	  `normalize_clip` gains `mode` and `target_lufs`.
170	- **Proof:** exports of normalised fixtures measured by the proof's BS.1770 within ±0.5 LU;
171	  the owner's recording; a selection of two levels landing equal.
172	
173	### AP2 — limiters, and an export that reaches its loudness (A1, A13)
174	
175	- A **clip limiter** stage in the tap: lookahead, 4× oversampled true-peak detection, a ceiling
176	  in dBTP. Because the fader is downstream, the stage is told the clip's gain (decision AU-n:
177	  the base volume, with fades and ducks only ever lowering it), and its lookahead is a lead
178	  like noise reduction's (SY-25).
179	- The **export:** a float decode before the gain (#86, closing it), a master limiter in the
180	  float write pass so the loudness target limits instead of capping, and an `audio_bits` choice
181	  of 16 or 24 on WAV and AIFF.
182	- Loudness Normalize uses the clip limiter, so the owner's recording reaches −16 LUFS at
183	  −1 dBTP. If choice 2 says so, Loudness becomes the button's default here.
184	- **Proof:** every export's true peak at or under its ceiling by the proof's oversampler; the
185	  loudness target met within ±0.5 LU on `phase5_proof.py`'s crest fixture, which today lands
186	  quieter; a 24-bit file decoded with its low bits used; the owner's recording.
187	- **Manual check:** no pumping or distortion on speech and on music.
188	- **Built in two parts, by size.** Part 1: the clip limiter, `audio.limiter` (format 30), its
189	  Limiter section and `set_audio` key, and Loudness Normalize through it as the default
190	  (AU-20…AU-26; its record below). Part 2: the export's float decode (#86), the master limiter
191	  in the float write pass and `audio_bits` (AU-27 on).
192	
193	### AP3 — EQ, hum removal and channel selection (A3, A7, B7)
194	
195	- **EQ:** a high-pass with a slope, a low-pass, low and high shelves and a number of parametric
196	  bands (set at AP3), with voice presets (rumble cut, de-mud, presence). An EQ section in the
197	  Sound sub-tab with the response curve drawn.
198	- **Hum:** notches at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, depth and harmonic count.
199	- **Channels:** both, left only, right only, swapped, before the mono fold, so a mic recorded
200	  on one channel of a stereo file plays at its level.
201	- **Model:** `audio.eq`, `audio.hum`, `audio.channels`; format bump; MCP keys.
202	- **Proof:** tones and sweeps through each band against the biquad's analytic response
203	  (±0.1 dB); notch depth at each harmonic; a channel pick sample-identical to its source channel.
204	
205	### AP4 — gate, expander and de-esser (A5, A6)
206	
207	- A downward **expander/gate** sharing the compressor's envelope follower: threshold relative
208	  to the clip's measured level (AP1), ratio, range, attack, hold, release.
209	- A **de-esser:** a compressor keyed on a high band (frequency, threshold, range).
210	- **Model, inspector, MCP** as AP3; format bump.
211	- **Proof:** a tone burst over noise, the pause floor lowered by the range and the burst
212	  untouched; sibilant noise bursts reduced in band and the voice band untouched; the owner's
213	  recording's pause floor.
214	
215	### AP5 — voice isolation (A4; B4's verdict)
216	
217	- **Isolation** by `AUSoundIsolation` (S2), rendered offline per clip window into
218	  `cache/isolated/` on the ramp-audio pattern: an Amount (wet/dry), dry while pending, the
219	  export waiting for its render, re-rendered when the window or the file changes.
220	- **De-reverb (B4):** if S2 measured reverberation removed, it is this control and the guide
221	  says so; otherwise B4 is filed with tier C and the measurement.
222	- **Proof:** the render aligned with the dry clip within a sample (cross-correlation); the pause
223	  floor and the speech band against the dry clip; dry while pending; an export that waits.
224	- **Manual check:** artefacts on the owner's voice at Amount 100 % and 50 %.
225	
226	### AP6 — Enhance Voice, the leveller, and clean-up when a voice-over lands (B1, B3, B8)
227	
228	- **Enhance Voice** (Clip menu, a button in the Sound sub-tab, an `enhance_voice` tool): reads
229	  the clip's loudness, its peak and the noise floor over the VAD cache's non-speech spans, then
230	  writes ORDINARY settings a person can see and change — high-pass, isolation or noise
231	  reduction, gate, de-esser if the high band is hot, a compressor set from the clip's own
232	  level, the limiter and the loudness target. One undo step; pressing it twice changes nothing.
233	- **Leveller (B3):** a slow gain-rider stage for a speaker who moves on and off the mic, off by
234	  default, turned on by Enhance Voice when the speech's short-term loudness range calls for it.
235	- **At record time (B8):** a recorder setting, "Enhance the microphone when it lands", applying
236	  Enhance Voice to the Microphone clip after the landing, as its own undo step (AU-68).
237	- **Proof:** the owner's recording to −16 LUFS ±0.5 at −1 dBTP with its pause floor lowered;
238	  idempotence; one undo step; a voice-over that lands enhanced.
239	- **Built in three parts, by size, as AP2 was.** Part 1: Enhance Voice itself — the measurements,
240	  the rules, the loudness cache's high band (version 2), the volume solved on the clip rendered
241	  through its own chain for Enhance and Loudness Normalize alike (the owner's answer,
242	  2026-10-31), the Measuring Sound sheet, the button, Clip ▸ Enhance Voice and `enhance_voice`
243	  (AU-60…AU-65; its record below). Part 2: the leveller, `audio.leveller` (a format bump) — after the
244	  owner's answer of 2026-10-31 a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's loudness and
245	  speech and applied with no state in the tap — its section, and Enhance turning it on from the
246	  speech's short-term loudness range (AU-66, AU-67; its record below). Part 3:
247	  "Enhance the microphone when it lands", the recorder setting and its `UserDefaults` key,
248	  applied after the landing as its own undo step (AU-68, AU-69; its record below).
249	
250	### AP7 — live loudness and true-peak metering (A8)
251	
252	- Momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS and true peak while playing, over the true mix
253	  (S3's method), with a reset; the per-clip readout is AP1's.
254	- **Proof:** a probe compiled from `app/Sources` fed EBU Tech 3341's test signals, each within

275	- J- and L-cuts that keep sync, and Detach Audio made reversible (Attach Audio).
276	- **Asked at AP9:** a LINKED pair — Detach's two clips carrying one link id, moved, cut and
277	  deleted together, with ⌥-drag trimming one half alone (recommended: it fits one kind of

313	- Short grains of the mix at the scrub position while the playhead is dragged, off when the

1	# Creator survey: what would make Frame Job a leading creator editor
2	
3	## Summary
4	
5	This survey is dated 1 November 2026. It asks what would make Frame Job a leading editor for content creators. It draws on five inputs:
6	
7	- an inventory of the tree;
8	- four research sweeps (creator tools, pro editors, screen and tutorial tools, creator demand);
9	- three strategists' proposals;
10	- the candidates merged from those proposals;
11	- adversarial checks of each candidate against the code, Apple's frameworks and the market.
12	
13	Frame Job is already ahead of most creator tools on finishing: its audio chain, colour and HDR, codecs, and an MCP surface that covers the whole editor. It loses creators earlier, at the jobs that now define a creator editor:
14	
15	- cutting a talk by its transcript;
16	- polishing a screen recording from the cursor;
17	- turning a horizontal edit into vertical shorts;
18	- finding the clips worth posting;
19	- switching podcast angles by speaker;
20	- cutting the presenter out of the background.
21	
22	Agent access no longer sets a tool apart, because most AI-forward editors gained an MCP server in 2026. No rival combines what Frame Job has: a full editor whose every edit is a pure, undoable op, analysis that runs on the creator's Mac, and AI on the creator's own key with no credits.
23	
24	The recommendation is to ship those creator jobs as on-device commands whose results land as ordinary edits on the timeline, in the order below. The rest is either table stakes to pick up later or not worth chasing.
25	
26	## What Frame Job has
27	
28	Frame Job is a native macOS editor for Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later. It is a Swift/AppKit app over a Rust core, Apache-2.0, with no account and no backend. As of 1 November 2026 it has the following.
29	
30	- **Editing.** One kind of track. Move, trim, slip, roll, rate-stretch, split, lift, ripple delete, insert and overwrite. Nests. Picture and sound linked for J- and L-cuts. Markers with a chapter flag. A second preview window. Every edit is one undo step through one mutation point, and a refused edit says why in the rule's own sentence.
31	- **Picture.** Transform, crop, blend modes, chroma key, spotlight, obscure regions, text with reveals, shapes with gradients, blurred backgrounds, and matte tracks that let any clip cut the track behind it. Actions animate almost every property, including speed, which is how speed ramps work. 13 transitions, and Zoom to Region for screencasts.
32	- **Audio.**
33	  - A per-clip chain: voice isolation, EQ, hum and noise reduction, gate, a phrase-level leveller, de-esser, compressor and true-peak limiter.
34	  - Enhance Voice, Match Audio, Normalize to LUFS, Duck by Speech, and Synchronize Audio with drift correction.
35	  - Track compressor and limiter, a live loudness meter, stems, and a −1 dBTP master on every export.
36	- **Clean-up.** Remove Silences (on-device Silero VAD), Remove Filler Words (AssemblyAI word timings; cloud-only), and `get_transcript`. The Assistant cuts false starts when asked.
37	- **Captions.** On-device or AssemblyAI transcription. Subtitles plus five word-by-word styles and three looks. SRT and WebVTT export; SRT import.
38	- **Colour and HDR.**
39	  - Grading: wheels, curves, hue curves, looks, .cube LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, and four scopes.
40	  - Log footage: Apple Log (detected on import), S-Log3, V-Log and Canon log.
41	  - HDR: HLG projects with HLG, HDR10 and SDR deliverables, on a 16-bit float compositor.
42	- **Graphics.** Sandboxed JavaScript modules that return SVG per frame, 23 bundled templates, shareable `.fjgraphic` packages, and agents that write new graphics.
43	- **Recording.** A display or a window through ScreenCaptureKit, with system audio, a separate microphone file, click rings, pause and resume, a camera beside the screen (bottom-right), and voice-over.
44	- **Export.** H.264, HEVC (10-bit and with alpha), AV1 and VP9 through bundled encoders, ProRes, audio formats and stems, GIF, APNG and stills. An Export Queue, embedded chapters, and loudness targets of −14 and −16 LUFS.
45	- **Agents.** 106 product tools over a local socket (one per edit, plus app-state tools), the bundled `framejob-mcp` helper, and `render_frame` so an agent can look at its work. An in-app Assistant runs on the creator's own Anthropic key and shows its spend.

149	- **Editing is the biggest time sink.** One vendor classified 27,555 comments on 44 creator-education channels. Editing and production was the largest category, at 21.4% of actionable comments, ahead of monetisation at 15.6% [D1]. This is one vendor's analysis, not a survey.

173	## The bets
174	
175	The bets are ranked by how many creators each reaches, how often they would use it, and how far it puts Frame Job ahead rather than level, discounted by effort and risk.
176	
177	Every bet has the same shape. Analysis that Frame Job already caches, or that macOS provides on the device, feeds a planner. The planner writes edits the core already knows how to make. Each result is therefore an ordinary undo step on a real timeline, and each command becomes an MCP tool that the Assistant and outside agents can run with no new agent work.
178	
179	Effort is build effort (S, M, L, XL), never lines of code.
180	
181	| Rank | Bet | Effort | Serves |
182	|---|---|---|---|
183	| 1 | Transcript tab | L | Everyone who records themselves talking |
184	| 2 | Screen recordings with the cursor as data | L | Screencasts, tutorials, courses, product demos |
185	| 3 | Make Vertical Version | M (copy), L (linked versions) | Everyone who posts shorts |
186	| 4 | Find Clips | M on top of 3 | Podcasters, long-form YouTubers, streamers |
187	| 5 | Switch by Speaker, and every audio track | M | Video podcasts and interviews |
188	| 6 | Camera cutout and layouts | L | Screencasters, talking heads, streamers |

190	Bets 1 and 2 remove the two points where talking creators and the home segment give up. Bets 3 and 4 complete the long-to-short loop. Bet 5 takes the podcast format on the strength of the audio chain. Bet 6 closes the presenter-camera gap.

192	### 1. Transcript tab: cut by deleting words, with retakes found for review
193	
194	**Pitch.** A Transcript tab shows the timeline's words in timeline order. The word being spoken is highlighted during playback, and clicking a word moves the playhead to it. The creator selects a sentence and presses Delete, and that span ripples out of the video as one undo step. Cut words stay greyed in place and can be restored.
195	
196	A review pass strikes through long pauses and, where an AssemblyAI transcript exists, filler words. After the §11 decision below, it also strikes earlier takes of each repeated line and false starts. One click removes everything struck, as one undo step. Words inside a nest or a transition overlap show as not editable, with the reason.
197	
198	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** On its own this brings Frame Job level. Editing by transcript ships in:
199	
200	- Descript [C7], Screen Studio 4 [S4] and Tella [S11];
201	- Loom, on its Business + AI plan [S15];
202	- Prequel [S20] and Gling [C31].
203	
204	Adobe lists Paper Edit in Premiere 26.5 [P4], though one verifier disputed it. Cap's changelog lists a word-level editor [S16] that a verifier could not confirm shipped.
205	
206	Frame Job pulls ahead on terms and on depth:
207	
208	- **Cost.** The on-device transcript costs nothing per minute. Descript meters media minutes and AI credits [D7] and draws complaints about speed [D8].
209	- **No model needed for retakes.** They are found by a deterministic comparison of neighbouring sentences, with no key.
210	- **Depth.** Every cut is an ordinary ripple edit in a full editor, with the audio chain, grading and graphics behind it, so restoring a cut is exact.
211	- **Agents for free.** The same word-to-timeline mapping already serves agents: `get_transcript` answers in timeline ticks, and `ripple_delete_ranges` is one undo step. "Drop the first take of every repeated line" therefore works the same by click or by chat.
212	
213	Editing is the largest topic in one vendor's analysis of creator comments [D1].
214	
215	**Builds on.** `DeviceTranscriptCache.swift` and `MediaTranscript.swift` (words cached per media in source ticks); AssemblyAI transcripts; `get_transcript` (`AgentServer+Transcript.swift`); `rc_project_source_map` (`speed_map.rs`, spec §11 SR-20) through speed, ramps and reverse; `ripple_delete_ranges` (`core/src/edit_time.rs`); `detect_fillers` and its lock, nest and transition rules.
216	
217	**Effort.** L, as a short road map: the view with seek; delete as ranges; greyed, restorable words; the retake pass after its decision.
218	
219	**Risks and what comes first.**
220	- Spec §11 TR-3 says a false start is never offered without a conversation. AI-6 and W-9 say no pipeline picks words to cut by meaning. A deterministic retake pass is such a pipeline, so it needs an amending §11 decision before code. Pauses and fillers already sit within TR-3 and TR-4.
221	- Restore is not one existing op. It is `insert_time` plus `trim_end` into the left clip's handle, grouped, or `add_clip` with a source range (next tier).
222	- On-device transcription kept 1 of 8 fillers in the owner's test (TR-7), so filler strike-through needs an AssemblyAI key.
223	- `MAX_CLIPS` (4,096) counts every clip, nested ones included, and each text cut splits every unlocked track. About 1,000 cuts over four tracks reaches the cap.
224	- The first fill of a whole-timeline view runs the recogniser at a few seconds per minute of speech. After that it is cached.
225	- A multi-hour transcript in one text view, kept in step with edits made elsewhere, needs care. The new pane needs a planned file split under the 600-line cap.
226	
227	The companion item Punch in on cuts (next tier, S) hides the jump cuts this bet leaves.
228	
229	### 2. Screen recordings with the cursor as data
230	
231	**Pitch.** The recorder stops burning the pointer and click rings into the picture. Beside the movie it saves the cursor's path and image and every click. If the creator opts in, it also saves the shortcuts pressed. When the recording lands:
232	
233	- zoom actions already sit on the action lane at each click and each burst of typing;
234	- the cursor is its own layer, which can be made bigger, restyled, smoothed or hidden when idle, and gets click ripples;
235	- each shortcut appears as a Keyboard keys overlay;
236	- long typing stretches can be sped up.
237	
238	All of it is ordinary actions, clips and graphics that the creator can drag or delete. Recordings made before this ships, and imported screen videos, behave as today.
239	
240	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** The polished-screencast category rests on cursor data:
241	
242	- Screen Studio zooms where clicks happened [S2] and edits the cursor after recording [S3];
243	- Prequel stores the pointer as data [S19];
244	- Cap [S16], FocuSee [S18], Tella [S11] and Camtasia [S8] [S9] do the same.
245	
246	Frame Job's recorder stores none of it, so Frame Job loses its own home segment to a recorder that costs about $29 a month [S7]. This bet brings Frame Job level on polish. It pulls ahead because those recorders are shallow editors and Frame Job is a full one. Its auto zooms are actions on a real timeline, next to grading, the audio chain, captions and graphics, and an agent can re-plan them ("zoom only on the clicks in the settings pane").
247	
248	Being free is not unique by itself. OpenScreen is a free, MIT-licensed Screen Studio alternative with about 40,000 stars, archived after v1.5.0 [S23], and Cap sells a $58 lifetime licence [S17].
249	
250	**Builds on.** `RecordingSetup.swift`, which sets `showsCursor` and `showMouseClicks` today; `add_zoom_action` (`core/src/edit_zoom.rs`); `add_speed_ramp`; the Keyboard keys graphic template; the recorder panel's grants; `recipe_layer.rs`; `MediaConsolidator` and relink.
251	
252	**Effort.** L.
253	
254	**Risks and what comes first.**
255	- Spec §11 (`recording.md`) decides three things this bet reverses: the cursor and click ring are taken as drawn and nothing is reconstructed; callouts stay out; a recording is ordinary media, with no source kind and no schema bump. The owner amends §11 first, as CAM-1 did for the camera.
256	- Shortcuts need the Input Monitoring grant, which `RecorderStatusItem.swift` deliberately avoids today. Key capture should be opt-in and record only modifier shortcuts by default. It must never record secure fields, and it must show plainly when it is on.
257	- The cursor must follow the screen clip's own transform and zoom actions. It has to be drawn as part of that clip's layer, or the two have to be nested with the zooms on the nest. A sprite on another track would drift.
258	- `NSCursor.currentSystem` is marked deprecated in macOS 27.0 in Apple's availability metadata, so a replacement is needed.
259	- The sidecar cannot be regenerated, so Consolidate and Relink must carry it.
260	- Timing can anchor on the screen's first-frame time, which the camera spike measured within 0.5 ms. Issue #370 is a microphone-offset problem and is not inherited.
261	- Motion blur on zooms needs sub-frame sampling and is out of scope.
262	- Code from AGPL-licensed recorders is not carried over, the same rule as for Concat.
263	
264	### 3. Make Vertical Version
265	
266	**Pitch.** File ▸ Make Vertical Version… writes a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac. It does this with ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. In a screen recording made after bet 2, it follows the cursor instead. Captions re-lay for the short side, and graphics re-layout from the canvas size. A shot that cannot be cropped gets Add Blurred Background.
267	
268	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes. OpusClip [C11], CapCut [C4], Premiere [P21], Final Cut Pro for iPad [P17], Riverside [C9], Kapwing [C20] and Screen Studio [S1] all ship it, and auto-repurposing is the most-wanted creator AI feature in one survey [D2]. Frame Job pulls ahead on terms. CapCut moved Auto Reframe behind Pro in April 2026 [C4]. Here it is free and local, and the result is editable pan actions rather than a render. If the owner chooses linked versions (one cut, with a framing per shape), Frame Job is ahead of every rival, because their vertical copies drift from the master.
269	
270	**Builds on.** `fill_scale` (`edit_fit.rs`); Add Blurred Background (`edit_background.rs`); word captions sized to the shorter side (`CaptionStyle.swift`); graphics that read `ctx.canvas`; actions (`edit_action.rs`); nests (`edit_nest.rs`); `set_canvas` (`edit_canvas.rs`); File ▸ Duplicate; the E9 Vision spike in `tools/proof/effects_spike/`.
271	
272	**Effort.** M as a regenerated copy. L for linked versions, which need a canvas per version, framing overrides per clip and a format bump.
273	
274	**Risks and what comes first.**
275	- Spec §1 lists auto-reframe as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it first. The reason given there, heavy pixel work outside the one-pass compositor, no longer applies: the analysis runs offline and its output is actions.
276	- No two actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. A clip that already carries an action (a zoom, a grade, a ramp) needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas freezes at the size it was nested at.
277	- `set_canvas` does not rescale action end states. A screencast's existing zoom actions keep their 16:9 targets, and the planner must rewrite them.
278	- `MediaCacheLane` is a width-2 lane for audio decodes, so video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows.
279	- The planner should use face, human and saliency rectangles with tracking, not masks: the E9 spike found that foreground masks flicker on video.
280	- Two people in frame, a speaker leaving the frame, and shot changes inside one flattened clip each need a rule.
281	
282	### 4. Find Clips
283	
284	**Pitch.** Clip ▸ Find Clips…, run on an episode, a VOD or a finished edit, lists 10 to 30 candidates of 20 to 60 seconds. Each candidate shows:
285	
286	- in and out points snapped to sentence ends;
287	- its length;
288	- a one-line reason, such as "laughter after the punchline";
289	- a preview.
290	
291	There is no virality score. Make Short turns the checked candidates into vertical projects through bet 3. Each short is word-captioned, has fillers removed where a cloud transcript exists, and is queued for export.
292	
293	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Long-to-short is what OpusClip [C10] [C12], Riverside [C9], Submagic [C14] and Kapwing [C20] sell, all metered by credits. YouTube's own free tool covers only 10 countries and 7 languages [D9]. Frame Job pulls ahead in three ways:
294	
295	- **Local signals.** Laughter, applause and cheering from Sound Analysis, the 10 ms loudness, speech spans and sentence ends are all measured on the Mac.
296	- **The creator's own key.** Ranking runs on the creator's Claude key, with no per-minute credits.
297	- **Real timelines.** Each candidate opens as an editable timeline.
298	
299	A stated reason for each moment, rather than a score, answers the documented complaint that clippers cut in the wrong place [D16].
300	
301	**Builds on.** `get_transcript` (timeline ticks); `ClipLoudness.swift` and the per-media loudness cache; `media_speech.rs`; `detect_fillers` and `ripple_delete_ranges`; caption Restyle with Replace; the Export Queue; the Assistant helper (`agent/`) and its price table; `set_range`.
302	
303	**Effort.** M on top of bet 3. Without bet 3 it produces horizontal clips only.
304	
305	**Risks and what comes first.**
306	- Ranking quality is the whole product.
307	- On-device FoundationModels has a 4,096-token context and needs Apple Intelligence turned on. It is a chunked, weaker fallback, not an equal path.
308	- Speaker labels exist only on AssemblyAI transcripts requested with speakers.
309	- No op copies a timeline range into a new project: `new_project` takes a path, and Duplicate copies everything. One is needed.
310	- Sound Analysis (`SNClassifySoundRequest` `.version1`, 303 labels on macOS 26.5.1, laughter, applause and cheering among them) is noisy on game audio and music beds.
311	- Long transcripts cost tokens, so show an estimate range before running.
312	
313	### 5. Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file
314	
315	**Pitch.** The creator brings two to four cameras and a mic per person, lines them up with Synchronize Audio, and chooses Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking, judging each mic's speech spans against that mic's own noise floor. It uses the wide shot during crosstalk and holds a minimum shot length. The whole switch is one undo step, and every cut is an ordinary split the creator can roll or re-pick. OBS multitrack files and multichannel recorder files import every audio track, not only the first.
316	
317	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Automatic switching is sold as AutoPod for about $29 a month [D14], as Resolve SmartSwitch in Studio [P8], and inside hand-off or metered tools such as Eddie [C32] and Descript. Premiere users have asked for it for years [D13], and video podcasts are the fastest-growing creator format [D10] [D11] [D12]. Frame Job already owns the hard audio half: drift-corrected sync, cached speech spans, the loudness cache, Match Audio, Enhance Voice, the leveller, a −16 LUFS target and stems. Adding the picture half makes it a free podcast editor. An agent can also re-run the switch with new rules, such as "cut to wide whenever both laugh".
318	
319	**Builds on.** `AudioSync*.swift` (alignment as `move_clip` and `set_speed`); `SileroVAD.swift` and `media_speech.rs`; `audio_duck_speech.rs`; `ClipLoudness.swift`; `set_enabled` (a clip with its picture disabled is not decoded, per `nest.rs` `shows_video`); `ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`; `core/src/container.rs` and every `CompositionBuilder.firstTrack` audio caller.
320	
321	**Effort.** M for speaker switching on stacked tracks plus every audio track. L for a multicam clip with an angle grid and live overrides.
322	
323	**Risks and what comes first.**
324	- Spec §1 lists multicam as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it, either narrowly (stacked tracks) or fully.
325	- Reading every audio track touches every `firstTrack(.audio)` caller: the builder, Silence, the isolation, ramp, voice and reverse renderers, and the transcription extract. It needs a format bump.
326	- Splitting linked picture and sound halves of three angles every 8 s for two hours gives about 5,400 clips, which is over the 4,096 cap. The switch should cut picture only and keep the mics whole.
327	- Mic bleed can mislead the switch, and one-mic shows need Vision mouth activity instead.
328	- Transitions decode both angles. Decoding three or four 4K angles has not been measured (see the next tier).
329	- Zoom and Riverside already deliver one file per participant, so the multitrack fix chiefly serves OBS and multichannel WAV.
330	
331	### 6. Camera cutout and layouts
332	
333	**Pitch.** The creator ticks Remove Background on a camera clip. Vision segments the person on the Mac, rendered in the background the way Reverse is. A Layout pop-up switches the camera at the playhead, with an animated move, between:
334	
335	- corner bubble (circle or rounded);
336	- side by side;
337	- stacked for vertical;
338	- camera full;
339	- screen only.
340	
341	"Hide camera while silent" fades the camera out during pauses. Text Behind Subject follows from cutout: a title sits between the person and their background.
342	
343	**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** This is mostly catch-up. Screen Studio 4 (cutout in beta) [S6], Cap 0.6 [S16], Tella [S11], Prequel [S19] and Loom [S13] shipped camera cutout or layouts in September and October 2026. Final Cut Pro [P14], Premiere [P2] and Resolve [P8] ship one-click subject masks. Frame Job's recorded camera is fixed in the bottom-right corner. It pulls ahead only in combination: layouts are actions any agent can write, the camera gets Frame Job's grading and LUT engine, and with bet 2 the whole screencast polish lives inside a full editor.
344	
345	**Builds on.** Issue #124 and its E9 Vision spike; `ReverseRenderer`, `ReverseCache`, `BackgroundRender` and `MediaCacheLedger`; matte tracks (`recipe_matte.rs`); actions over transform, crop, corner radius and shadow; Add Background; the speech spans of the microphone media.
346	
347	**Effort.** L.
348	
349	**Risks and what comes first.**
350	- Edge quality on hair is a risk. Balanced person masks are 512×384 and likely need a refinement pass. Accurate masks run at 1.7× realtime and take 1.7 GiB per minute.
351	- Non-person masks flicker on video, so non-person cutout is for stills only.
352	- A mask on a Luma matte track has no link to the camera clip and drifts on trims, splits and speed changes. A per-layer mask with a format bump is the sound design.
353	- Issue #124's `texture(2)` binding is stale: looks now hold texture 2 and curves texture 3.
354	- The camera clip has no sound of its own, so hide-while-silent reads the microphone's spans through the microphone clip.
355	- Spec §1's ML non-goal, and issue #124's proposed decision D5, must enter §11 first.
356	- The 8-decoder budget is a warning, not a refusal. HLG projects need the mask in the right working space.
357	
358	### The next tier
359	
360	- **Proposals: play an agent's multi-step edit before it lands (M; Recipes later, also M).** Only Frame Job can do this cheaply. Handles are immutable. The export pin already renders a project that is not the current one. `performGroupedEdit` already makes one undo step from many. An agent's turn becomes a side chain the creator plays and compares A/B with the current cut, then accepts as one named step or rejects. This answers the 44% who want to review or undo and the 37% who want to see what the agent does [D4]. It amends spec §11 AI-10, which accepted ten Undos for a ten-call turn. It matters most once bets 1 and 4 produce agent-driven batches. Recipes come after Proposals and need three things: tool allow-lists enforced by the gate, because a shared recipe is a prompt-injection path; cost shown as an estimate range, because `pricing.ts` prices a run after it happens; and prompts served from `mcp-proxy`, because `core/src/agent.rs` is generic code.
361	- **Punch in on cuts (S).** Alternates scale between about 100% and 112% across cuts within one take, centred on the face, with `set_video` x, y and scale as one grouped step. It is free and exact, and needs no disclosure. Ship it right after bet 1's first phase.
362	- **Source ranges, skimming, In and Out, favourite ranges (M).** `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` gain a source range, and `opTool` prints it into the MCP tools automatically. This is the precondition for placing a found moment and for a clean restore in bet 1. Add proxies only after a measurement shows a shortfall, under a recorded decision on a playback-only builder input.
363	- **Caption styles, brand kit and project templates (M).** Colour controls are safe under spec §11 W-10. Size and font changes need re-paging or a W-10 amendment. Per-word emphasis and emoji need a `model_words.rs` field and a format bump under W-2 and W-3. Whether emoji render correctly in HLG projects is unverified.
364	- **Publish polish slice (S).** A copyable 00:00 chapter list from chapter markers, checked against YouTube's rule [D21]; approximate platform safe-zone overlays [D24]; named platform export targets. Skip AI titles and thumbnails, which YouTube Studio is adding itself [C29].
365	- **Measure multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback (S).** Bet 5 and any claim to lead depend on it. It is a measurement, not performance work.
366	- **`search_media` over cached transcripts (S).** The useful slice of a footage index. Build the Vision and Sound Analysis analysis inside bets 3, 4 and 6.
367	- **Merge the in-app tutorials after TU4 (S).** Creators arriving from CapCut need onboarding. The merge needs TutorialTargets rows for the audio road map.
368	- **Optical-flow slow motion, spike first (S, then M).** `VTFrameProcessor` accepts only 64RGBAHalf on this Mac, and its handling of HDR encodings is untested. Interpolated smooth cuts across a jump cut stay a spike, not a commitment.
369	- **WebVTT import (S); translated captions later (M).** A later phase of a caption road map, not a bet.
370	
371	## Not worth chasing
372	
373	| Item | Reason |
374	|---|---|
375	| Generative media: AI B-roll and video, avatars, voice clones, lip-synced dubbing | Nothing on the device can do it, so it means brokering credit-metered vendor APIs, the model Frame Job competes against. It carries disclosure risk [D25]. YouTube [C26] and Instagram [C28] now dub and translate for free. |
376	| Direct upload, scheduling, hosted share links, platform analytics | An open-source app with no backend cannot keep OAuth client secrets. A shared quota would cap all users together, and posting APIs need audits. Share links need a server. Bring-your-own storage is the only later form that fits. |
377	| Stock libraries; a template marketplace | These need licensing, curation and a backend. One developer cannot match CapCut's volume [C1] or MotionVFX inside Final Cut Pro [P15]. Agent-written graphics and `.fjgraphic` packages are the counter. |
378	| Eye-contact correction, face retouching | Apple has no public API for these on recorded video. They would need cloud or custom generative face models, with likeness risk and a per-frame cost the one-pass compositor cannot absorb. |
379	| Cloud sync, collaboration, mobile or iPad apps, Windows | Each needs a backend or a second platform. |
380	| Remote guest recording, live multi-camera capture | This is Riverside's moat [C9] and needs WebRTC servers. Import the per-guest files instead, and switch between them with bet 5. |
381	| A virality score | Creators distrust scored clips [D16]. A stated reason per moment is honest and controllable. |
382	| A standalone on-device footage index | The major editors shipped footage search within a year [P1] [P13] [P9]. Vision gives only fixed labels, so free-text search needs a bundled model whose licence is unverified. Build slices inside bets 3, 4 and 6, plus `search_media`. |
383	| Script to cut: a listening teleprompter that assembles takes | Teleprompters are common [S19] [S16]. Script-first recording suits a minority. `SpeechEngine.swift` is file-based today. The valuable kernel, retake removal, belongs in bet 1. |
384	| Translated captions and soft subtitle tracks as a bet | Platforms translate themselves [C26] [C28]. ADA Title II needs same-language captions, which Frame Job already makes. Platforms take the sidecar SRT and VTT files Frame Job already writes. |
385	| A publish kit as a headline | YouTube Studio is adding AI titles and title and thumbnail tests [C29]. The on-device model's context cannot hold a long transcript, and Frame Job already meets the loudness targets. Only the S slice is worth doing. |
386	| More MCP surface or a second agent mode as the headline | MCP became expected in 2026 [C6] [C13] [C21] [P10]. Every creator job shipped as ops becomes an agent tool anyway. |
387	| Stabilisation, for now | Phones stabilise in camera, and stabilisation mainly serves handheld vlogs. It is feasible later as a cached render. |
388	| Live-compositor motion blur | It needs several sub-frame passes, which breaks the one-pass compositor. |
389	| A plugin system | It contradicts the closed effect vocabulary (spec §11 R5-1, G-1) that preview and export parity and the proof suite rest on. |
390	| Pro finishing as headline features (Dolby Vision, synthetic depth of field) | Resolve and Final Cut Pro own these [P9]. Frame Job's colour and HDR already lead every creator tool. |
391	| Analytics-driven idea features | The platforms hold the data [C23] [C29]. |
392	
393	## Decisions for the owner
394	
395	1. **Lead segment.** Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
396	2. **Which spec §1 non-goals to lift, and how far.**
397	   - Auto-reframe: needed for bet 3.
398	   - Multicam: narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5).
399	   - ML and heavy pixel work: needed for camera cutout (issue #124's D5, bet 6).
400	   - Optical-flow retiming and motion blur: stay out until a spike.
401	   - A plugin system: stays out.
402	3. **Which spec §11 decisions to amend before code.**
403	   - TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1).
404	   - `recording.md`: cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and a schema bump (bet 2).
405	   - AI-10, for Proposals.
406	   - W-10, for inspector caption styling.
407	4. **Shortcut capture.** Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, with capture opt-in and limited to modifier shortcuts by default.
408	5. **Vertical versions.** A regenerated copy (M), or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
409	6. **Language models.** Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
410	7. **Cloud.** Confirm that bring-your-own key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
411	8. **Performance.** Allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
412	9. **Real use.** Cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
413	10. **Positioning.** Whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises [C5] [S7] [D19], metered credits [D7] [P7] and content-licence scares [D18].
414	
415	## Sources
416	
417	The "What Frame Job has" section cites repository paths only and has no external sources. The bets and Not worth chasing sections cite the tags below; no source is first cited there. Dates are each page's as-of date as recorded by the research sweeps.
418

content.content:
1	## Shared ground — CJ0 and shared infrastructure
2	
3	This is the part of road map "creator-jobs" (`designs/creator-jobs.md`) that no single bet owns:
4	the scope and the record (CJ0a), the tolls (CJ0b, CJ0c, CJ0d), the key rule (CJ1), and the
5	infrastructure two or more bets would otherwise build twice or collide on (CJ2a, CJ2b, CJ3,
6	CJ6). The six bets (TX transcript, CU cursor and recorder, VR vertical, FC find clips, SW switch
7	by speaker, CO cutout and layouts) are designed elsewhere. This section names what they build on,
8	reconciles what their sections assumed about it ("What the bets build on"), and sets the order
9	they run in. Line counts are `wc -l` at `d0661e5d` (main, 2026-11-01).
10	
11	### Goal
12	
13	A person gets two things from the shared phases directly, and everything else through the bets:
14	
15	- **Honest AI controls.** A command that would send to Claude or AssemblyAI is greyed out when its
16	  key is missing, and its tooltip says which key and where to set it. An agent's call that would
17	  send is refused with the same sentence. Nothing falls back to a weaker on-device model. Results
18	  already paid for keep working without a key.
19	- **Split at Shot Changes.** Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes cuts a flattened video (a finished edit,
20	  a downloaded clip, a stream VOD) at each hard cut, as one undo step. It is the first command on
21	  the analysis lane and the lane's proof in real use.
22	
23	For the bets, the shared phases provide: one gate for keys; one lane, one store, one reader and
24	one sheet for every analysis of pictures and sounds, with hard cuts and face samples as its first
25	kinds; a decided clip ceiling; the files at the cap cut once, before three lanes reach for them;
26	and the record (decisions, IDs, lanes, trial, samples). A new project from a range of the
27	timeline is FC1 and FC2's (bet 4), not a shared phase: only FC uses it. Source ranges on the
28	placement ops are the survey's next tier, and no bet uses them (CJ4 retired).

491	  `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>.json`, and a payload folder, `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>/`,
492	  holding whatever files the kind names (`faces` a `samples.bin`, `shots` a `frames.bin`, CO's

496	  presentation time (`shots`), samples at k / rate (`faces`, `subjects`), fixed chunks (masks),
497	  windows at k × hop (`sound-events`) — and stores per grid point only values that depend on that
498	  point's input and a fixed neighbourhood the kind names (`shots`' two previous frames), never on
499	  where a job began or on what else is cached. Thresholds over time, minimum lengths, smoothing
500	  and identity are applied when a request is answered, over the requested window. The marker
501	  holds the `AnalysisStamp`, the payload's files and the COVERAGE: the sorted, merged ranges of
502	  grid indices stored. A request is a hit when the coverage holds every index of its window plus
503	  the kind's read margin; otherwise a job runs only the missing ranges, each with the kind's
504	  pre-roll, and the coverage grows. Payload files are written through a `.partial` and a rename,
505	  the marker last, all inside `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The `AnalysisStamp`
506	  is the source's identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no path), the kind
507	  and its version (Vision request revisions inside it), a digest of the kind's parameters, the OS

510	  HDR transfer; `fullRange`; a PQ peak). A stamp that differs in any field is a miss: the next
511	  store deletes the marker first, then the payload, and starts empty (§5.6's order). So relink,
512	  consolidate and `set_media_color` invalidate as they do every cache. Coordinates are normalised
513	  0…1 in the media's display orientation, origin top-left, and every answer carries the display
514	  width and height; times are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or reversal over the
515	  file reuses them through `SourceMap` and `ReverseMirror`.

517	  `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` over the first video track, decoded to 32BGRA, scaled to the kind's
518	  long edge and turned to display orientation from the track's orientation codes
519	  (`CompositionBuilder+Orientation.swift`). The converted reader is an
520	  `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` over `MediaImporter.oneClip`'s composition, rendered at

524	  rule 5 says otherwise for a kind; every other media is read direct. Frames are read in

527	- **CJ-24 — `shots`, the first kind: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.**
528	  Each frame's signature (CJ-S4 picks it: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, or a
529	  4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at long side 256) gives two stored values, d1, its L1 distance to the
530	  frame before, and d2, its distance to the frame two before; the kind's pre-roll is two frames.
531	  When answered, frame i is a cut when d1(i) ≥ T; d2(i + 1) ≥ T, so a single flash frame that
532	  returns to the shot is not a cut; and d1(i) is the largest d1 within m frames either side, ties
533	  to the earlier frame. A dissolve, whose frame-to-frame distances stay under T, is not a cut. T
534	  and m are CJ-S4's; the read margin is m + 1 frames each side. The same window answers the same
535	  cuts whatever was asked before.
