609	
610	Each rule is fixed here, before its run, and hashed at CJ0a. Instruments go in
611	`tools/proof/creator_spike/`; each run's `results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `creator-jobs.md`
612	as `rule_sha256` (CAM-2's precedent), and the verdict is recorded in the road map and in the
613	decision named. The analysis spikes are one set: CJ-S2 (Vision), CJ-S3 (the lane) and CJ-S4
614	(shots) hold the only rules for rate, size, device, log input, playback impact and shot
615	detection; VR1 and CO1 re-run their rows for their own kinds under the same rules.
616	
617	- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling (at CJ6's head; decides CJ-9).** Question: how many clips can a
618	  project hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096,
619	  8,192, 16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as
620	  packages. N above 4,096 needs a scratch Release build with the cap raised, never committed.
621	  Measured: (1) `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2)
622	  `rc_project_from_json` plus `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times,
623	  median; (4) over MCP, one `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo, each from the call
624	  to its answer; (5) after (4), the time until the next main-thread call (`get_project`) answers,
625	  which covers Swift's snapshot decode and the timeline's refresh; (6) after an edit, the time
626	  until `play_preview` composes its first frame, which covers `CompositionBuilder`'s rebuild; (7)
627	  the timeline's draw, from a probe built through `swift_build.py` that lays out and draws a
628	  `TimelineView` of N clips offscreen at the fit-all zoom and at the default zoom, median of 20;
629	  (8) the app's resident memory after 50 undo steps of `split`. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N
630	  for which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms, (4) applies and undoes in ≤ 1 s each, (5) ≤ 1 s,
631	  (6) ≤ 2 s, (7) ≤ 33 ms at both zooms, and (8) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical memory.
632	  N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096 and CJ6 ends with
633	  the verdict and no code.
634	- **CJ-S2 — Vision on video (at CJ3's head; decides CJ-30 and CJ-32; replaces VR-S1's rules 1–4
635	  and CO-S1's device question).** Question: on which device, at what rate and size, and from which
636	  reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate on this Mac? Inputs: the face
637	  fixtures of "Samples and fixtures", always; S-TH1, S-TH2, S-TH3 and S-TH4 when they exist.
638	  Measured: the cache bytes of three runs on each of CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; seconds per minute
639	  of source for decode, rectangles, and rectangles with landmarks, at long sides 720, 1280 and
640	  1920 and native; face recall (the share of samples, in the spans where a face is known present,
641	  with a box overlapping it) at each size; recall and reader cost raw against converted on each
642	  log or HLG sample; face share over S-TH1's first 60 s. **Rules:**
643	  1. **Device:** the fastest of the three whose three runs are byte-identical. If none is, the CPU
644	     when it meets rule 2's rate; otherwise the fastest, with every proof comparing against the
645	     cache only (E9's rule).
646	  2. **Rate:** 10 samples a second if decode plus rectangles plus landmarks run at least 3× real
647	     time on 1080p30 and 1.5× on 4K30 on the chosen device; else 5; else 2.5 (VR-S1's numbers).
648	  3. **Size:** the smallest long side of 720, 1280 and 1920 whose face recall is at least 98 % of
649	     recall at native size, on the small-face fixture and on S-TH1 when it exists.
650	  4. **Landmarks** stay in `faces` if they cost at most 2× rectangles alone; else mouth opening is
651	     a `mouths` kind on the same grid, built by SW8.
652	  5. **Log and HDR input:** the converted reader, unless on every log or HLG sample run raw recall
653	     is at least 98 % of converted recall AND the converted reader costs more than 1.5× the direct
654	     one per frame (CJ-S3's figure); then the face kinds read raw. With no such sample, converted.
655	  6. **Face share** on S-TH1's first 60 s, which its brief makes front-facing: below 95 % stops
656	     VR1 and SW8 until an amendment of CJ-30. CJ3 lands on the fixtures either way; without S-TH1
657	     the row is skipped by name and owed in CJ3's record.
658	  VR1 re-runs rules 1–3 and 5 for its `subjects` requests (human rectangles and saliency) with the
659	  same instrument, and keeps VR-S1's rules 5 and 6. CO1 runs rule 1 for its mask request.
660	- **CJ-S3 — The lane (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23; replaces CO-S4).** Question: what
661	  does decoding for analysis cost, does a second concurrent picture job pay, and does analysis
662	  cost playback? Measured on a 4K HEVC 10-bit HLG file and a 1080p H.264 file (synthetic, by
663	  `ffmpeg`, until S-TH4 exists): frames a second through the direct and the converted reader at
664	  long sides 256 and 1280; the total throughput of one job and of two; and `play_preview`'s
665	  composed frames over 20 s of a 1080p30 timeline idle, then with a `shots` job running.
666	  **Rules:** (a) **width:** 2 only if two jobs reach at least 1.5× one job's throughput; else 1.
667	  (b) **playback:** when composed frames with a job running fall by more than 2 % against idle,
668	  the picture queue pauses while any transport plays and resumes when none does (CJ-21). CJ3 (a
669	  `faces` job), VR1 (`subjects`) and CO1 (masks) each re-run (b) with their own job at their head;
670	  the first failure turns the pause on for every picture kind, recorded as an amendment of CJ-21.
671	  (c) **reader:** the converted reader for converting media and the direct one for the rest,
672	  unless CJ-S2's rule 5 says otherwise for a kind.
673	- **CJ-S4 — The shot signature (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-24; replaces VR-S2).** Question:
674	  which signature, threshold T and neighbourhood m find hard cuts inside one flattened clip?
675	  Candidates: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, and a 4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at
676	  long side 256, both by L1 distance. Inputs: the shots fixture (known cuts, a dissolve, a white
677	  flash frame); a no-cut talking head (S-TH1, else ten minutes of the moving-still fixture); and
678	  flattened exports with known cut lists (the trial's exports when they exist, and always a
679	  synthetic one: a fixture project of 40 clips cut from four `testsrc` variants, exported by Frame
680	  Job, its cut list read from `get_project`). **Rule:** the signature and T with the highest
681	  recall on the flattened exports subject to at most one false cut per 10 minutes on the no-cut
682	  input, and m the largest of 4, 6, 8 and 12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It
683	  passes at recall ≥ 98 % on the flattened exports. If no candidate passes, a 64 × 36 luma sum of
684	  absolute differences joins as a second signal and the run repeats; if that fails, CJ-24 ships
685	  with the measured recall stated in the guide.

1178	**How Vision-dependent proofs stay deterministic.** (1) A planner's rows run on canned analyses
1179	and assert bytes. (2) Vision's rows on fixtures and real samples assert tolerances fixed before
1180	the run, never exact numbers. (3) A determinism row compares two runs on the pinned device, byte
1181	for byte. (4) A proof compares against the cache, never against a recomputation. (5) Every stamp
1182	carries the OS build, the compute device and the reader's input, and every results file records
1183	all three. (6) Stored values depend on one grid point, so an answer never depends on call order
1184	(CJ2a's A9). (7) What only a person can judge — whether a reframe, a cutout or a switch looks
1185	right on real footage — is a JOB row.

469	- **CJ-20 — Analysis is a cache, made on demand.** It never runs at import, is never project
470	  state, and is never read by the composition plan or the frame recipe. A planner reads it and
471	  writes ordinary edits. A render drawn from it (CO's masks) is substituted by Swift, as a
472	  reversed file is (§5.6). So no analysis kind bumps the format. VR-10's on-demand rule is this
473	  one; the speech cache's import-time rule stands for speech.
474	- **CJ-21 — One lane, `AnalysisLane`, process-wide, with two queues.** A picture queue (decodes
475	  and Vision) and a sound queue (audio decodes and Sound Analysis), so a sound job never waits
476	  behind a face job. Each is its own `DispatchQueue` at `.utility`, never the cooperative pool and
477	  never `MediaCacheLane`; the picture queue's width is spike CJ-S3's (1 until it earns 2), the
478	  sound queue's 1. A job is a source, a window and the kinds asked for it; kinds that share a
479	  reader, a size and a grid decode once (VR's subjects and CJ3's faces). Jobs are wanted by owners
480	  — a document's command, a tool call, an export — as ramp audio's renders are (SR-12): a job
481	  nobody wants is cancelled, one wanted again while it runs is not, `wait` returns on landing,
482	  failure or cancellation, and an owner's `settled` runs on main. A job takes no `CachePass` and
483	  writes only through `CacheLedger.publish(in:for: nil)`, so an import pass and an analysis job of
484	  the same media never cancel or wait on each other. `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>` (a build with
485	  `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` only) holds each job for s seconds before its first frame, polling
486	  cancellation every 50 ms, as `-RCDevRampRenderHold` does. When CJ-S3's playback rule turns it
487	  on, the picture queue pauses between frames while any transport plays and resumes when none
488	  does, through a new internal `BackgroundRender.anyPlaying` over its `transports`
489	  (`BackgroundRender.swift:71`).
490	- **CJ-22 — The store.** A kind's results for one source are a marker,
491	  `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>.json`, and a payload folder, `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>/`,
492	  holding whatever files the kind names (`faces` a `samples.bin`, `shots` a `frames.bin`, CO's
493	  masks one movie per chunk). `<source>` is the media id, or `<media id>r` for a kind that reads a
494	  media's reversed render (CO-4). A kind whose variants must coexist puts the variant in its
495	  name (`masks-standard`, `masks-best`). Every kind has a grid on source time — frames by
496	  presentation time (`shots`), samples at k / rate (`faces`, `subjects`), fixed chunks (masks),
497	  windows at k × hop (`sound-events`) — and stores per grid point only values that depend on that
498	  point's input and a fixed neighbourhood the kind names (`shots`' two previous frames), never on
499	  where a job began or on what else is cached. Thresholds over time, minimum lengths, smoothing
500	  and identity are applied when a request is answered, over the requested window. The marker
501	  holds the `AnalysisStamp`, the payload's files and the COVERAGE: the sorted, merged ranges of
502	  grid indices stored. A request is a hit when the coverage holds every index of its window plus
503	  the kind's read margin; otherwise a job runs only the missing ranges, each with the kind's
504	  pre-roll, and the coverage grows. Payload files are written through a `.partial` and a rename,
505	  the marker last, all inside `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The `AnalysisStamp`
506	  is the source's identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no path), the kind
507	  and its version (Vision request revisions inside it), a digest of the kind's parameters, the OS
508	  build, the compute device, and the reader's input: `raw`, or the conversion as
509	  `ConvertedThumbsStamp` records it (curve and gamut, or the LUT's path, size and second, or the
510	  HDR transfer; `fullRange`; a PQ peak). A stamp that differs in any field is a miss: the next
511	  store deletes the marker first, then the payload, and starts empty (§5.6's order). So relink,
512	  consolidate and `set_media_color` invalidate as they do every cache. Coordinates are normalised
513	  0…1 in the media's display orientation, origin top-left, and every answer carries the display
514	  width and height; times are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or reversal over the
515	  file reuses them through `SourceMap` and `ReverseMirror`.
516	- **CJ-23 — The frame reader.** `AnalysisFrames.swift` has two readers. The direct reader is an
517	  `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` over the first video track, decoded to 32BGRA, scaled to the kind's
518	  long edge and turned to display orientation from the track's orientation codes
519	  (`CompositionBuilder+Orientation.swift`). The converted reader is an
520	  `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` over `MediaImporter.oneClip`'s composition, rendered at
521	  the kind's size through step 0, so analysis sees what the person sees; `oneClip`
522	  (`MediaImporter+ThumbnailSource.swift:311`) loses `private` and nothing else in that file
523	  changes. A media whose picture converts (Camera Log, HLG, PQ) is read converted unless CJ-S2's
524	  rule 5 says otherwise for a kind; every other media is read direct. Frames are read in
525	  presentation order; each goes to the kind's per-frame callback, and a sample at k / rate takes
526	  the first frame whose presentation time is at or after it (VR's callbacks).
527	- **CJ-24 — `shots`, the first kind: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.**
528	  Each frame's signature (CJ-S4 picks it: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, or a
529	  4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at long side 256) gives two stored values, d1, its L1 distance to the
530	  frame before, and d2, its distance to the frame two before; the kind's pre-roll is two frames.
531	  When answered, frame i is a cut when d1(i) ≥ T; d2(i + 1) ≥ T, so a single flash frame that
532	  returns to the shot is not a cut; and d1(i) is the largest d1 within m frames either side, ties
533	  to the earlier frame. A dissolve, whose frame-to-frame distances stay under T, is not a cut. T
534	  and m are CJ-S4's; the read margin is m + 1 frames each side. The same window answers the same
535	  cuts whatever was asked before.

537	  reusing it.** Exactly one of `media` and `clip`. With `media` the window defaults to the whole

543	  (`queued_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at` in process uptime seconds, only when this call ran a

609	
610	Each rule is fixed here, before its run, and hashed at CJ0a. Instruments go in
611	`tools/proof/creator_spike/`; each run's `results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `creator-jobs.md`
612	as `rule_sha256` (CAM-2's precedent), and the verdict is recorded in the road map and in the
613	decision named. The analysis spikes are one set: CJ-S2 (Vision), CJ-S3 (the lane) and CJ-S4
614	(shots) hold the only rules for rate, size, device, log input, playback impact and shot
615	detection; VR1 and CO1 re-run their rows for their own kinds under the same rules.
616	
617	- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling (at CJ6's head; decides CJ-9).** Question: how many clips can a
618	  project hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096,
619	  8,192, 16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as
620	  packages. N above 4,096 needs a scratch Release build with the cap raised, never committed.
621	  Measured: (1) `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2)
622	  `rc_project_from_json` plus `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times,
623	  median; (4) over MCP, one `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo, each from the call
624	  to its answer; (5) after (4), the time until the next main-thread call (`get_project`) answers,
625	  which covers Swift's snapshot decode and the timeline's refresh; (6) after an edit, the time
626	  until `play_preview` composes its first frame, which covers `CompositionBuilder`'s rebuild; (7)
627	  the timeline's draw, from a probe built through `swift_build.py` that lays out and draws a
628	  `TimelineView` of N clips offscreen at the fit-all zoom and at the default zoom, median of 20;
629	  (8) the app's resident memory after 50 undo steps of `split`. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N
630	  for which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms, (4) applies and undoes in ≤ 1 s each, (5) ≤ 1 s,
631	  (6) ≤ 2 s, (7) ≤ 33 ms at both zooms, and (8) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical memory.
632	  N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096 and CJ6 ends with
633	  the verdict and no code.
634	- **CJ-S2 — Vision on video (at CJ3's head; decides CJ-30 and CJ-32; replaces VR-S1's rules 1–4
635	  and CO-S1's device question).** Question: on which device, at what rate and size, and from which
636	  reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate on this Mac? Inputs: the face
637	  fixtures of "Samples and fixtures", always; S-TH1, S-TH2, S-TH3 and S-TH4 when they exist.
638	  Measured: the cache bytes of three runs on each of CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; seconds per minute
639	  of source for decode, rectangles, and rectangles with landmarks, at long sides 720, 1280 and
640	  1920 and native; face recall (the share of samples, in the spans where a face is known present,
641	  with a box overlapping it) at each size; recall and reader cost raw against converted on each
642	  log or HLG sample; face share over S-TH1's first 60 s. **Rules:**
643	  1. **Device:** the fastest of the three whose three runs are byte-identical. If none is, the CPU
644	     when it meets rule 2's rate; otherwise the fastest, with every proof comparing against the
645	     cache only (E9's rule).
646	  2. **Rate:** 10 samples a second if decode plus rectangles plus landmarks run at least 3× real
647	     time on 1080p30 and 1.5× on 4K30 on the chosen device; else 5; else 2.5 (VR-S1's numbers).
648	  3. **Size:** the smallest long side of 720, 1280 and 1920 whose face recall is at least 98 % of
649	     recall at native size, on the small-face fixture and on S-TH1 when it exists.
650	  4. **Landmarks** stay in `faces` if they cost at most 2× rectangles alone; else mouth opening is
651	     a `mouths` kind on the same grid, built by SW8.
652	  5. **Log and HDR input:** the converted reader, unless on every log or HLG sample run raw recall
653	     is at least 98 % of converted recall AND the converted reader costs more than 1.5× the direct
654	     one per frame (CJ-S3's figure); then the face kinds read raw. With no such sample, converted.
655	  6. **Face share** on S-TH1's first 60 s, which its brief makes front-facing: below 95 % stops
656	     VR1 and SW8 until an amendment of CJ-30. CJ3 lands on the fixtures either way; without S-TH1
657	     the row is skipped by name and owed in CJ3's record.
658	  VR1 re-runs rules 1–3 and 5 for its `subjects` requests (human rectangles and saliency) with the
659	  same instrument, and keeps VR-S1's rules 5 and 6. CO1 runs rule 1 for its mask request.
660	- **CJ-S3 — The lane (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23; replaces CO-S4).** Question: what
661	  does decoding for analysis cost, does a second concurrent picture job pay, and does analysis
662	  cost playback? Measured on a 4K HEVC 10-bit HLG file and a 1080p H.264 file (synthetic, by
663	  `ffmpeg`, until S-TH4 exists): frames a second through the direct and the converted reader at
664	  long sides 256 and 1280; the total throughput of one job and of two; and `play_preview`'s
665	  composed frames over 20 s of a 1080p30 timeline idle, then with a `shots` job running.
666	  **Rules:** (a) **width:** 2 only if two jobs reach at least 1.5× one job's throughput; else 1.
667	  (b) **playback:** when composed frames with a job running fall by more than 2 % against idle,
668	  the picture queue pauses while any transport plays and resumes when none does (CJ-21). CJ3 (a
669	  `faces` job), VR1 (`subjects`) and CO1 (masks) each re-run (b) with their own job at their head;
670	  the first failure turns the pause on for every picture kind, recorded as an amendment of CJ-21.
671	  (c) **reader:** the converted reader for converting media and the direct one for the rest,
672	  unless CJ-S2's rule 5 says otherwise for a kind.
673	- **CJ-S4 — The shot signature (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-24; replaces VR-S2).** Question:
674	  which signature, threshold T and neighbourhood m find hard cuts inside one flattened clip?
675	  Candidates: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, and a 4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at
676	  long side 256, both by L1 distance. Inputs: the shots fixture (known cuts, a dissolve, a white
677	  flash frame); a no-cut talking head (S-TH1, else ten minutes of the moving-still fixture); and
678	  flattened exports with known cut lists (the trial's exports when they exist, and always a
679	  synthetic one: a fixture project of 40 clips cut from four `testsrc` variants, exported by Frame
680	  Job, its cut list read from `get_project`). **Rule:** the signature and T with the highest
681	  recall on the flattened exports subject to at most one false cut per 10 minutes on the no-cut
682	  input, and m the largest of 4, 6, 8 and 12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It
683	  passes at recall ≥ 98 % on the flattened exports. If no candidate passes, a 64 × 36 luma sum of
684	  absolute differences joins as a second signal and the run repeats; if that fails, CJ-24 ships
685	  with the measured recall stated in the guide.

1178	**How Vision-dependent proofs stay deterministic.** (1) A planner's rows run on canned analyses
1179	and assert bytes. (2) Vision's rows on fixtures and real samples assert tolerances fixed before
1180	the run, never exact numbers. (3) A determinism row compares two runs on the pinned device, byte
1181	for byte. (4) A proof compares against the cache, never against a recomputation. (5) Every stamp
1182	carries the OS build, the compute device and the reader's input, and every results file records
1183	all three. (6) Stored values depend on one grid point, so an answer never depends on call order
1184	(CJ2a's A9). (7) What only a person can judge — whether a reframe, a cutout or a switch looks
1185	right on real footage — is a JOB row.

777	### Spikes
778	
779	Each rule is fixed here, before its run, and stored by SHA-256 in the run's `results.json`
780	(CJ-7). Each spike runs at the head of the phase it decides, as TX-S3 always did. The records go
781	in the road map's phase record and in the decision each one feeds. The instruments live in
782	`tools/proof/transcript_spike/` and `tools/proof/retake_spike/`, built through
783	`tools/proof/swift_build.py`.
784	
785	- **TX-S1 — The fill's cost** (runs at the head of TX1; needs no owner media).
786	  - **Question:** how fast does `SpeechEngine` recognise long speech on this Mac, can one run
787	    cover a whole file, and does a fill slow playback?
788	  - **Method:** a probe calls `SpeechEngine.transcribe` on synthetic speech, made of `say`
789	    phrases joined into 10-minute and 60-minute files, and on S-TH1 and S-LONG1 when they exist.
790	  - **It measures:**
791	    - wall time;
792	    - peak added memory;
793	    - temporary WAV size;
794	    - word count;
795	    - each word's start against the same audio recognised as six 10-minute windows (median and
796	      95th-percentile |Δ|);
797	    - in the Release app over MCP, `play_preview`'s frames composed over 10 s of a 1080p
798	      timeline while a 60-minute fill runs at `.userInitiated`, and again at `.utility`, each
799	      against the same 10 s idle (CJ-S3's measurement for the analysis lane).
800	  - **Rules:**
801	    - Outcome A, one whole-file run per media (TX-12), if the 60-minute run finishes within 6
802	      minutes (≥ 10× real time) and its peak added memory is at most 1/32 of physical memory.
803	      Otherwise outcome B, per-clip windows from the playhead outward.
804	    - The fill keeps `.userInitiated` if `play_preview` composes at least 95 % of its idle count
805	      during it. Otherwise it runs at `.utility` if that reaches 95 %. If neither does, the fill
806	      pauses while the transport plays and resumes when it stops, and TX-12 records the figures.
807	    - Either way the measured rate replaces "a few seconds per minute" in the guide.
808	- **TX-S2 — The view** (runs at the head of TX2a).
809	  - **Question:** which view holds a three-hour transcript and leaves the transport keys to the
810	    editor?
811	  - **The candidates, in order:**
812	    - (b) a custom `NSView` laid out by TextKit 2 (`NSTextLayoutManager` over
813	      `NSTextContentStorage`, viewport layout);
814	    - (c) an `NSTableView` of paragraph rows;
815	    - (a) a read-only `NSTextView` subclass.
816	  - **Fixture:** 27,000 synthetic words in 900 paragraphs, with 40 collapsed cuts and 300 strikes,
817	    in the offscreen harness on the main thread.
818	  - **It measures:**
819	    - first layout of the visible part;
820	    - a full rebuild after an edit;
821	    - moving the highlight;
822	    - hit-testing a click to a word;
823	    - a selection across paragraphs;
824	    - added memory.
825	  - **Rule:** take the first of (b), (c) and (a) that meets all of these:
826	    - first layout ≤ 200 ms;
827	    - rebuild ≤ 100 ms;
828	    - highlight ≤ 2 ms;
829	    - hit-test ≤ 1 ms;
830	    - added memory ≤ 1/256 of physical memory;
831	    - Space and J/K/L reach `handleEditorKey` with no change to a frozen file.
832	  - **(a) is the last resort.** It meets the last test only with a change to `handleEditorKey`'s
833	    first line (`EditorViewController.swift:713`). It is taken only if (b) and (c) both fail,
834	    and that one-line change is then recorded as TX-21's deviation.
835	- **TX-S3 — Cut edges** (runs at the head of TX3).
836	  - **Question:** where should a word's cut fall, when on-device word ranges tile the audio and
837	    start 270 ms early?
838	  - **Fixtures:**
839	    1. `say` phrases joined by silences of 60, 120, 250, 500 and 1,000 ms, so every word onset is
840	       known from the synthesis.
841	    2. The owner's scripted o2 (`tools/proof/media/filler-sample/`, 29.4 s).
842	    3. S-TH1 when it exists.
843	  - **The rules compared:**
844	    - E0: the transcript's edges as given;
845	    - E1: E0 corrected by `CaptionPages.lead(for:)`;
846	    - E2: onset-to-onset from the voice cache, as TX-30 words it (lead-corrected midpoints, the
847	      previous word of the same clip and media), with E1 as its fallback, at guards of 0, 32, 64
848	      and 96 ms.
849	  - **It measures:**
850	    - per boundary on (1): a clipped onset (the cut ends after a kept word's true onset, or
851	      starts before a deleted word's true end) and the error against the true onset;
852	    - on (2) and (3): the share of edges in voice-cache non-speech and under −40 dBFS in the peak
853	      cache.
854	  - **Rule:**
855	    - Take E2 with the smallest guard that clips no onset on (1) and keeps at least 95 % of
856	      real-speech edges in non-speech.
857	    - Else take E1 if it clips none on (1).
858	    - Else E0, with JOB-TX2 the only judge. TX-30 records which.
859	- **TX-S4 — The retake rule** (runs at the head of TX7, after TX-70 is recorded; needs S-RT1,
860	  with its `say` twin as the synthetic half).
861	  - **Question:** which phrase split, window and similarity find planted retakes and restarts
862	    without striking the traps?
863	  - **The script and its answer key** are in `tools/proof/retake_spike/SCRIPT.md`: 8 retakes, 8
864	    restarts, 6 repeats and 6 traps. The traps are deliberate repetitions: an anaphora, "that
865	    that", a refrain and a list.
866	  - **The reads.**
867	    - Both reads are recognised on this Mac.
868	    - AssemblyAI is used only if the owner allows the paid run (about a cent, under P-3's
869	      budget).
870	  - **The grid:**
871	    - pause P {0.4, 0.6, 0.8 s};
872	    - window K {2, 3};
873	    - similarity θ {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8};
874	    - one-word repeats {off, pause-separated}.
875	  - **Rule:**
876	    - Among the settings that strike no trap word on either read, take the one with the highest
877	      recall of retakes plus restarts on the owner's read. Ties go to the higher θ.
878	    - If that recall is under 80 %, the retake kind ships off by default.
879	    - If no setting strikes no trap word, the retake kind ships off by default, and restarts and

880	      repeats ship on at the setting with the fewest trap strikes on both reads together, ties
881	      to the higher θ.
882	    - TX-71 records the setting, and the strikes it makes on S-TH1 go to JOB-TX5.

839	    mapping, per geometry change), and sample times to source ticks.

841	    - The path is pinned at every click.

848	      it never computes one.

1760	### Risks
1761	
1762	- **`NSCursor.currentSystem` will answer nil "in a future version of macOS"** (`NSCursor.h:155`).
1763	  - It typechecks with no warning today (SDK 26.2, target 26.0). A later SDK may mark it
1764	    deprecated at 27.0. That adds a warning to the 4-warning baseline only if Swift warns below
1765	    the deployment target.
1766	  - At run time the recorder checks every sample for nil; a recording with no image draws the
1767	    arrow and says so (CU-S1's rule). CU-S1's A10 measures a replacement, which is built only
1768	    if `currentSystem` already fails.
1769	- **Input Monitoring is attributed to the terminal for a shell launch** (R0 q1), and an event
1770	  tap may need a relaunch after the grant. The sentences carry `launchClause`, CU-S1 measures
1771	  the relaunch, and JOB-4 checks it.
1772	- **Key data is sensitive.** CU-7's mitigations: no typed character is ever stored; nothing
1773	  during secure input; a visible mark. The remaining limit: a password typed where secure input
1774	  is off leaves its keystroke times in the file. The panel's sentence and the guide say so,
1775	  and JOB-5 shows it.
1776	- **Granted proofs.** An ad-hoc build loses Screen Recording, Input Monitoring and the poster's
1777	  Accessibility at every `make app` (CJ-4), so the granted rows skip by name in a pipeline.
1778	  Every mutant listed has an ungranted killer (a probe, `land_recording` or a fixture); the
1779	  granted rows are extra coverage, and their residue is JOB rows.
1780	- **The frame watch is now on every screen recording.** Its resume workaround (CAM-9 (6)) was
1781	  measured in only 2 + 3 runs. K4 runs pause and resume on every granted proof run, K0 holds the
1782	  rule, and K6 bounds its CPU.
1783	- **A cursor file lost or not moved with the movie leaves a Separate recording with no
1784	  pointer.** Mitigations:
1785	  - Consolidate carries it (CU5) and Relink keeps or replaces it (CU3b);
1786	  - the Media tab names a missing file;
1787	  - an export and `render_frame` name it in `cursor_warnings`;
1788	  - In the picture stays available;
1789	  - CU-14 makes a failed write the landing's note.
1790	- **Timing.** E1's fallback (21 ms) is about one 60 fps frame. With Separate it is used
1791	  whenever a segment starts on a still screen; CU-S2 bounds it and K9 checks it.
1792	- **Window sources.** An occluding window over the recorded window still shows the cursor at
1793	  its position, because occlusion is not sampled. CU-S2 may STOP window sources, which then

1795	- **Hidden cursors.** An app that hides the pointer while typing may still report an image.

3	### Goal
4	
5	A creator finishes a 16:9 edit and chooses **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. Frame Job opens a
6	copy of the project at 9:16 (1080 × 1920 from a 1080p canvas, 2160 × 3840 from a 4K one) or 1:1.
7	In the copy:
8	
9	- every full-frame picture fills the tall frame and follows the face, the person or the salient
10	  region that Vision found on the Mac, as eased x, y and scale actions on the clip's own action
11	  lane, which the creator selects and nudges on the canvas like any other action;
12	- a shot with nothing to follow (a screen, a landscape, a two-shot too wide to crop) is shown
13	  whole over a blurred copy of itself;
14	- a cut inside a clip (an export of another edit, imported as one file) is a hard cut in the
15	  framing too;
16	- word captions are paged again for the narrow frame from their own words, so corrections made
17	  by hand survive, and subtitles take the narrow frame's measure;
18	- a graphic that filled the 16:9 frame is re-sized to the tall one and lays itself out again;
19	- a background plate or blurred backdrop that filled the 16:9 frame fills the tall one;
20	- every other layer (a camera bubble, a title, a logo) keeps its relative place;
21	- existing zooms keep what they showed: each is composed with the framing, never left aiming at
22	  16:9 targets.

25	the canvas they are on (a 4K talking head on a 1080p canvas, a 16:9 clip dropped into a vertical
26	project). After bet 2, a screen recording's vertical version follows the cursor. After bet 5, a
27	two-person wide shot follows whoever is speaking. Later, if the owner chooses, one project holds
28	several **framings** of one cut (linked versions), so a trim in the 16:9 cut is a trim in the 9:16
29	one.

31	Nothing is uploaded, nothing needs a key, and every result is an ordinary undo step and an MCP

272	  the path, enforces coverage and writes actions. It is an op rather than a composite because two

633	- **VR-S1 — People and saliency on video** (at VR1's start, after CJ-S2's verdict, on CJ-32's pinned
634	  device).
635	  - *Question:* at what rate and frame size do `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2 and
636	    `VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2 run deterministically and fast enough, and
637	    do person boxes hold when the face is lost?
638	  - *Instrument:* `tools/proof/creator_spike/vr_subjects/` (synchronous VN* calls, as
639	    `effects_spike/vision_job.swift`), reading frames through CJ-23's reader. Inputs: S-TH1 (with
640	    its leave, turn-away and side-on beats marked by the owner), S-VR1 (HLG), and CJ's
641	    moving-still fixture.
642	  - *Rules:*
643	    1. **The rate** is `faces`' rate if both requests together, at `faces`' frame size, run at
644	       ≥ 4× realtime (CJ-S2's bar); otherwise every other `faces` sample.
645	    2. **The frame size** is `faces`' unless person recall there is more than 1 percentage point
646	       under recall at a long side of 1440 on S-TH1, in which case it is 1440.
647	    3. **Determinism:** three runs on the pinned device give byte-identical files. Otherwise STOP:
648	       the kind's stamp carries a tolerance instead (an amendment before VR1's code, CJ-S2's form).
649	    4. **People stay** if the person box is found in ≥ 90 % of S-TH1's turned-away and side-on
650	       samples. Otherwise `people` is dropped from `subjects` and VR-21's person tier is removed
651	       by amendment before VR1's code.
652	    5. **HLG:** with S-VR1, person recall through CJ-23's converted path is recorded; no rule
653	       (CJ-23 decides the path).
654	- **VR-S2 — The planner's first numbers** (with VR2a, over cached analyses, no video).
655	  - *Question:* which dead zone, pan speed and composition give a talking head that is framed
656	    without fidget?
657	  - *Instrument:* the core's planner run from a test binary over S-TH1's cached `faces` and
658	    `subjects`, T1's and T2's, and the canned fixtures. The grid is dead zone {6, 10, 15} % ×
659	    speed {0.3, 0.5, 0.8} windows/s × headroom {33, 38, 42} %. It measures containment (the face
660	    centre inside the window's central 60 %) and moves per minute.
661	  - *Rule:* the setting with the highest containment at no more than 6 moves per minute. If no
662	    setting reaches 97 % containment, the dead zone shrinks one step and the cap rises to 8.
663	    JOB-31 judges the feel.
664	- **VR-S3 — Face-to-mic agreement** (at VR6's start).
665	  - *Question:* does mouth opening against SW-21's turns tell which face is which mic?
666	  - *Instrument:* over S-PC2 recorded with a microphone each (and the two-face moving-still with
667	    synthetic turns), the agreement for the true pairing and for the swapped one.
668	  - *Rule:* the threshold is the midpoint between the lowest true-pair agreement and the highest
669	    swapped-pair agreement when they separate. If they do not, VR6 always asks (VR-61), and the
670	    guide says so.
671	- **VR-S4 — A framing switch in the preview** (before VR7a's code, only if the owner says yes).
672	  - *Question:* how long does the preview take to rebuild when the canvas size changes on a

676	    it keeps the last two framings' compositions. A framing whose plan warns past 8 decoders is

1179	### Risks
1180	
1181	- **Upscaled 1080p.** A 1080p source fills a 1080 × 1920 frame at ×1.78, which is visibly soft.
1182	  Nothing hides it. The guide says to shoot 4K for vertical, and JOB-33 judges it.
1183	- **Vision on log, dark or small faces.** CJ-S2 measures faces on the owner's footage, and VR-S1
1184	  people; a person too small at the chosen size forces 1440, at analysis cost.
1185	- **Results that move with macOS.** A new OS can change Vision's answers. CJ-22's stamp pins the
1186	  kind's version, the OS build and the device, so a new OS re-analyses on the next command. Proofs
1187	  compare against the cache, not against a recomputation.
1188	- **The wrong subject.** A poster on the wall, a face on a monitor, or an audience member can win
1189	  VR-21's score. The hysteresis, the nudge and the Follow popup are the answers. A recording with a
1190	  sidecar never follows faces (VR-51).
1191	- **Composition inside existing actions.** A framing move inside an existing action is
1192	  approximated by that action's curve, and splitting an eased action re-eases both halves. Both
1193	  are counted in the summary. Coverage still holds (VR-7).
1194	- **Motion presets.** A clip with a moving `video.motion` keeps it, and the coverage guarantee
1195	  excludes its span; a During motion excludes the whole clip. The summary names each.
1196	- **Timeline clutter.** A long take gets many framing actions on its lane. Each is an ordinary
1197	  action the person can delete.
1198	- **Decoder budget.** Each `fit` clip adds a blurred copy that decodes the same file. The plan
1199	  warns past 8 concurrent video tracks, and it does not refuse.
1200	- **Track cap.** Backdrops share one track (VR-25). Only overlapping `fit` clips on different
1201	  tracks need a second. At 64 the step is refused in the core's sentence, nothing is made, and the
1202	  summary names it.
1203	- **Graphics written by people or agents.** A graphic that does not lay itself out from
1204	  `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` may overflow the tall frame. Only the bundled templates and their
1205	  unedited copies are fixed (VR-43, VR-44). The guide and `docs/graphics-api.md` say how.
1206	- **Portrait projects change.** VR-41 changes Subtitles and Text ▸ Presets on every portrait
1207	  project, not only vertical versions; landscape and square output is byte-identical.
1208	- **Untimed or restyled captions** cannot be re-paged. Their track is kept, placed by `keep`, and
1209	  listed.
1210	- **Analysis time.** A one-hour recording takes minutes even windowed, and three kinds read it.
1211	  The Analyzing sheet has Stop, a tool answers `analyzing` past CJ-25's bound instead of blocking,
1212	  and the cache makes a second run free.
1213	- **The copy drifts from the master.** That is by design until linked versions exist. JOB-35 says
1214	  whether it matters.
1215	- **Files at the cap.** `edit_action.rs` (595) must take nothing: if VR2b needs a helper there, it
1216	  pays the end-patch toll first. `CaptionLayout.swift` (581) pays its toll at VR4.
1217	  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` and `ReelCore.swift` pay theirs at VR7a and VR7b.
1218	- **Linked versions are large.** VR7a–VR9 touch every op that carries actions and the
1219	  recipe-and-plan seam. The owner's yes at VR7a is the gate, and VR-S4 runs before the code.

1	## Bet 4 — Find Clips: ranked moments that open as real vertical edits
2	
3	### Goal
4	
5	A creator with a long recording — an episode, a stream's VOD, a finished horizontal edit — chooses
6	Clip ▸ Find Clips…. Frame Job listens to it on the Mac: the words and where sentences end, who is
7	speaking, where the speech is loud or fast, and where people laugh, clap or cheer. The window then
8	lists the Mac's candidate moments in time order, each with its sentences, its marks and a Play
9	button, and the timeline shows each as a numbered wash. This much needs no key.
10	
11	With the creator's own Anthropic key set, Rank sends the transcript, with those readings marked in
12	it, to Claude, which picks the 10, 20 or 30 best moments of 20 to 60 seconds. The window says what
13	Rank sends and what it will probably cost before the press. Each picked moment is listed with its
14	in and out points on sentence ends, its length, a short title and a one-line reason ("laughter
15	after the punchline", "the one sentence that answers the episode's question"). There is no score.
16	
17	The creator ticks the moments worth posting and presses Make Shorts. Each ticked moment becomes
18	its own saved Frame Job project: exactly that range of the timeline, made vertical by bet 3's Make
19	Vertical Version, with filler words cut where a cloud transcript holds them, word-captioned in the
20	chosen style, and queued on the Export Queue. Every short is an ordinary project that opens as an
21	editable timeline. Nothing on the source timeline changes.
22	
23	Two pieces stand on their own and need no key: File ▸ New Project from Range… (CJ5's, which this
24	bet builds on) and File ▸ Make Short from Range… (the short pipeline for a range the creator chose
25	by hand). An outside agent gets the analysis without the ranking: `find_clips` answers the
26	sentences, the readings and the candidate windows the Mac found, and the agent ranks them with its
27	own model, so Frame Job runs no model for it (the design's recommendation; FC6 asks the owner).

522	Each rule is fixed here and its text stored by SHA-256 before its run (CJ-7). A spike runs at the
523	head of the phase that needs it, and its verdict is recorded as the decision named. Paid runs are
524	behind `--live --cap`, held to P-6's ledger and the month's budget. An Anthropic request reads its
525	key only through `tools/proof/assistant_prompt_eval.py`'s `anthropic_key()` (:79). An AssemblyAI
526	request goes through `tools/proof/cloud_spike/`'s client, whose key is `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY`
527	(`aai.py`:32), supplied by the owner for that run, and through `cloud_live_ledger.py` with its cap.
528	Only the owner's own speech is sent anywhere (S-TH1, S-ST1); a sample with a guest (S-PC1,
529	S-LONG1) is sent only when the guest has agreed, and the spike's README records that.

531	- **FC-S1 — Sound Analysis as a signal (before FC3; verdict FC-30).** Question: on macOS 26.5.1,
532	  does `.version1` find laughter, applause and cheering in the owner's recordings well enough to
533	  steer the pool, how fast, and at which window? Inputs: the events sample S-EV (with the owner's
534	  written onset list), at least 10 minutes of speech only (S-TH1 and S-ST1 together), a talk over
535	  music (S-MU), and `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`. Runs: windows 1.0, 1.5 and 3.0 s at overlap 0.5,
536	  through `SNAudioFileAnalyzer` and through `SNAudioStreamAnalyzer` fed by `speechReader`.
537	  **Rule:**
538	  - A group is first-class when one threshold t ∈ {0.3, 0.4, …, 0.8}, chosen on the odd-numbered
539	    labelled events and applied unchanged to the even-numbered ones, finds at least 70 % of them
540	    (an onset within ±1 s) and calls at most one window per 10 minutes of the speech-only and
541	    music inputs that group. A group with fewer than 10 held-out (even-numbered) events is weak by
542	    rule, whatever its recall, so one cheer cannot decide a group.
543	  - The window kept is the one with the best laughter recall among those whose run is at least
544	    60× real time. A tie goes to 1.5 s. If no window reaches 60×, the slowest acceptable window is
545	    the one kept and the figure is recorded; the pass covers only played spans in any case
546	    (CJ-22's runs).
547	  - The stream analyzer is used if its event times agree with the file analyzer's within one hop.
548	    Otherwise the kind's version records which one ran and FC-31 is amended.
549	- **FC-S2 — The ranking's request shape and cost (at FC5's head; verdicts FC-50's constants,
550	  FC-51, FC-63).** Questions: (a) does the helper, configured with one app tool `submit_ranking`,
551	  no deferred tool and `fallbacks` off, send a request the API accepts; (b) does `countTokens` of
552	  the request text built from a transcript fit FC-62's estimate; (c) does `claude-opus-5-5` submit
553	  a valid ranking on its first call; (d) what does a run cost against the estimate; (e) does the
554	  ranker's `cancel` after a valid submission leave no further request? Inputs: S-TH1's transcript
555	  (the owner alone), S-ST1's when present, and two public-domain texts cut into timed sentences at
556	  2.6 words per second (their sources named in the spike's README); S-PC1 or S-LONG1 only with the
557	  guest's agreement. Runs: 10 in all at counts 10, 20 and 30, cap $3.00. **Rule:**
558	  - (a) passes if no request is refused. If the request with `TOOL_SEARCH` beside one non-deferred
559	    tool is refused, FC5's diff adds `search: false` (FC-51).
560	  - (b) passes if FC-S3's estimate lies within its recorded margin of `countTokens` on every
561	    input; otherwise FC-S3's constants are refitted on the union of both spikes' inputs.
562	  - (c) passes if at least 9 of 10 runs submit a valid ranking (FC-63's checks) on the first call
563	    and 10 of 10 within two. If it fails, FC5's diff instead adds a one-shot `rank` message using
564	    structured output (`output_config.format`), and FC6 is designed on that.
565	  - (d) passes if every run's priced cost lies within [`low`, `ceiling`] computed before it. The
566	    10th and 90th percentiles of output tokens per candidate become FC-50's `output_low` and
567	    `output_typical` per candidate.
568	  - (e) passes if each run's `cost` events number exactly its submissions.

570	  on-device rule, FC-62's constants, FC-45's accepted limit).** Questions: do this Mac's words end
571	  sentences often enough to cut at sentence ends; how fast is on-device recognition; how many

575	  - On-device sentence ends are usable if at least 80 % of AssemblyAI's sentence ends have an

1093	### Risks
1094	
1095	- **Ranking quality is the whole product.** A ranked list a creator does not trust is worse than
1096	  none. FC9's trial is the test, and prompt changes after it cost paid runs under the month's
1097	  budget.
1098	- **Sound Analysis may be weak on real podcasts.** Soft chuckles are hard to hear, music beds and
1099	  game audio confuse it, and the pre-spike reading already called speech `music` at 1 s windows.
1100	  FC-30 can demote a group to weak, and then only the words carry the ranking.
1101	- **Sentence edges on device.** If FC-S3 fails, edges come from pauses and are approximate without
1102	  a cloud transcript, and the window says so.
1103	- **Time on first run.** Recognising a two-hour episode on device takes minutes (TX-S1's and
1104	  FC-S3's figures), and a `find_clips` call holds the agent lane that long (FC-45). After that,
1105	  TR-14's cache and the analysis store make it fast.
1106	- **Cost and length.** An eight-hour VOD's transcript can pass FC-62's limit, and a model the
1107	  price table lacks cannot be priced in advance. Both are refused or said, never guessed. The
1108	  local token estimate can be wrong by more than FC-S3's margin on unusual text; the API's own
1109	  refusal is then the backstop, and its cost is recorded.
1110	- **Text leaves the Mac.** The transcript goes to Anthropic at Rank and only then. FC-64 says so
1111	  before the press, and a creator with a guest's recording may still need the guest's consent;
1112	  the guide says so.
1113	- **Classifier refusals.** A transcript about security or medicine can trip a safety classifier.
1114	  With fallbacks off (FC-51), the run ends with FC-61's sentence and its cost; the person can rank
1115	  part of the timeline.
1116	- **The helper is shared with Rasterize.** FC5's diff must land in both, or `agent/src` stops
1117	  being one file set. It is one issue, filed at FC5, and the root `CLAUDE.md`'s claim is updated.
1118	- **Range edges are CJ5's.** Transitions, ramps, timed caption pages, nests and linked pairs at an
1119	  edge are where `keep_range` can go wrong; N1 is the overlap case the first draft got wrong.
1120	  FC8a's proof rows are a second check from FC's side.
1121	- **Many documents.** Thirty shorts opened at once would approach the instance's forty-document
1122	  deadlock; FC-82 closes each after queueing, and N7 shows no window for it.
1123	- **Disk.** Each short carries every kept media's caches. On APFS a clone costs almost nothing
1124	  until written; on another volume (an exFAT external drive) it is a full copy per short. N6 and
1125	  FC8b measure it.
1126	- **Bet 3's interface.** FC9 needs VR3's step as a function applied to a document it did not
1127	  create (VR-30). If VR lands only a command that makes its own copy, FC9 makes two documents per
1128	  short until that is fixed.
1129	- **Consolidated media.** A source whose media sits inside its own package gives shorts that
1130	  point into that package; moving it means a relink. Media files are never copied (CJ-51).

520	### Spikes
521	
522	Each rule is fixed here and its text stored by SHA-256 before its run (CJ-7). A spike runs at the
523	head of the phase that needs it, and its verdict is recorded as the decision named. Paid runs are
524	behind `--live --cap`, held to P-6's ledger and the month's budget. An Anthropic request reads its
525	key only through `tools/proof/assistant_prompt_eval.py`'s `anthropic_key()` (:79). An AssemblyAI
526	request goes through `tools/proof/cloud_spike/`'s client, whose key is `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY`
527	(`aai.py`:32), supplied by the owner for that run, and through `cloud_live_ledger.py` with its cap.
528	Only the owner's own speech is sent anywhere (S-TH1, S-ST1); a sample with a guest (S-PC1,
529	S-LONG1) is sent only when the guest has agreed, and the spike's README records that.
530	
531	- **FC-S1 — Sound Analysis as a signal (before FC3; verdict FC-30).** Question: on macOS 26.5.1,
532	  does `.version1` find laughter, applause and cheering in the owner's recordings well enough to
533	  steer the pool, how fast, and at which window? Inputs: the events sample S-EV (with the owner's
534	  written onset list), at least 10 minutes of speech only (S-TH1 and S-ST1 together), a talk over
535	  music (S-MU), and `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`. Runs: windows 1.0, 1.5 and 3.0 s at overlap 0.5,
536	  through `SNAudioFileAnalyzer` and through `SNAudioStreamAnalyzer` fed by `speechReader`.
537	  **Rule:**
538	  - A group is first-class when one threshold t ∈ {0.3, 0.4, …, 0.8}, chosen on the odd-numbered
539	    labelled events and applied unchanged to the even-numbered ones, finds at least 70 % of them
540	    (an onset within ±1 s) and calls at most one window per 10 minutes of the speech-only and
541	    music inputs that group. A group with fewer than 10 held-out (even-numbered) events is weak by
542	    rule, whatever its recall, so one cheer cannot decide a group.
543	  - The window kept is the one with the best laughter recall among those whose run is at least
544	    60× real time. A tie goes to 1.5 s. If no window reaches 60×, the slowest acceptable window is
545	    the one kept and the figure is recorded; the pass covers only played spans in any case
546	    (CJ-22's runs).
547	  - The stream analyzer is used if its event times agree with the file analyzer's within one hop.
548	    Otherwise the kind's version records which one ran and FC-31 is amended.
549	- **FC-S2 — The ranking's request shape and cost (at FC5's head; verdicts FC-50's constants,
550	  FC-51, FC-63).** Questions: (a) does the helper, configured with one app tool `submit_ranking`,
551	  no deferred tool and `fallbacks` off, send a request the API accepts; (b) does `countTokens` of
552	  the request text built from a transcript fit FC-62's estimate; (c) does `claude-opus-5-5` submit
553	  a valid ranking on its first call; (d) what does a run cost against the estimate; (e) does the
554	  ranker's `cancel` after a valid submission leave no further request? Inputs: S-TH1's transcript
555	  (the owner alone), S-ST1's when present, and two public-domain texts cut into timed sentences at
556	  2.6 words per second (their sources named in the spike's README); S-PC1 or S-LONG1 only with the
557	  guest's agreement. Runs: 10 in all at counts 10, 20 and 30, cap $3.00. **Rule:**
558	  - (a) passes if no request is refused. If the request with `TOOL_SEARCH` beside one non-deferred
559	    tool is refused, FC5's diff adds `search: false` (FC-51).
560	  - (b) passes if FC-S3's estimate lies within its recorded margin of `countTokens` on every
561	    input; otherwise FC-S3's constants are refitted on the union of both spikes' inputs.
562	  - (c) passes if at least 9 of 10 runs submit a valid ranking (FC-63's checks) on the first call
563	    and 10 of 10 within two. If it fails, FC5's diff instead adds a one-shot `rank` message using
564	    structured output (`output_config.format`), and FC6 is designed on that.
565	  - (d) passes if every run's priced cost lies within [`low`, `ceiling`] computed before it. The
566	    10th and 90th percentiles of output tokens per candidate become FC-50's `output_low` and
567	    `output_typical` per candidate.
568	  - (e) passes if each run's `cost` events number exactly its submissions.
569	- **FC-S3 — Sentence ends, recognition speed and transcript size (before FC4; verdicts FC-41's
570	  on-device rule, FC-62's constants, FC-45's accepted limit).** Questions: do this Mac's words end
571	  sentences often enough to cut at sentence ends; how fast is on-device recognition; how many
572	  tokens does a transcript cost? Inputs: S-TH1 (and S-ST1 when present), transcribed on device and
573	  once by AssemblyAI (one request per file, at most $0.50 in all, with `disfluencies` and
574	  speakers; S-TH1's also becomes FC8a's filler fixture). **Rule:**
575	  - On-device sentence ends are usable if at least 80 % of AssemblyAI's sentence ends have an
576	    on-device sentence end (FC-41) within 0.5 s, and the two sentence counts are within 30 % of
577	    each other.
578	  - **Otherwise** FC-41's on-device arm drops punctuation and ends a sentence at a word followed
579	    by a non-speech run of at least 0.6 s on `MediaSpeech`'s 32 ms grid (probability below
580	    `defaultVoiceConfidence`), or at a change of track where two voice clips play at once. The
581	    spike runs that rule against AssemblyAI's ends too and records its agreement. With either
582	    rule in force, the Find Clips window and `find_clips`' `notes` say "Edges are approximate
583	    without a cloud transcript." when the scope has on-device words.
584	  - The on-device recognition speed (seconds of speech per second, cold and from TR-14's cache)
585	    is recorded as FC-45's accepted figure, beside TX-S1's.
586	  - FC-62's `fixed`, `per_word` and `per_sentence` are fitted by `countTokens` (free) over request
587	    texts built from the transcripts, the largest residual recorded as the margin. The model
588	    window `max_input_tokens` of `claude-opus-5-5` is recorded with them.

1093	### Risks
1094	
1095	- **Ranking quality is the whole product.** A ranked list a creator does not trust is worse than
1096	  none. FC9's trial is the test, and prompt changes after it cost paid runs under the month's
1097	  budget.
1098	- **Sound Analysis may be weak on real podcasts.** Soft chuckles are hard to hear, music beds and
1099	  game audio confuse it, and the pre-spike reading already called speech `music` at 1 s windows.
1100	  FC-30 can demote a group to weak, and then only the words carry the ranking.
1101	- **Sentence edges on device.** If FC-S3 fails, edges come from pauses and are approximate without
1102	  a cloud transcript, and the window says so.
1103	- **Time on first run.** Recognising a two-hour episode on device takes minutes (TX-S1's and
1104	  FC-S3's figures), and a `find_clips` call holds the agent lane that long (FC-45). After that,
1105	  TR-14's cache and the analysis store make it fast.
1106	- **Cost and length.** An eight-hour VOD's transcript can pass FC-62's limit, and a model the
1107	  price table lacks cannot be priced in advance. Both are refused or said, never guessed. The
1108	  local token estimate can be wrong by more than FC-S3's margin on unusual text; the API's own
1109	  refusal is then the backstop, and its cost is recorded.
1110	- **Text leaves the Mac.** The transcript goes to Anthropic at Rank and only then. FC-64 says so
1111	  before the press, and a creator with a guest's recording may still need the guest's consent;
1112	  the guide says so.
1113	- **Classifier refusals.** A transcript about security or medicine can trip a safety classifier.
1114	  With fallbacks off (FC-51), the run ends with FC-61's sentence and its cost; the person can rank
1115	  part of the timeline.
1116	- **The helper is shared with Rasterize.** FC5's diff must land in both, or `agent/src` stops
1117	  being one file set. It is one issue, filed at FC5, and the root `CLAUDE.md`'s claim is updated.
1118	- **Range edges are CJ5's.** Transitions, ramps, timed caption pages, nests and linked pairs at an
1119	  edge are where `keep_range` can go wrong; N1 is the overlap case the first draft got wrong.
1120	  FC8a's proof rows are a second check from FC's side.
1121	- **Many documents.** Thirty shorts opened at once would approach the instance's forty-document
1122	  deadlock; FC-82 closes each after queueing, and N7 shows no window for it.
1123	- **Disk.** Each short carries every kept media's caches. On APFS a clone costs almost nothing
1124	  until written; on another volume (an exFAT external drive) it is a full copy per short. N6 and
1125	  FC8b measure it.
1126	- **Bet 3's interface.** FC9 needs VR3's step as a function applied to a document it did not
1127	  create (VR-30). If VR lands only a command that makes its own copy, FC9 makes two documents per
1128	  short until that is fixed.
1129	- **Consolidated media.** A source whose media sits inside its own package gives shorts that
1130	  point into that package; moving it means a relink. Media files are never copied (CJ-51).

1	## Bet 5 — Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file
2	
3	### Goal
4	
5	A creator records a video podcast or an interview with two to four cameras and a microphone per
6	person. They line the files up with Synchronize Audio, select them, and choose Clip ▸ Switch by
7	Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking. It judges each microphone's speech against that
8	microphone's own level, so a guest's voice leaking into the host's microphone does not cut to
9	the host. It shows the wide shot while two people talk over each other, holds a minimum shot
10	length, and lets short replies ("yeah", "mm") pass without a cut. The result is one undo step:
11	a new Program track of ordinary clips, each a piece of one camera, in front of the cameras,
12	which stay whole and hidden on their own tracks. The microphones are not touched. Every cut can
13	be rolled like any other cut, and Clip ▸ Switch Angle re-picks the camera for one shot. Later
14	phases add a one-microphone mode that reads mouth opening from CJ3's face tracks, and an Angle
15	Viewer that shows every camera at once and switches while the timeline plays.
16	
17	Separately, Frame Job stops reading only the first audio track of a file. An OBS recording with
18	the mix on track 1, the microphone on track 2 and the desktop on track 3 imports all three. A
19	recorder or mixer file with many channels in one track (a RØDECaster Pro II, a Zoom F-series,
20	a MixPre) offers each channel as its own source, and so does a wireless kit that records two
21	people on the left and right of one stereo track. Each track or channel can be placed as its own
22	clip with its own audio chain, and Detach Audio makes one linked sound clip per track. Every
23	measurement — the waveform, loudness, Normalize, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech, Remove Silences,
24	Synchronize Audio, transcription — reads the track or channel the clip plays.
25	
26	Every command has its MCP tool. No phase needs a key.
27	
28	### Owner's answers applied
29	
30	- **All six bets are in one road map.** This is bet 5, prefix SW; its phases are SW0–SW9b.
31	- **Every spec §1 non-goal is lifted.** For this bet that means multicam. The bet builds
32	  multicam in full: synced angles, a program track of shots, re-picking, an Angle Viewer and
33	  switching while playing (SW1, SW2a–SW2b, SW9a, SW9b). It does this without a multicam source
34	  kind: the shots are ordinary clips on an ordinary track (SW-10, SW-90). That is a design
35	  choice, not a non-goal; the owner can ask for a multicam clip instead at SW9a.
36	- **§11 decisions that implement a non-goal stand until a phase amends them in writing.** This
37	  bet amends none of them. Nest clips keep having no in point (`core/src/nest.rs:22`), there is
38	  still one kind of track (spec §2), and the effect vocabulary stays closed (R5-1). It does amend
39	  one §11 rule that is not a non-goal: the foundations rule that `async`/`await` lives only in
40	  `MediaImporter` gains one more named file (SW-43), as W-8 added `SpeechEngine.swift`.
41	- **Input Monitoring.** Not used by this bet.
42	- **The key rule.** Nothing in this bet uses a language model or a cloud model. Switch by
43	  Speaker reads the loudness cache, Silero VAD's speech cache and, in SW8, CJ3's `faces` kind
44	  (Vision face landmarks) — all on the device, none needing a key. The Assistant can call the
45	  bet's tools on its own key, as it calls every tool. Transcribing a second audio track with
46	  AssemblyAI needs the AssemblyAI key exactly as transcribing the first does today (CJ-3).
47	- **Lead segments and lanes.** Reading every audio track serves the first segment as well as
48	  podcasts: screen recordists who record with OBS keep their microphone on its own track. So the
49	  audio-track phases run in lane A, after TX's transcript phases and before FC's; the switch
50	  phases run last in lane C, as CJ-2 orders video podcasts last. Lane A has the room: FC's Make
51	  Short phase waits on lane C's CJ5 and VR's version maker either way. This is an amendment to
52	  CJ-2's lane plan, recorded before any SW code (draft below, under "Decisions"). No fourth lane
53	  is added.
54	- **Real use.** The owner cuts one real video per lead segment alongside bet 1 (CJ-5). For
55	  podcasts, JOB-51 asks the owner to cut one real episode with Switch by Speaker once SW2b lands;
56	  the verdict is recorded as SW-29, the way GR-9 recorded grading's trial.
57	- **Survey decision 8** (the multi-stream 4K and multi-hour measurement) is asked at CJ0
58	  (question 4). SW0 runs it as this bet's first spike, SW-S2, and only after the owner's yes
59	  (SW-2).
60	- **Build arrangement.** Every format number below is provisional ("format 38p") until its
61	  phase lands; the integrator renumbers on collision. Decision IDs are SW-n0…SW-n9 per phase
62	  (SW0's are SW-1…SW-9); scope-level drafts are offered to CJ0 for numbering.
63	
64	### How it fits the tree
65	
66	At `d0661e5d`. Line counts are `wc -l`.
67	
68	**A media is one file with one sound.**

70	  nothing about how many audio tracks or channels the file has. Its `speech` spans
71	  (format 29, AU-110) belong to the file as a whole.

73	  the doc above it: "two entries for one path would each carry their own bookmark, thumbnails

77	  precedent for a fact about what a clip reads that changes neither the plan's structure nor

79	  but the literals in `add_clip` (`edit_clip.rs:203`) and `set_reversed` (`:602`), and the
80	  exhaustive destructuring at `:589`, must name a new field.

84	  (`app/Sources/MediaImporter.swift:79`, `hasAudio: !audioTracks.isEmpty` at :114). It tests

127	  (`AudioSync.swift:240–273`, features, samples and speech by media) all read through media ids.
128	- `ProjectDocument.generateCaches()` (`ProjectDocument.swift:818–825`) runs at open, import,

1351	### Risks
1352	
1353	- **AVFoundation and many channels.** What the tap and the export's mix see for a stream of more
1354	  than two channels is unmeasured; SW-S1 decides between the tap and a copy, and the copy costs
1355	  temporary disk (about 0.5 GB an hour per channel at 24-bit mono) and render time.
1356	- **Cuts between long-GOP 4K files on one composition track may hitch.** SW-S2 (a) measures it;
1357	  the fix is SW2c's plan change.
1358	- **Rebuild time with a thousand shots** is unmeasured (SW-S2 (b)); the owner's order puts
1359	  performance work after features, so a shortfall becomes a recorded limit and an issue.
1360	- **SW-S2 is costly.** About 34 GB and up to an hour of encoding, and a three-hour file twice
1361	  that; SW-2 runs it only after the owner's yes, and (d) only on S-LONG1 or behind its own flag.
1362	- **Bleed and loud laughter.** One margin will not suit every room; SW-S4 sets the defaults on
1363	  owner-confirmed turns and the sheet exposes the margin.
1364	- **Sync.** The switch trusts the placement. A slipped or moved shot falls out of sync with the
1365	  microphones like any synced clip; the guide says so.
1366	- **`MAX_CLIPS`.** A three-hour show at a two-second minimum can pass 4,096; the switch refuses
1367	  first and says what to raise, reading the ceiling CJ-9 leaves.
1368	- **Hidden angles still sound.** Camera scratch audio doubles the microphones unless muted; the
1369	  switch mutes non-microphone angles by default, and SW-20 never takes a camera's sound as a
1370	  microphone beside picture-less microphone files.
1371	- **Older media.** A media imported before SW3a has no `audio_streams`; its other tracks and its
1372	  channels are reached only after a relink to the same file (SW-30).
1373	- **Cache volume.** Per-source caches multiply the sync features (23 MB an hour each) and speech
1374	  files; SW-41 makes only the sources clips play.
1375	- **Link groups change a format-28 field and every link rule**, through the link readers in
1376	  twelve core files (SW7a's Core bullet lists them). AP9's proof re-runs whole; one mutant per
1377	  rule.
1378	- **Stream order.** If AVFoundation's order differs from the container's (SW-S1 (a)), track names

480	
481	Each rule is fixed here and hashed before its run (CJ-7): instruments land under
482	`tools/proof/cutout_spike/`, next to the E9 instruments they extend, and each run's
483	`results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `designs/creator-jobs.md` as `rule_sha256`. Each runs on the

487	- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate and read size.**
488	  Question: which Vision request, rate and read size give the best outline per second of analysis
489	  on talking-head footage, and does a portrait source read upright (CJ-23's display orientation)
490	  cut as well as a landscape one?
491	  Candidates: person `.balanced`, person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with
492	  `generateScaledMaskForImage`; each at every source frame (capped at 30 masks a second of
493	  source), at 15 and at 10 a second; frames read at the source's size and at a long side of 1920.
494	  Truth: S-KEY1's keyed composites ("Samples and fixtures").
495	  Measured on every truth frame against the mask the compositor would show there (CO-3's
496	  nearest-hold rule, so a capped rate's lag counts):
497	  J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5;
498	  B = mean |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge, at 1080p;
499	  B on the gesture segment;
500	  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment;
501	  realtime factor = source seconds per wall second for read, Vision and mask write together, at
502	  1080p30 and 4K30, pinned to the Neural Engine.
503	  Also: S-KEY1's composite re-tagged with a 90° rotation matrix (a portrait source with truth),
504	  and the first Vision call of a fresh process (E9's compile cost, recorded with no rule).
505	  **Rule.**
506	  (a) A candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is out.
507	  (b) The rate is every frame, unless B on the gesture segment at 15 a second is within 5 % of B
508	  at every frame (then 15), and again at 10 a second within 5 % (then 10).
509	  (c) **Standard** is the fastest remaining candidate that runs at least 1.0× realtime at 1080p30
510	  at that rate and whose J is within 0.02 of the best J. If none reaches 1.0×, the rate steps
511	  down (every frame → 15 → 10) and (c) is applied again. If none reaches 1.0× at 10 a second,
512	  Standard is the fastest candidate within 0.02 J at 10 a second, and its realtime factor is
513	  recorded as a risk in the road map.
514	  (d) **Best** is the candidate with the lowest B, kept only if its B is at least 15 % below
515	  Standard's and it runs at least 0.25× realtime. Otherwise there is no Best, and no Quality
516	  control is built.
517	  (e) The read size is a long side of 1920 for a larger source when J and B there are within
518	  0.005 and 2 % of the source size's; otherwise the source size.
519	  (f) The rotated composite's J is within 0.01 of the unrotated composite's. If not, STOP: CJ-23
520	  is amended before CO1 to read coded frames and pass the orientation to Vision.
521	  If S-KEY1 has not arrived by CO0, (c) runs for speed alone on the E9 fixtures and S-TH1 if
522	  present, Standard is person `.balanced` at the fastest rate (every frame, 15, 10) that reaches
523	  1.0× realtime (E9 chose `.balanced` at 10 masks a second), and (b), (d), (e) and (f) run when
524	  S-KEY1 arrives, before CO4.
525	
526	- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.**
527	  Question: does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact,
528	  small and cheap enough to build and play?
529	  Instrument: a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through `tools/proof/swift_build.py` (the mask
530	  track and `texture(4)` do not exist before CO2a). For each edit below it takes the core's plan
531	  of a project built through the FFI, adds by hand a mask track whose segments copy the picture
532	  segments, fills both through `CompositionBuilder.fill`, and reads every frame through a probe
533	  compositor — a subclass of the compositor class the project would use — that fetches both
534	  tracks' buffers per request. Frame counts come from the probe's own `AVPlayer` over the same
535	  composition.
536	  Fixture: a synthetic movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and mask chunks written
537	  from it with chunk-relative times by CO-3's nearest-hold rule; a bar code reads back which mask
538	  frame arrived with which picture frame.
539	  Tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy; chunk lengths
540	  5, 10 and 30 s.
541	  **Rule.** The mask track (CO-3) is kept when all six hold:
542	  (1) **Registration.** Every frame shows the mask of the nearest analysed source frame (ties to
543	  the earlier in the stream its segment reads), at every-frame analysis and at 15 a second, across:
544	  a trim; ×0.5; ×2; ×1.37 with a chunk boundary inside the segment; a speed ramp that crosses a
545	  chunk boundary; a freeze frame; a reversed clip (its mirrored chunks, CO-4 (e)); a split; a clip
546	  inside a nest; a cross-dissolve; and an HLG variable-frame-rate source (S-TH1 when present, an
547	  `ffmpeg`-made HLG VFR fixture otherwise).
548	  (2) **Colour path.** The value the probe compositor reads differs from the DECODED mask by at
549	  most 1/255 at every pixel, in an SDR and an HLG composition, under the compositor class each
550	  would be built with. If the plain class conforms the mask, a composition with a mask track is
551	  built with `ConvertingCompositor` and (2) is measured again under it.
552	  (3) **Codec loss.** The decoded masks' IoU against Vision's own masks (both > 0.5) is at least
553	  0.995, and their mean |difference| inside the 8 px edge band at most 3 levels.
554	  (4) **Size.** At most 15 MB per minute of 30 fps source at Standard.
555	  (5) **Playback.** A 1080p30 camera with its mask track over a 4K screen recording composes, over
556	  20 s that cross at least five chunk boundaries, at least 99 % of the frames it composes without
557	  the mask track.
558	  (6) **Build.** `CompositionBuilder.build` of a 60-minute camera cut into 120 clips, every one cut
559	  out, takes at most 100 ms more (median of 10) than the same build without mask tracks.
560	  The chunk length L is the shortest of 5, 10 and 30 s that passes (5) and (6) and whose
561	  per-chunk fixed cost (the writer session, the file) adds under 5 % to analysis time per minute;
562	  the encoding is the smaller of the two that pass. Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured
563	  on (1), (2), (5) and (6) and kept if it passes. If neither passes, CO stops after CO1 and the
564	  owner is asked.
565	
566	- **CO-S3 — Whether the edge needs refinement, and which** (at CO0 when S-KEY1 exists, else at
567	  CO4's start).
568	  Question: how much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512×384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and
569	  4K, and what does it cost per frame?
570	  Candidates:
571	  r0, bilinear sampling and a smoothstep remap (the edge and feather controls);
572	  r1, a joint bilateral upsample inside the layer stage (3×3 mask texels weighted by the picture's
573	  colour distance, read as `KeyReading` reads);
574	  r2, a guided filter in a pass before the destination, at twice the mask's size.
575	  Instrument: a standalone Metal probe over S-KEY1's frames and their masks.
576	  Measured: B (as in CO-S1) on S-KEY1's composites, and cost per frame, full-frame, at 1080p and
577	  4K (200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of medians — MT0's method).
578	  **Rule.** The cheapest candidate whose B is at most 1.1 × the lowest B ships, provided it costs
579	  at most 1.0 ms at 1080p and 3.0 ms at 4K above r0. If r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0
580	  ships and the better one is filed with its numbers.
581	
582	- **CO-S4 — The analysis beside playback.**
583	  Question: does mask analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames?
584	  Instrument: CO-S1's instrument as a SEPARATE process under `taskpolicy -c utility`, analysing
585	  S-TH1 (or the E9 push-in) at Standard on the Neural Engine, while the Release app's
586	  `play_preview` plays a 1080p30 project for 20 s. The app's own lane does not exist yet; the
587	  Neural Engine and the decoders are shared system-wide, which is what is measured.

589	  **Rule.** If the median composed count falls by more than 2 %, `AnalysisLane` pauses while any
590	  transport plays and resumes when none does (CO-9, amending CJ-21); otherwise it runs throughout.

1217	### Risks
1218	
1219	- **Edges.** Balanced masks are 512×384 stretched over the frame; hair and fast hands may look cut
1220	  with scissors. CO-S3 bounds what refinement buys and JOB-60 is the owner's verdict. If it is
1221	  "not good enough", the remedy is a matting-model candidate (CO-1), which must carry a licence
1222	  an Apache-2.0 app can ship.
1223	- **Vision misses** backlit, from-behind and small figures (E9 §5b). The status says "No person
1224	  found" for a window; a partial miss mid-clip shows as a missing arm.
1225	- **Analysis time.** At every frame, Standard may run near or below 1× realtime; CO-S1 (c) steps
1226	  the rate down to keep 1×, and if even 10 a second misses it the figure is recorded as a risk. An
1227	  hour of camera is then about an hour of background work. Chunks limit it to the windows clips
1228	  use.
1229	- **Cache size.** CO-S2 bounds Standard at 15 MB per minute; Best may be several times that.
1230	- **The mask track's colour.** A composition must not colour-manage a mask frame. CO-S2 (2)
1231	  measures it per compositor class; a failure moves CO-3 to the fallback.
1232	- **Decoders and builds.** Each cut-out instance adds a decode, and each chunk an asset per build.
1233	  The eight-decoder warning counts mask tracks; CO-S2 (5) and (6) bound playback and build cost
1234	  and choose the chunk length.
1235	- **Masks differ across Macs.** GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels. A package carries its
1236	  masks; a Mac that regenerates them may draw a slightly different edge. Proofs compare against
1237	  cached masks.
1238	- **The uniform block.** CO-8's size depends on whether CU's group lands first; the integrator
1239	  renumbers it with the proofs' pins.
1240	- **Layouts against existing placement.** A switch replaces the base placement of every role clip
1241	  starting before the next layout action; a camera placed by hand there is overwritten unless
1242	  `through` bounds the reach (the landing always passes it). Zooms and moving actions are refused
1243	  and nested (CO-62); a nested screen loses rounded corners, because a nest clip's radius reaches
1244	  no layer (`nest.rs:382`). A layout action deleted at a clip's head leaves its base and loses its
1245	  marker, so an earlier switch can then reach over it.
1246	- **Bet interactions.** Bet 1's cuts split every unlocked track; a split's second half takes the
1247	  evaluated layout as its base, so a switch holds across cuts. Bet 1 shows words inside a nest as
1248	  not editable, and CO-62 may nest picture clips; it never nests the microphone. Bet 2's cursor
1249	  rides in the screen clip's layer (CU-4), so it moves with the screen and its nest. CU's Auto Zoom
1250	  on a screen in `side_by_side` solves its regions against the whole canvas, not the box; the
1251	  remedy is the same nest. Bet 3's vertical version should use `stacked` for screen-and-camera
1252	  pairs rather than reframing each clip.
1253	- **API drift.** If Apple deprecates the `VN*` segmentation classes in favour of the `async`-only
1254	  Swift API (as `NSCursor.currentSystem` was deprecated), the analyser needs the `async`
1255	  confinement W-8 allows, in `MediaImporter.swift` or a decision that widens it.
1256	- **Licences.** Concat, Cap and OpenScreen code, shaders and models are not opened or carried over.
