487	- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate and read size.**
488	  Question: which Vision request, rate and read size give the best outline per second of analysis
489	  on talking-head footage, and does a portrait source read upright (CJ-23's display orientation)
490	  cut as well as a landscape one?
491	  Candidates: person `.balanced`, person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with
492	  `generateScaledMaskForImage`; each at every source frame (capped at 30 masks a second of
493	  source), at 15 and at 10 a second; frames read at the source's size and at a long side of 1920.
494	  Truth: S-KEY1's keyed composites ("Samples and fixtures").
495	  Measured on every truth frame against the mask the compositor would show there (CO-3's
496	  nearest-hold rule, so a capped rate's lag counts):
497	  J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5;
498	  B = mean |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge, at 1080p;
499	  B on the gesture segment;
500	  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment;
501	  realtime factor = source seconds per wall second for read, Vision and mask write together, at
502	  1080p30 and 4K30, pinned to the Neural Engine.
503	  Also: S-KEY1's composite re-tagged with a 90° rotation matrix (a portrait source with truth),
504	  and the first Vision call of a fresh process (E9's compile cost, recorded with no rule).
505	  **Rule.**
506	  (a) A candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is out.
507	  (b) The rate is every frame, unless B on the gesture segment at 15 a second is within 5 % of B
508	  at every frame (then 15), and again at 10 a second within 5 % (then 10).
509	  (c) **Standard** is the fastest remaining candidate that runs at least 1.0× realtime at 1080p30
510	  at that rate and whose J is within 0.02 of the best J. If none reaches 1.0×, the rate steps
511	  down (every frame → 15 → 10) and (c) is applied again. If none reaches 1.0× at 10 a second,
512	  Standard is the fastest candidate within 0.02 J at 10 a second, and its realtime factor is
513	  recorded as a risk in the road map.
514	  (d) **Best** is the candidate with the lowest B, kept only if its B is at least 15 % below
515	  Standard's and it runs at least 0.25× realtime. Otherwise there is no Best, and no Quality
516	  control is built.
517	  (e) The read size is a long side of 1920 for a larger source when J and B there are within
518	  0.005 and 2 % of the source size's; otherwise the source size.
519	  (f) The rotated composite's J is within 0.01 of the unrotated composite's. If not, STOP: CJ-23
520	  is amended before CO1 to read coded frames and pass the orientation to Vision.
521	  If S-KEY1 has not arrived by CO0, (c) runs for speed alone on the E9 fixtures and S-TH1 if
522	  present, Standard is person `.balanced` at the fastest rate (every frame, 15, 10) that reaches
523	  1.0× realtime (E9 chose `.balanced` at 10 masks a second), and (b), (d), (e) and (f) run when
524	  S-KEY1 arrives, before CO4.
525	
526	- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.**
527	  Question: does a mask movie inserted as a second composition track arrive registered, exact,
528	  small and cheap enough to build and play?
529	  Instrument: a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through `tools/proof/swift_build.py` (the mask
530	  track and `texture(4)` do not exist before CO2a). For each edit below it takes the core's plan
531	  of a project built through the FFI, adds by hand a mask track whose segments copy the picture
532	  segments, fills both through `CompositionBuilder.fill`, and reads every frame through a probe
533	  compositor — a subclass of the compositor class the project would use — that fetches both
534	  tracks' buffers per request. Frame counts come from the probe's own `AVPlayer` over the same
535	  composition.
536	  Fixture: a synthetic movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and mask chunks written
537	  from it with chunk-relative times by CO-3's nearest-hold rule; a bar code reads back which mask
538	  frame arrived with which picture frame.
539	  Tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy; chunk lengths
540	  5, 10 and 30 s.
541	  **Rule.** The mask track (CO-3) is kept when all six hold:
542	  (1) **Registration.** Every frame shows the mask of the nearest analysed source frame (ties to
543	  the earlier in the stream its segment reads), at every-frame analysis and at 15 a second, across:
544	  a trim; ×0.5; ×2; ×1.37 with a chunk boundary inside the segment; a speed ramp that crosses a
545	  chunk boundary; a freeze frame; a reversed clip (its mirrored chunks, CO-4 (e)); a split; a clip
546	  inside a nest; a cross-dissolve; and an HLG variable-frame-rate source (S-TH1 when present, an
547	  `ffmpeg`-made HLG VFR fixture otherwise).
548	  (2) **Colour path.** The value the probe compositor reads differs from the DECODED mask by at
549	  most 1/255 at every pixel, in an SDR and an HLG composition, under the compositor class each
550	  would be built with. If the plain class conforms the mask, a composition with a mask track is
551	  built with `ConvertingCompositor` and (2) is measured again under it.
552	  (3) **Codec loss.** The decoded masks' IoU against Vision's own masks (both > 0.5) is at least
553	  0.995, and their mean |difference| inside the 8 px edge band at most 3 levels.
554	  (4) **Size.** At most 15 MB per minute of 30 fps source at Standard.
555	  (5) **Playback.** A 1080p30 camera with its mask track over a 4K screen recording composes, over
556	  20 s that cross at least five chunk boundaries, at least 99 % of the frames it composes without
557	  the mask track.
558	  (6) **Build.** `CompositionBuilder.build` of a 60-minute camera cut into 120 clips, every one cut
559	  out, takes at most 100 ms more (median of 10) than the same build without mask tracks.
560	  The chunk length L is the shortest of 5, 10 and 30 s that passes (5) and (6) and whose
561	  per-chunk fixed cost (the writer session, the file) adds under 5 % to analysis time per minute;
562	  the encoding is the smaller of the two that pass. Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured
563	  on (1), (2), (5) and (6) and kept if it passes. If neither passes, CO stops after CO1 and the
564	  owner is asked.
565	
566	- **CO-S3 — Whether the edge needs refinement, and which** (at CO0 when S-KEY1 exists, else at
567	  CO4's start).
568	  Question: how much does an edge-aware upsample of a 512×384 mask improve the outline at 1080p and
569	  4K, and what does it cost per frame?
570	  Candidates:
571	  r0, bilinear sampling and a smoothstep remap (the edge and feather controls);
572	  r1, a joint bilateral upsample inside the layer stage (3×3 mask texels weighted by the picture's
573	  colour distance, read as `KeyReading` reads);
574	  r2, a guided filter in a pass before the destination, at twice the mask's size.
575	  Instrument: a standalone Metal probe over S-KEY1's frames and their masks.
576	  Measured: B (as in CO-S1) on S-KEY1's composites, and cost per frame, full-frame, at 1080p and
577	  4K (200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, the median of medians — MT0's method).
578	  **Rule.** The cheapest candidate whose B is at most 1.1 × the lowest B ships, provided it costs
579	  at most 1.0 ms at 1080p and 3.0 ms at 4K above r0. If r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0
580	  ships and the better one is filed with its numbers.

582	- **CO-S4 — The analysis beside playback.**
583	  Question: does mask analysis at utility QoS drop preview frames?
584	  Instrument: CO-S1's instrument as a SEPARATE process under `taskpolicy -c utility`, analysing
585	  S-TH1 (or the E9 push-in) at Standard on the Neural Engine, while the Release app's
586	  `play_preview` plays a 1080p30 project for 20 s. The app's own lane does not exist yet; the
587	  Neural Engine and the decoders are shared system-wide, which is what is measured.

589	  **Rule.** If the median composed count falls by more than 2 %, `AnalysisLane` pauses while any
590	  transport plays and resumes when none does (CO-9, amending CJ-21); otherwise it runs throughout.

1218	
1219	- **Edges.** Balanced masks are 512×384 stretched over the frame; hair and fast hands may look cut
1220	  with scissors. CO-S3 bounds what refinement buys and JOB-60 is the owner's verdict. If it is
1221	  "not good enough", the remedy is a matting-model candidate (CO-1), which must carry a licence
1222	  an Apache-2.0 app can ship.
1223	- **Vision misses** backlit, from-behind and small figures (E9 §5b). The status says "No person
1224	  found" for a window; a partial miss mid-clip shows as a missing arm.
1225	- **Analysis time.** At every frame, Standard may run near or below 1× realtime; CO-S1 (c) steps
1226	  the rate down to keep 1×, and if even 10 a second misses it the figure is recorded as a risk. An
1227	  hour of camera is then about an hour of background work. Chunks limit it to the windows clips
1228	  use.
1229	- **Cache size.** CO-S2 bounds Standard at 15 MB per minute; Best may be several times that.
1230	- **The mask track's colour.** A composition must not colour-manage a mask frame. CO-S2 (2)
1231	  measures it per compositor class; a failure moves CO-3 to the fallback.
1232	- **Decoders and builds.** Each cut-out instance adds a decode, and each chunk an asset per build.
1233	  The eight-decoder warning counts mask tracks; CO-S2 (5) and (6) bound playback and build cost
1234	  and choose the chunk length.
1235	- **Masks differ across Macs.** GPU and ANE differ by up to 25 levels. A package carries its
1236	  masks; a Mac that regenerates them may draw a slightly different edge. Proofs compare against
1237	  cached masks.
1238	- **The uniform block.** CO-8's size depends on whether CU's group lands first; the integrator
1239	  renumbers it with the proofs' pins.
1240	- **Layouts against existing placement.** A switch replaces the base placement of every role clip
1241	  starting before the next layout action; a camera placed by hand there is overwritten unless
1242	  `through` bounds the reach (the landing always passes it). Zooms and moving actions are refused
1243	  and nested (CO-62); a nested screen loses rounded corners, because a nest clip's radius reaches
1244	  no layer (`nest.rs:382`). A layout action deleted at a clip's head leaves its base and loses its
1245	  marker, so an earlier switch can then reach over it.

1247	  evaluated layout as its base, so a switch holds across cuts. Bet 1 shows words inside a nest as
1248	  not editable, and CO-62 may nest picture clips; it never nests the microphone. Bet 2's cursor

# Road map "creator-jobs" — the jobs that send creators elsewhere

**Not opened yet.** CJ0a opens it: it records the owner's answers below as CJ-1…CJ-9 with the
bets' scope-level decisions, rewrites spec §1 and §2, and makes the two spec splits. The brief is
`designs/creator-survey.md`: its "The bets" (lines 173–356) and the market sections they cite. The
planned worktree is `.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs`, branch `worktree-creator-jobs`, cut from main
when CJ0a starts. Decisions go in a new `designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` (one series,
continued in `creator-jobs-2.md` past about 500 lines), each with its row in
`11-decisions/README.md` and that file's Lines cell. This file holds the plan and, as phases land,
each phase's record. Line counts and line numbers are `wc -l` and `grep -n` at `d0661e5d` (main,
2026-11-01); a phase re-reads them at its start.

## Goal

Frame Job finishes video better than most creator tools: its audio chain, colour and HDR, codecs
and an MCP surface over the whole editor (survey, "What Frame Job has"). It loses creators earlier,
at six jobs that now define a creator editor. After this road map each is a command that runs on
the Mac, lands as ordinary undo steps on a real timeline, and has an MCP tool that runs the same
planner:

1. **The Transcript tab (TX).** The timeline read as words, in timeline order. Selected words are
   deleted on every unlocked track as one step; cut words stay greyed and come back with Restore
   Words. A review pass strikes long pauses, fillers (where an AssemblyAI transcript exists),
   retakes, restarts and repeats, for the person to keep or remove in one step.
2. **Screen recordings with the cursor as data (CU).** The recorder saves the cursor's path,
   images, clicks, scrolls and (opt-in) shortcuts beside the movie, and the editor draws the
   cursor as part of the screen clip's layer. Auto Zoom, shortcut overlays, sped-up typing and
   motion blur follow, each as ordinary actions and clips, and the recorder can run them on
   landing.
3. **Make Vertical Version (VR).** A 9:16 or 1:1 copy of a finished edit, each picture following
   the face, person or salient region Vision found on the Mac (the cursor in a recording made
   after CU, the speaker in a two-shot after SW), as eased x, y and scale actions; captions
   re-paged and graphics re-laid. Linked versions in one project are designed and asked.
4. **Find Clips (FC).** A long recording analysed on the Mac (sentences, speakers, loudness,
   laughter, applause, cheering), ranked by Claude on the person's key with a stated reason per
   moment and no score, and made into saved, captioned, vertical shorts on the Export Queue.
5. **Switch by Speaker, and every audio track (SW).** A program track of shots cut to whoever is
   speaking, judged on each microphone against its own level; Switch Angle; an Angle Viewer and
   switching while playing; a one-microphone mode from faces. Every audio track and channel of a
   file played, measured and transcribed.
6. **Camera cutout and layouts (CO).** Remove Background on a camera clip from Vision's person
   masks, Text Behind Subject, camera layouts switched at the playhead (corner, side by side,
   stacked, camera full, screen only), the same at record time, and the camera hidden while
   silent.

The shared phases (CJ) give a person two things directly — every command that would send to
Claude or AssemblyAI greyed without its key, with a tooltip saying which key and where; and Clip ▸
Split at Shot Changes and File ▸ New Project from Range… — and give the bets one key gate, one
analysis lane, store, reader and sheet, a decided clip ceiling, and the files at the cap cut once
before three lanes reach for them.

## What it delivers first

The lead segment is people who record themselves talking: talking-head YouTube and screen
tutorials (TX, CU, CO). Repurposing to shorts comes next (VR, FC), then video podcasts (SW).

- **The baseline.** When TX1 starts, the owner cuts T1 (a talking head, sample S-TH1) and T2 (a
  screen tutorial, S-ST1) in that day's build, to a state they would publish, and records every
  point where they left Frame Job or gave up (CJ-5).
- **The checkpoint, after TX3.** The owner reads T1 as text in the Transcript tab, follows it while
  it plays, clicks a word to seek, selects words and presses ⌫ to cut them on every unlocked track
  as one step "Delete Words". They cut T1 again this way; the verdict is recorded before TX4
  starts, and lane A builds CJ5a meanwhile.
- **Then the rest of the tab.** TX5 greys cut words and restores them; TX6 and TX7 strike pauses,
  fillers and retakes for review. TX8 is the trial's closing run.
- **Beside it, lane B (T2's kind of video).** Every screen recording saves its cursor (CU1b), the
  editor draws it (CU3c), a Cursor section restyles it (CU4), Auto Zoom plans zooms at clicks and
  typing (CU7), shortcut overlays (CU8), Speed Up Typing (CU9b), and all of it on landing (CU10).
- **Beside it, lane C (the camera).** Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes proves the analysis lane (CJ2b);
  then Remove Background (CO3), cleaner edges (CO4) and Text Behind Subject (CO5).
- **Then shorts:** Make Vertical Version (VR3, VR4), Find Clips and Make Shorts (FC7a–FC9); camera
  layouts at the playhead and at record time (CO6–CO8). **Then podcasts:** Switch by Speaker
  (SW2b), every audio track (SW3a–SW7b), the Angle Viewer (SW9a, SW9b).

## The owner's answers (2026-11-01)

> "Add all: 1-6. Remove all explicit non-goals. The recorder can ask for input monitoring.
> Anything that requires significant AI should require that the user has supplied a key.
> Otherwise disable. "Cutting one real video per lead segment in Frame Job alongside the first
> bet" OK. Create a full design, then we'll compact and begin."

How each is applied — the orchestrator's reading, recorded at CJ0a. Each line is a default the
owner can change.

- **"Add all: 1-6"** is all six bets of the survey's "The bets", in one road map (CJ-2), led by
  people who record themselves talking (survey decision 1's recommendation). The survey's next
  tier (lines 358–369) and "Not worth chasing" (371–391) are not in it, and are neither in nor
  out.
- **"Remove all explicit non-goals"** answers survey decision 2. CJ-1 lifts every exclusion spec
  §1's non-goal paragraph names (`designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md:13–40`) and its bar sentence
  (`:9–11`), and §2's "Left out" list (`02-six-ideas.md:24–26`):
  - **Lifted:** multicam; grading beyond per-clip controls (already in by GR-1) and the features
    once marked not wanted (GR-20, GR-27…GR-30); a plugin system and §1's clause "nothing else is
    scriptable" (G-1); §1's clause keeping third-party Audio Unit hosting out (AU-2); motion blur;
    stabilisation; optical-flow retiming; auto-reframe; ML or heavy pixel work outside the
    compositor's one pass; callouts and reconstructing afterwards what the recorder saw
    (`recording.md`, CAM-1); any platform but macOS; and §2's pointer effects, templates,
    publishing to YouTube or Vimeo and a stock-media library.
  - **Lifting makes a thing allowed, not scheduled.** This road map builds, from that list:
    multicam (SW, as a program track over angle tracks, SW-3), auto-reframe (VR-1), ML outside
    the one pass (Vision boxes and person masks made offline and drawn in the one pass: CJ2a,
    CJ3, VR1, CO1), reconstructed callouts (CU's cursor, zooms and keystroke overlays) and motion
    blur on zooms and the cursor (CU11, spike-gated). Nothing else on the list is built.
  - **Decisions that implement a non-goal stand as current design** until a phase that needs
    otherwise amends them in writing, before its code: G-1 (a graphic is a source; nothing else
    becomes scriptable here), AU-2 (no third-party Audio Unit is hosted here), R5-1 (effects are
    closed vocabularies), and `recording.md`'s "a recording is ordinary media" (which CU-2
    amends at CU0a). Their amendment lines say "§1's clause lifted; the decision stands as
    current design" (CJ0a's table).
  - GR-20 and GR-27…GR-30 were the owner's own "not wanted"; CJ0a asks the owner to confirm the
    literal reading (question 5).
- **"The recorder can ask for input monitoring"** answers survey decision 4 (CJ-4). Only the
  recorder panel asks, and only when the person turns on Record shortcuts and presses Record;
  `record_screen` only reads the grant. Capture is opt-in per recording, records each ⌘ or ⌃
  shortcut by name and only the TIME of every other key press, nothing while any app holds secure
  input, and shows a mark in the menu bar while on (CU-3, CU-7). It is the recorder's fourth
  grant, after Screen Recording, Microphone and Camera.
- **"Anything that requires significant AI should require … a key. Otherwise disable."** answers
  survey decisions 6 and 7 (CJ-3). Its exact reading:
  - A feature needs a key when it sends to a language model or a cloud model: Claude through the
    person's Anthropic key (Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant, AI-8) or AssemblyAI through its key
    (Settings ▸ Transcription, R6-5).
  - Without the key, every control that would make a NEW request is disabled, its tooltip
    CJ-11's sentence naming the key and where it is set; every tool call that would send refuses
    with that sentence, at the point it would send — after its own earlier refusals and after any
    answer it can give from a cache.
  - "Present" is a stored non-empty key, or the proof's environment variable, in R6-5's order.
    Whether a key is valid is the service's answer to a request and never decides a control.
  - A result already paid for stays usable without a key: cached AssemblyAI transcripts serve
    captions (R6-16), Remove Filler Words, the review's filler strikes and a short's filler cut;
    a cached Find Clips ranking is read at no cost.
  - No on-device fallback: Apple FoundationModels is not used, and filler detection stays
    AssemblyAI's (TR-7 stands).
  - Not "significant AI" and never gated: Vision, Sound Analysis, Speech (`SpeechEngine`),
    Silero VAD and `AUSoundIsolation` — Apple frameworks and models that run today without a key.
  - It applies to the shipped features too (Remove Filler Words, Generate Captions' AssemblyAI
    engine, `transcribe`'s cloud engine, `transcribe_for_fillers`, the Assistant), through one
    implementation, CJ1's `ModelKeys`.
- **"Cutting one real video per lead segment … alongside the first bet. OK."** answers survey
  decision 9 (CJ-5). T1 (talking head, S-TH1) and T2 (screen tutorial, S-ST1) are cut three times:
  the baseline when TX1 starts, the checkpoint after TX3 (T1 by deleting words), and the closing
  run at TX8. Each is recorded in "The owner's trials" below and the verdict under CJ-5, as
  grading's trial was under GR-9. Later segments have trials of their own (CU12, VR-38, FC-91,
  SW-29).
- **"Create a full design, then we'll compact and begin"** is this file. After compaction the
  orchestrator starts at CJ0a, which asks CJ0a's five questions first.
- **Survey decisions not answered:** 5 (a vertical copy or linked versions) is asked at VR7a, after
  the vertical trial; 8 (the multi-stream 4K and multi-hour measurement) is CJ0a's question 4,
  run as SW-S2 in SW0 on a yes; 10 (positioning) is not a build question. Decision 3's AI-10 and
  W-10 amendments belong to the next tier; no bet needs them.

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Working arrangement.** `.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs` (branch `worktree-creator-jobs`) is
  the integration branch. Each phase is one litecode pipeline (design → adversary → implement →
  review → fix), handoff dir `~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-<phase id lowercased>` (`cj-tx2a`,
  `cj-cu0b`, …), built in a lane worktree of its own, gated (`make gate`) and committed there,
  then rebased onto the integration branch by one serialized integrator, one landing at a time,
  and gated again. Merging into main follows CJ0a's question 1 (recommended: fast-forward after
  each landing, since other work continues on main). Commits stage only the phase's own files
  (other sessions share the tree).
- **Lanes: at most three, split by the files they touch.** **A, words:** the key gate, the
  Transcript tab, New Project from Range, Find Clips, then every audio track. **B, recorder and
  placement:** the cursor and the recorder, then camera layouts, hide while silent and link
  groups. **C, pictures:** the analysis lane, the camera cutout, faces, Make Vertical Version,
  the clip ceiling, then the switch. A lane whose next phase needs another lane's unlanded phase
  waits; it never builds against an unlanded one. The integrator may move a phase to an idle lane
  when its dependencies have landed and no running phase holds its files, and records the move.
- **Collisions and renumbering, at each landing.** A format bump is provisional ("38p") until its
  phase lands; the integrator renumbers it, its `schema_vN.rs` and its `format_history.rs`
  paragraph when another lane landed one first. Decision IDs are renumbered only when two phases
  claimed one. JOB numbers are renumbered inside their block. The integrator also reconciles the
  pinned counts (CJ-8 (g)), the screen catalog's numbers, the spec index's Lines cells,
  `UIMenuTable.swift` and `capture_spike/inventory.json` rows, `menus-and-shortcuts.md` (a key
  equivalent is checked for a clash, CJ-8 (e)), and the `LayerUniforms` size pins (CJ-8 (b)).
- **IDs (CJ-7).** Phases are `XXn`, XX one of TX (transcript), CU (cursor and recorder), VR
  (vertical), FC (find clips), SW (switch by speaker), CO (cutout and layouts) and CJ (shared); a
  phase split by size is `XXna`, `XXnb`…, sharing its number's block. Phase XXn owns decisions
  XX-n0…XX-n9; XX0 owns XX-1…XX-9, and a bet with no zero phase records its scope-level decisions
  at CJ0a under its own prefix (VR-1…VR-7, TX-70; SW's SW-3 sits in SW0's block). CJ0 owns
  CJ-1…CJ-9. Spikes are XX-S1, XX-S2…. Manual checks are `JOB-n` in blocks of ten: CJ 1–9, TX
  10–19, CU 20–29, VR 30–39, FC 40–49, SW 50–59, CO 60–69, then 70 onward for a bet that needs
  more. The checkpoint after TX3 is CP1.
- **Agent parity.** Every user-visible edit has its MCP mirror: a handler (a row in
  `AgentServer+CreatorJobs.swift`'s `creatorHandlers`, CJ-8 (d)), a catalog entry declaring
  `scope`, and a comment naming the UI path. A command that is a composite of ops lands as one
  undo step through `performGroupedEdit`, and its tool runs the same planner; a rule that must
  hold inside the core makes it an op (CJ-8 (f)). Every new property is a `set_video` or
  `set_audio` key, every answer readable through `get_project` or the tool's own answer.
- **Proof currency.** The repo's: placements read back through `get_project`, PNGs compared byte
  for byte, exports decoded to PCM and measured by the proof's own arithmetic, planners on canned
  analyses (CJ-26) so their rows are byte-exact on any Mac, Vision's rows on fixtures and samples
  against tolerances fixed before the run, and a proof compared against the cache, never a
  recomputation (E9's rule). The recorded run of each phase is against Release, after the gate's
  `make app`. Mutants target each phase's decisions, about one per branch, threshold, refusal or
  ordering, run once on the final instrument. What only a person can judge is a JOB row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- **The key rule in practice.** Every keyed control or tool is a row of `ModelKeys.keyed` (CJ1),
  tests presence only through `ModelKeys.present`, refuses in `ModelKeys`' sentence at the point
  it would send, and its catalog description names its key (the parity check's sixth part,
  CJ-13). Proofs run with `-RCSecretFolder` on an empty scratch folder and the variables unset,
  or a dummy key against `assemblyai_fake.py` or `anthropic_fake.py`; the owner's stored keys are
  never read (R6-9, AI-13). `.secrets/` is never opened.
- **Spend.** Only three runs spend money, each behind `--live --cap` and the month's budget (P-3,
  P-6), its dollars reported: FC-S2 (Anthropic, cap $3.00), FC-S3 (AssemblyAI, cap $0.50) and
  FC8a's prompt eval (`assistant_prompt_eval.py --live --cap 1.00`). TX-S4's AssemblyAI read (about
  a cent) runs only if the owner allows it.
- **Samples.** The owner's recordings live in `tools/proof/media/creator/` (gitignored), with a
  row each in `samples/README.md`; they are never committed, since they carry the owner's face and
  voice, and are sent to a cloud service only by a spike that names it, with a guest's
  recordings sent only with the guest's agreement. No phase waits for a sample: a row that needs
  a missing one skips by name and is owed in the phase's record.
- **Persisted fields** carry serde defaults, are written only when set, and bump the format
  (`core/CLAUDE.md`); an older project opens unchanged and renders byte-identically.
- **Size.** A file at the ~600-line cap (400 for a file created after the rule) gives something up
  before it takes anything on, as a pure move landed and gated alone; frozen files take wiring
  only. A phase is sized for one litecode pipeline; effort is never measured in lines, and no
  feature has a line budget.
- **Long or costly runs** (SW-S2's 34 GB fixture, a three-hour file, FC8b's thirty shorts) run only
  behind their own flags and after the owner's yes. A single flaky failure is re-run once before
  any investigation; a soak over 30 minutes is asked first.

## How it fits the tree

At `d0661e5d`.

**Where the non-goals are written.** Only in the spec and in §11 entries that cite it:
`designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md` (47 lines: "Mac only" at 7, the bar sentence at 9–11, the
non-goal paragraph at 13–40), `02-six-ideas.md` (26 lines; "Left out" at 24–26),
`designs/spec/README.md:20` (the index row; `spec_index_proof.py` checks its Lines cells in
`make test`), and the §11 entries `recording.md:6–15`, `camera-recording.md:15–38` (CAM-1),
`graphics.md:6–16` (G-1), `audio.md:52–59` (AU-2), `grading.md:26–36` (GR-1),
`effects-motion.md:6–10` (R5-1), `grading-3.md:466` (GR-20) and `grading-4.md:99–108`
(GR-27…GR-30). `README.md`, `docs/guide/` and the three `CLAUDE.md` files hold none;
`CONTEXT.md:37,57`'s "plugin" is vocabulary and stays; `designs/adr/` is history.

**Keys: two keys, two stores, seven presence reads, three behaviours.**

# Road map "creator-jobs" — the jobs that send creators elsewhere

**Not opened yet.** CJ0a opens it: it records the owner's answers below as CJ-1…CJ-9 with the
bets' scope-level decisions, rewrites spec §1 and §2, and makes the two spec splits. The brief is
`designs/creator-survey.md`: its "The bets" (lines 173–356) and the market sections they cite. The
planned worktree is `.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs`, branch `worktree-creator-jobs`, cut from main
when CJ0a starts. Decisions go in a new `designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` (one series,
continued in `creator-jobs-2.md` past about 500 lines), each with its row in
`11-decisions/README.md` and that file's Lines cell. This file holds the plan and, as phases land,
each phase's record. Line counts and line numbers are `wc -l` and `grep -n` at `d0661e5d` (main,
2026-11-01); a phase re-reads them at its start.

## Goal

Frame Job finishes video better than most creator tools: its audio chain, colour and HDR, codecs
and an MCP surface over the whole editor (survey, "What Frame Job has"). It loses creators earlier,
at six jobs that now define a creator editor. After this road map each is a command that runs on
the Mac, lands as ordinary undo steps on a real timeline, and has an MCP tool that runs the same
planner:

1. **The Transcript tab (TX).** The timeline read as words, in timeline order. Selected words are
   deleted on every unlocked track as one step; cut words stay greyed and come back with Restore
   Words. A review pass strikes long pauses, fillers (where an AssemblyAI transcript exists),
   retakes, restarts and repeats, for the person to keep or remove in one step.
2. **Screen recordings with the cursor as data (CU).** The recorder saves the cursor's path,
   images, clicks, scrolls and (opt-in) shortcuts beside the movie, and the editor draws the
   cursor as part of the screen clip's layer. Auto Zoom, shortcut overlays, sped-up typing and
   motion blur follow, each as ordinary actions and clips, and the recorder can run them on
   landing.
3. **Make Vertical Version (VR).** A 9:16 or 1:1 copy of a finished edit, each picture following
   the face, person or salient region Vision found on the Mac (the cursor in a recording made
   after CU, the speaker in a two-shot after SW), as eased x, y and scale actions; captions
   re-paged and graphics re-laid. Linked versions in one project are designed and asked.
4. **Find Clips (FC).** A long recording analysed on the Mac (sentences, speakers, loudness,
   laughter, applause, cheering), ranked by Claude on the person's key with a stated reason per
   moment and no score, and made into saved, captioned, vertical shorts on the Export Queue.
5. **Switch by Speaker, and every audio track (SW).** A program track of shots cut to whoever is

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Working arrangement.** `.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs` (branch `worktree-creator-jobs`) is
  the integration branch. Each phase is one litecode pipeline (design → adversary → implement →
  review → fix), handoff dir `~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-<phase id lowercased>` (`cj-tx2a`,
  `cj-cu0b`, …), built in a lane worktree of its own, gated (`make gate`) and committed there,
  then rebased onto the integration branch by one serialized integrator, one landing at a time,
  and gated again. Merging into main follows CJ0a's question 1 (recommended: fast-forward after
  each landing, since other work continues on main). Commits stage only the phase's own files
  (other sessions share the tree).
- **Lanes: at most three, split by the files they touch.** **A, words:** the key gate, the
  Transcript tab, New Project from Range, Find Clips, then every audio track. **B, recorder and
  placement:** the cursor and the recorder, then camera layouts, hide while silent and link
  groups. **C, pictures:** the analysis lane, the camera cutout, faces, Make Vertical Version,
  the clip ceiling, then the switch. A lane whose next phase needs another lane's unlanded phase
  waits; it never builds against an unlanded one. The integrator may move a phase to an idle lane
  when its dependencies have landed and no running phase holds its files, and records the move.
- **Collisions and renumbering, at each landing.** A format bump is provisional ("38p") until its
  phase lands; the integrator renumbers it, its `schema_vN.rs` and its `format_history.rs`
  paragraph when another lane landed one first. Decision IDs are renumbered only when two phases
  claimed one. JOB numbers are renumbered inside their block. The integrator also reconciles the
  pinned counts (CJ-8 (g)), the screen catalog's numbers, the spec index's Lines cells,
  `UIMenuTable.swift` and `capture_spike/inventory.json` rows, `menus-and-shortcuts.md` (a key
  equivalent is checked for a clash, CJ-8 (e)), and the `LayerUniforms` size pins (CJ-8 (b)).
- **IDs (CJ-7).** Phases are `XXn`, XX one of TX (transcript), CU (cursor and recorder), VR
  (vertical), FC (find clips), SW (switch by speaker), CO (cutout and layouts) and CJ (shared); a
  phase split by size is `XXna`, `XXnb`…, sharing its number's block. Phase XXn owns decisions
  XX-n0…XX-n9; XX0 owns XX-1…XX-9, and a bet with no zero phase records its scope-level decisions
  at CJ0a under its own prefix (VR-1…VR-7, TX-70; SW's SW-3 sits in SW0's block). CJ0 owns
  CJ-1…CJ-9. Spikes are XX-S1, XX-S2…. Manual checks are `JOB-n` in blocks of ten: CJ 1–9, TX
  10–19, CU 20–29, VR 30–39, FC 40–49, SW 50–59, CO 60–69, then 70 onward for a bet that needs
  more. The checkpoint after TX3 is CP1.
- **Agent parity.** Every user-visible edit has its MCP mirror: a handler (a row in
  `AgentServer+CreatorJobs.swift`'s `creatorHandlers`, CJ-8 (d)), a catalog entry declaring
  `scope`, and a comment naming the UI path. A command that is a composite of ops lands as one
  undo step through `performGroupedEdit`, and its tool runs the same planner; a rule that must
  hold inside the core makes it an op (CJ-8 (f)). Every new property is a `set_video` or
  `set_audio` key, every answer readable through `get_project` or the tool's own answer.
- **Proof currency.** The repo's: placements read back through `get_project`, PNGs compared byte
  for byte, exports decoded to PCM and measured by the proof's own arithmetic, planners on canned
  analyses (CJ-26) so their rows are byte-exact on any Mac, Vision's rows on fixtures and samples
  against tolerances fixed before the run, and a proof compared against the cache, never a
  recomputation (E9's rule). The recorded run of each phase is against Release, after the gate's
  `make app`. Mutants target each phase's decisions, about one per branch, threshold, refusal or
  ordering, run once on the final instrument. What only a person can judge is a JOB row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- **The key rule in practice.** Every keyed control or tool is a row of `ModelKeys.keyed` (CJ1),
  tests presence only through `ModelKeys.present`, refuses in `ModelKeys`' sentence at the point
  it would send, and its catalog description names its key (the parity check's sixth part,
  CJ-13). Proofs run with `-RCSecretFolder` on an empty scratch folder and the variables unset,
  or a dummy key against `assemblyai_fake.py` or `anthropic_fake.py`; the owner's stored keys are
  never read (R6-9, AI-13). `.secrets/` is never opened.
- **Spend.** Only three runs spend money, each behind `--live --cap` and the month's budget (P-3,
  P-6), its dollars reported: FC-S2 (Anthropic, cap $3.00), FC-S3 (AssemblyAI, cap $0.50) and
  FC8a's prompt eval (`assistant_prompt_eval.py --live --cap 1.00`). TX-S4's AssemblyAI read (about
  a cent) runs only if the owner allows it.
- **Samples.** The owner's recordings live in `tools/proof/media/creator/` (gitignored), with a
  row each in `samples/README.md`; they are never committed, since they carry the owner's face and
  voice, and are sent to a cloud service only by a spike that names it, with a guest's
  recordings sent only with the guest's agreement. No phase waits for a sample: a row that needs
  a missing one skips by name and is owed in the phase's record.
- **Persisted fields** carry serde defaults, are written only when set, and bump the format
  (`core/CLAUDE.md`); an older project opens unchanged and renders byte-identically.
- **Size.** A file at the ~600-line cap (400 for a file created after the rule) gives something up
  before it takes anything on, as a pure move landed and gated alone; frozen files take wiring
  only. A phase is sized for one litecode pipeline; effort is never measured in lines, and no
  feature has a line budget.
- **Long or costly runs** (SW-S2's 34 GB fixture, a three-hour file, FC8b's thirty shorts) run only
  behind their own flags and after the owner's yes. A single flaky failure is re-run once before
  any investigation; a soak over 30 minutes is asked first.

**Scope-level decisions of the bets, recorded at CJ0a (their phases' sections hold the rest).**

- **VR-1 — Auto-reframe is in, as analysis plus ordinary actions.** Subjects are found offline by
  Vision's rectangle and saliency requests on the Mac and cached in CJ2a's store; the core plans
  the framing, and the result is placement and actions on the clip. No mask, no shipped model, no
  pixel work outside the one-pass compositor.
- **VR-2 — Bet 3 needs no key.** No VR control is disabled for a missing key.
- **VR-3 — A regenerated copy first; linked versions designed and asked at VR7a.** The planner
  answers a framing path, a similarity per instant from the source canvas to the target; the copy
  composes it into each clip, and linked versions would store it per framing. With a no at VR7a,
  VR7a–VR9 are filed as one issue carrying this design.
- **VR-4 — Subjects are boxes, detected per sample, never tracked by Vision.** Faces come from
  CJ3's `faces`; people (`VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2, `upperBodyOnly` false) and salient
  regions (`VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2) from VR1's `subjects`. A fresh
  `VNImageRequestHandler` per sample; no `VNTrackObjectRequest` or other stateful request. Linking
  boxes across samples is the core planner's (CJ-31); masks are out for framing (E9: they flicker).
- **VR-5 — The planner is the core's, and `reframe_clip` is an op (CJ-8 (f)).** Swift measures and
  caches; the core maps samples into clip time, chooses subjects, plans, enforces coverage and
  writes actions, because coverage (VR-7) needs (★) and `fill_scale` and composition into
  existing action ends needs the actions' own evaluation. The op is a pure function of the project
  and the samples handed to it.
- **VR-6 — No nest is made to make room for framing.** Framing is composed into the clip's own base
  and actions; a nest would cost tracks against `MAX_TRACKS` and wall the clip off from blurred
  backgrounds, filler cuts and the transcript.
- **VR-7 — A followed picture never shows the canvas, with three named exceptions.** The window
  lies inside the clip's picture (scale at least fill, offsets clamped by (★)), every key is a
  covering state, and one curve carries x, y and scale, so every frame between keys covers too
  (the covering placements are convex). Exceptions: **`fit` spans** (the whole picture, the canvas
  around it, unless `backdrop` puts a blurred copy behind; a nest clip has none); **motion** (a
  `video.motion` that moves or turns the layer keeps its motion, and the guarantee excludes its
  span — the whole clip for a During motion; `spin` counts as rotation; `fade` is not an
  exception); **opacity** (fades, transitions and opacity below 1 are the author's).
- **TX-70 — A review pass may strike a phrase the speaker said again, found by comparing the
  spelled words of neighbouring phrases; it offers every strike for review and cuts nothing until
  the person removes it. Amends TR-3, AI-6 and W-9** (owner, 2026-11-01, accepting bet 1 with
  the survey's amendment). It finds a **restart** (a phrase whose words are the opening words of
  the next), a **retake** (a phrase of four or more words most of whose words recur, in order, at
  the start of one of the next few phrases, TX-71's numbers) and a **repeat** (one to four words
  said twice in a row); the earlier is struck, the last kept. It reads each word's text lowercased
  with edge punctuation trimmed (TR-8's rule, fillers left out), their order, the pauses between
  them (the voice cache) and sentence punctuation; phrases are compared only within one track and,
  where labels exist, one speaker; one take placed twice (the same media's same source ticks) is
  never a retake. No model reads the words, nothing is sent, no key is needed. A false start that
  repeats no words stays the assistant's, on the person's ask (TR-5). Amending lines: **TR-3**
  "a false start that repeats words — a restart, or a line said again — is found by TX-70's
  comparison of spelled words and offered struck for review; one that repeats no words is found
  only by reading what was meant, so no pipeline does it (W-9, AI-6); the assistant may, when the
  person asks (TR-5)"; **AI-6** "a pipeline may strike words for review by comparing their
  spelling, order and timing with the phrases beside them; that is not picking words by meaning,
  and nothing is cut until the person removes the strikes"; **W-9** "the Transcript tab's review
  pass strikes repeated phrases for the person to remove, by comparing spelled words, never by a
  language model; captions are untouched". Risk accepted: a deliberate repetition is struck and
  shown for review.
- **SW-3 — Multicam is in, as a program track over angle tracks.** Synced camera clips (angles)
  stay whole on their own tracks; a program track holds the shots, each an ordinary clip copied
  from an angle at the same time. Switch by Speaker writes the program track, Switch Angle

  multicam source kind and no nest in point: every shot can be rolled, trimmed, graded and deleted
  like any clip, and spec §2's one kind of track holds.

#### Every spike, with its rule

Each rule is fixed here before its run (CJ-7). Instruments go in `tools/proof/creator_spike/`
(CJ, VR, SW), `transcript_spike/` and `retake_spike/` (TX), `cursor_spike/` (CU) and
`cutout_spike/` (CO), probes built through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`; each run's
`results.json` stores `rule_sha256` (CJ-7), the OS build and the compute device. A spike's
verdict is recorded in its phase's record and in the decision it feeds before the phase's code.
Runs that need power run on AC (`pmset` first).

**The analysis set (CJ-S2, CJ-S3, CJ-S4 hold the only rules for device, rate, size, log input,
playback impact and shots; VR1 and CO1 re-run their rows for their own kinds.)**

- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling** (at CJ6's head; decides CJ-9). How many clips can a project hold
  before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096, 8,192,
  16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as packages;
  N above 4,096 needs a scratch Release build with the cap raised, never committed. Measured: (1)
  `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2) `rc_project_from_json` plus
  `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times, median; (4) over MCP, one
  `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo, each from the call to its answer; (5) after
  (4), the time until the next main-thread call (`get_project`) answers; (6) after an edit, the
  time until `play_preview` composes its first frame; (7) a probe that lays out and draws a
  `TimelineView` of N clips offscreen at the fit-all and the default zoom, median of 20; (8) the
  app's resident memory after 50 undo steps of `split`. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N for
  which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms, (4) applies and undoes in ≤ 1 s each, (5) ≤ 1 s,
  (6) ≤ 2 s, (7) ≤ 33 ms at both zooms, and (8) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical memory.
  N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096 and CJ6 ends with
  the verdict and no code.
- **CJ-S2 — Vision on video** (at CJ3's head; decides CJ-30 and CJ-32). On which device, at what
  rate and size, and from which reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate?
  Inputs: the face fixtures always; S-TH1…S-TH4 when they exist. Measured: the cache bytes of
  three runs on each of CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; seconds per minute of source for decode,
  rectangles, and rectangles with landmarks, at long sides 720, 1280, 1920 and native; face recall
  (the share of samples, in spans where a face is known present, with a box overlapping it) at
  each size; recall and reader cost raw against converted on each log or HLG sample; face share
  over S-TH1's first 60 s. **Rules:** (1) **Device:** the fastest of the three whose three runs
  are byte-identical; if none is, the CPU when it meets rule 2's rate; otherwise the fastest, with
  every proof comparing against the cache only. (2) **Rate:** 10 samples a second if decode plus
  rectangles plus landmarks run at least 3× real time on 1080p30 and 1.5× on 4K30 on the chosen
  device; else 5; else 2.5. (3) **Size:** the smallest long side of 720, 1280 and 1920 whose face
  recall is at least 98 % of recall at native size, on the small-face fixture and on S-TH1 when it
  exists. (4) **Landmarks** stay in `faces` if they cost at most 2× rectangles alone; else mouth
  opening is a `mouths` kind on the same grid, built by SW8. (5) **Log and HDR input:** the
  converted reader, unless on every log or HLG sample raw recall is at least 98 % of converted
  recall AND the converted reader costs more than 1.5× the direct one per frame (CJ-S3's figure);
  then face kinds read raw. With no such sample, converted. (6) **Face share** on S-TH1's first
  60 s below 95 % stops VR1 and SW8 until CJ-30 is amended; without S-TH1 the row skips by name
  and is owed in CJ3's record. VR1 re-runs rules 1–3 and 5 for its requests; CO1 re-runs rule 1
  for its mask request.
- **CJ-S3 — The lane** (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23; replaces CO's former CO-S4).
  What does decoding for analysis cost, does a second concurrent picture job pay, and does
  analysis cost playback? On a 4K HEVC 10-bit HLG file and a 1080p H.264 file (synthetic until
  S-TH4 exists): frames a second through the direct and the converted reader at long sides 256
  and 1280; the total throughput of one job and of two; `play_preview`'s composed frames over 20 s
  of a 1080p30 timeline idle and with a `shots` job running. **Rules:** (a) **width:** 2 only if
  two jobs reach at least 1.5× one job's throughput; else 1. (b) **playback:** when composed
  frames with a job running fall by more than 2 % against idle, the picture queue pauses while
  any transport plays and resumes when none does. CJ3 (`faces`), CO1 (`masks`) and VR1
  (`subjects`) each re-run (b) with their own job at their head; the first failure turns the pause
  on for every picture kind, recorded as an amendment of CJ-21. (c) **reader:** converted for
  converting media and direct for the rest, unless CJ-S2's rule 5 says otherwise for a kind.
- **CJ-S4 — The shot signature** (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-24). Which signature, threshold T
  and neighbourhood m find hard cuts inside one flattened clip? Candidates: a 32-bin luma
  histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, and a 4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at long side 256, both by
  L1 distance. Inputs: the shots fixture; a no-cut talking head (S-TH1, else ten minutes of the
  moving-still fixture); flattened exports with known cut lists (the trial's exports when they
  exist, and always a fixture project of 40 clips cut from four `testsrc` variants, exported by
  Frame Job, its cut list read from `get_project`). **Rule:** the signature and T with the highest
  recall on the flattened exports with at most one false cut per 10 minutes on the no-cut input;
  m the largest of 4, 6, 8 and 12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It passes at
  recall ≥ 98 %. If no candidate passes, a 64 × 36 luma sum of absolute differences joins as a
  second signal and the run repeats; if that fails, CJ-24 ships with the measured recall stated in
  the guide.

**TX.**

- **TX-S1 — The fill's cost** (at TX1's head; no owner media needed). How fast does
  `SpeechEngine` recognise long speech on this Mac, can one run cover a whole file, and does a
  fill slow playback? A probe calls `SpeechEngine.transcribe` on `say` phrases joined into 10- and
  60-minute files, and on S-TH1 and S-LONG1 when they exist; it measures wall time, peak added
  memory, temporary WAV size, word count, each word's start against the same audio recognised as
  six 10-minute windows (median and p95 |Δ|), and, in the Release app over MCP, `play_preview`'s
  composed frames over 10 s of a 1080p timeline while a 60-minute fill runs at `.userInitiated`,
  then at `.utility`, each against 10 s idle. **Rules:** outcome A, one whole-file run per media
  (TX-12), if the 60-minute run finishes within 6 minutes and its peak added memory is at most
  1/32 of physical memory; otherwise outcome B, per-clip windows from the playhead outward. The
  fill keeps `.userInitiated` if `play_preview` composes at least 95 % of its idle count during
  it; else `.utility` if that reaches 95 %; else the fill pauses while the transport plays. The
  measured rate replaces "a few seconds per minute" in the guide.
- **TX-S2 — The view** (at TX2a's head). Which view holds a three-hour transcript and leaves the
  transport keys to the editor? Candidates in order: (b) a custom `NSView` laid out by TextKit 2
  (`NSTextLayoutManager` over `NSTextContentStorage`, viewport layout); (c) an `NSTableView` of
  paragraph rows; (a) a read-only `NSTextView` subclass. Fixture: 27,000 synthetic words in 900
  paragraphs with 40 collapsed cuts and 300 strikes, in the offscreen harness on the main thread.
  Measured: first layout of the visible part, a full rebuild after an edit, moving the highlight,
  hit-testing a click, a selection across paragraphs, added memory. **Rule:** take the first of
  (b), (c), (a) that meets: first layout ≤ 200 ms; rebuild ≤ 100 ms; highlight ≤ 2 ms; hit-test ≤
  1 ms; added memory ≤ 1/256 of physical memory; Space and J/K/L reach `handleEditorKey` with no
  change to a frozen file. (a) meets the last only with a change to `handleEditorKey`'s first line
  (`EditorViewController.swift:713`), so it is taken only if (b) and (c) both fail, and that one
  line is recorded as TX-21's deviation.
- **TX-S3 — Cut edges** (at TX3's head). Where should a word's cut fall, when on-device word
  ranges tile the audio and start 270 ms early? Fixtures: (1) `say` phrases joined by silences of
  60, 120, 250, 500 and 1,000 ms (every onset known); (2) the owner's o2
  (`tools/proof/media/filler-sample/`, 29.4 s); (3) S-TH1 and S-RT1 when they exist. Rules
  compared: E0 the transcript's edges; E1 E0 corrected by `CaptionPages.lead(for:)`; E2
  onset-to-onset from the voice cache as TX-30 words it, with E1 as its fallback, at guards of 0,
  32, 64 and 96 ms. Measured: per boundary on (1), a clipped onset and the error against the true
  onset; on (2) and (3), the share of edges in voice-cache non-speech and under −40 dBFS in the
  peak cache. **Rule:** E2 with the smallest guard that clips no onset on (1) and keeps at least
  95 % of real-speech edges in non-speech; else E1 if it clips none on (1); else E0, with JOB-11
  the only judge. TX-30 records which.
- **TX-S4 — The retake rule** (at TX7's head; needs S-RT1, with its `say` twin as the synthetic
  half). Which phrase split, window and similarity find planted retakes and restarts without
  striking the traps? The script and its answer key are `tools/proof/retake_spike/SCRIPT.md`: 8
  retakes, 8 restarts, 6 repeats and 6 traps (an anaphora, "that that", a refrain, a list). Both
  reads are recognised on this Mac; AssemblyAI only if the owner allows the paid run. Grid: pause
  P {0.4, 0.6, 0.8 s}; window K {2, 3}; similarity θ {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8}; one-word repeats {off,
  pause-separated}. **Rule:** among the settings that strike no trap word on either read, take the
  highest recall of retakes plus restarts on the owner's read, ties to the higher θ; if that
  recall is under 80 %, the retake kind ships off by default. If no setting strikes no trap word,
  the retake kind ships off, and restarts and repeats ship on at the setting with the fewest trap
  strikes on both reads together, ties to the higher θ. TX-71 records the setting; its strikes on
  S-TH1 go to JOB-14.

**CU** (CU-S1…CU-S4 run in CU0b; rows whose grant is held by a launched `.app` run in a scratch
hardened-runtime bundle opened with `open -a`; rows that post input skip by name without
Accessibility for the poster, and the owner's one run covers them).

- **CU-S1 — Capture APIs, grants, clocks, the cursor's image.** Rows: A1 a listen-only
  `CGEventTap` (session) for mouse down/up, dragged and scroll, no grant; A2 the same tap for keys
  with no grant, Input Monitoring only, Accessibility only; A3 `NSEvent` global and local
  monitors, the same matrix; A4 `CGEvent(source: nil)?.location` polled at 120 Hz (µs per call,
  whether `CGWarpMouseCursorPosition` moves are seen); A5 `NSCursor.currentSystem` over TextEdit's
  text, a Safari link and a resize edge (identity, hot spot, reps, ms per call with a TIFF hash,
  the safe thread, whether it answers nil); A6 event timestamp against arrival
  `mach_absolute_time`, as ns, mach units and `systemUptime`; A7 keys delivered while the probe
  holds `EnableSecureEventInput()`; A8 whether the signed bundle needs a plist key or entitlement
  for ListenEvent, and whether a tap made before the grant works without a relaunch; A9 hidden
  cursors (a helper's `NSCursor.hide()`, TextEdit's `setHiddenUntilMouseMoves`): what
  `currentSystem`, its image and `CGCursorIsVisible()` report, 10 trials each; A10 a replacement
  for `currentSystem`: two 64 × 64 pt `SCStream`s around the pointer, `showsCursor` on and off,
  differenced, the silhouette's IoU against A5's image, 10 trials over three cursors. **Rule:**
  positions are polled (A4) if a poll costs ≤ 20 µs median and sees warps and real moves, else
  they come from the click source; clicks and scrolls use the tap if it delivers ≥ 99 % of 200
  events with no grant (Frame Job's own windows included), else the monitors if they do, else
  **STOP** (clicks not captured; the owner is asked before CU1a); keys use the tap under Input
  Monitoring alone, else the monitors, and if keys need Accessibility **STOP key capture** (CU6 is
  not built; the owner is asked); the image sampler asks at most 10 times a second plus once per
  mouse-down, `cursor_image=current-system` if A5 identifies another app's I-beam and pointing hand
  in ≥ 9 of 10 trials and its median cost × 10 Hz is ≤ 1 % of one core (≤ 1 ms a call), else
  `none` (no images; the cursor draws as Frame Job's arrow); whatever the verdict, every sample is
  checked for nil at run time, a nil records no change, and a segment whose every sample was nil
  writes `cursor_image: none` and says so on landing; hidden spans are recorded if a signal from
  A9 tells hidden from shown in ≥ 9 of 10 trials in both cases, else not (Hide when idle is the
  remedy); A10 is built only if A5 fails and its IoU is ≥ 0.9 in ≥ 9 of 10 trials
  (`image_fallback=a10`), else the arrow stands and an issue is filed with A10's numbers; the
  event clock is the hypothesis whose arrival − event lies in [0, 20 ms] for ≥ 99 % of events;
  secure input's delivered keys are noted, and the recorder drops keys under
  `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` either way. Verdict line: `VERDICT positions=<poll|events>
  clicks=<tap|monitor|STOP> keys=<tap|monitor|STOP> cursor_image=<current-system|none>
  hidden=<recorded|not-recorded> image_fallback=<a10|arrow> event_clock=<ns|mach|uptime>
  secure=<withheld|delivered> relaunch=<needed|not-needed>`.
- **CU-S2 — From global points to movie pixels, and the time anchor.** In the picture: record with
  `showsCursor = true` over a flat-colour full-screen window, the burned tip found per decoded
  frame, the cursor warped along a known path, every frame's `SCStreamFrameInfo` and the polled
  samples logged. Separate's exact configuration (`showsCursor = false`, `showMouseClicks = false`,
  420v): the truth is the instrument's own 24 pt marker moved to the warped point at each step.
  Still start: the screen held still 2 s while the cursor moves, then a full-screen colour flip at
  a logged host time, recording which anchor the segment used and its error. Sources: a display
  at Nominal and at Best (2×); the instrument's window moved and resized; a window of odd size
  (1001 × 701 pt at 1×); a picked window; a second display when attached; each in both
  configurations. Candidates: **M1** `pixel = (p − screenRect.origin) × contentScale ×
  pixelsPerPoint + contentRect.origin × pixelsPerPoint`, pixelsPerPoint the configured pixel width
  ÷ point width; **M2** M1 with `scaleFactor`; **M3** a fixed display frame from
  `SCDisplay.frame`; anchors E2, E1 and `DisplayTime` of the first complete frame. **Rule:** the
  mapping is the first of M1, M2, M3 with tip error ≤ 1.5 movie px at p95 on every source row
  (odd window included) over still frames; the anchor is the first of E2, E1, DisplayTime with time
  error ≤ one frame interval at p95 on every row of BOTH configurations (position error ÷ speed
  over moving frames); E1's still-start error over 10 runs ≤ 25 ms at p95, else the limit is
  recorded and the file still names E1. **STOP:** if no mapping passes for window sources, window
  recordings keep the burned cursor and the panel greys Separate for Window; if none passes for
  displays, the bet stops after CU1b; if a candidate passes In the picture but fails Separate,
  In the picture is the default (CU-36). The owner is told in each case.
- **CU-S3 — Do dirty rects locate typing?** Records the instrument's own `NSTextView` while text is
  inserted programmatically, beside distractors (the menu-bar clock, a spinner, a playing
  animation); per burst the median centre of the per-frame dirty-rect bounding boxes against the
  caret rect. **Rule:** pass if within 64 pt of the caret in ≥ 9 of 10 bursts: the file stores each
  complete frame's dirty bounding box and CU7 aims typing zooms at their median centre; otherwise
  nothing about dirty rects is stored and typing zooms aim at the last click before the burst,
  else the cursor's position at its start.
- **CU-S4 — The file's size and speed.** The core's reader prototype over a worst case: one hour
  at 120 Hz (432,000 samples), 3,600 clicks, 20,000 key marks, 40 images, each figure measured
  through a JSON request and answer as `rc_cursor_query` runs it. **Rule:** a JSON body
  (columnar integer µs and points × 100) if the file is ≤ 25 MB, parse and validate take ≤ 300 ms,
  and `state at t` takes ≤ 20 µs median once prepared; otherwise a binary columnar body
  (little-endian i64 arrays after a JSON header), version 1 either way. Smoothing's `prepare` at
  smoothing 1 takes ≤ 1 s on the one-hour file, else smoothing is prepared per 60 s window on
  demand, off the compositor's thread, and the verdict says which.
- **CU-S5 — Motion blur's cost** (before CU11; any time after CU0b). A probe through
  `MetalRenderer`'s pipelines draws one full-canvas layer N times at sub-frame transforms (a 2×
  zoom's middle, eased), accumulated in `rgba16Float`, N ∈ {4, 8, 16}, at 1920×1080 and
  3840×2160, measuring GPU time against the frame drawn once. **Rule:** ship zoom blur at the
  largest N in {16, 8, 4} adding ≤ 4 ms at 1080p and ≤ 8 ms at 4K on the owner's Mac, one N for
  preview and export; **STOP zoom blur** if N = 4 misses either bound (numbers recorded, an issue
  filed). Cursor blur (N sprite samples inside `layerSample`) ships either way.

**CO** (CO-S1 and CO-S2 at CO0; CO-S3 at CO0 when S-KEY1 exists, else at CO4's head; the former
CO-S4 is CJ-S3 (b), re-run by CO1).

- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate and read size.** Candidates: person `.balanced`,
  person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with `generateScaledMaskForImage`;
  each at every source frame (capped at 30 a second), at 15 and at 10 a second; frames read at the
  source's size and at a long side of 1920; on the device CJ-S2's rule 1 picks for the mask
  request (the Neural Engine until CO1 re-runs rule 1; a different pick re-measures speed). Truth:
  S-KEY1's keyed composites. Measured on every truth frame against the mask the compositor would
  show there (CO-3's nearest-hold): J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5; B = mean
  |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge at 1080p; B on the gesture segment;
  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment; realtime factor at 1080p30 and
  4K30; also S-KEY1's composite re-tagged with a 90° rotation matrix, and the first Vision call of
  a fresh process (recorded, no rule). **Rule:** (a) a candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is
  out; (b) the rate is every frame, unless B on the gesture segment at 15 a second is within 5 %
  of every-frame B (then 15), and again at 10 a second within 5 % (then 10); (c) **Standard** is
  the fastest remaining candidate at ≥ 1.0× realtime at 1080p30 at that rate whose J is within
  0.02 of the best; if none reaches 1.0×, the rate steps down (every frame → 15 → 10) and (c) is
  applied again; if none reaches 1.0× at 10, Standard is the fastest within 0.02 J at 10 and its
  realtime factor is recorded as a risk; (d) **Best** is the lowest-B candidate, kept only if its
  B is ≥ 15 % below Standard's and it runs ≥ 0.25× realtime, else no Best and no Quality control;
  (e) the read size is a long side of 1920 for a larger source when J and B there are within 0.005
  and 2 % of the source size's, else the source size; (f) the rotated composite's J is within 0.01
  of the unrotated, else **STOP**: CJ-23 is amended before CO1 to read coded frames and pass the
  orientation to Vision. Without S-KEY1 at CO0: speed only, on the E9 fixtures and S-TH1 if
  present, Standard = person `.balanced` at the fastest rate (every frame, 15, 10) reaching 1.0×
  realtime; (b), (d), (e), (f) run when S-KEY1 arrives, before CO4.
- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.** A probe compiled from `app/Sources` takes the
  core's plan of a project built through the FFI, adds by hand a mask track whose segments copy
  the picture segments, fills both through `CompositionBuilder.fill`, and reads every frame
  through a probe compositor (a subclass of the class the project would use) that fetches both
  tracks' buffers per request; frame counts from the probe's own `AVPlayer`. Fixture: a synthetic
  movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and mask chunks written from it with
  chunk-relative times by CO-3's nearest-hold rule. Tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the
  mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy; chunk lengths 5, 10 and 30 s. **Rule:** the mask track is
  kept when all hold: (1) **registration** — every frame shows the mask of the nearest analysed
  source frame (ties to the earlier in the stream its segment reads), at every-frame analysis and
  at 15 a second, across a trim, ×0.5, ×2, ×1.37 with a chunk boundary inside the segment, a ramp
  across a chunk boundary, a freeze, a reverse (mirrored chunks), a split, a nest, a
  cross-dissolve and an HLG variable-frame-rate source (S-TH4, else an `ffmpeg` HLG VFR fixture);
  (2) **colour path** — the value read differs from the DECODED mask by ≤ 1/255 at every pixel in
  an SDR and an HLG composition under the class each is built with (if the plain class conforms
  the mask, a composition with a mask track is built with `ConvertingCompositor` and (2) is
  measured again); (3) **codec loss** — decoded masks' IoU against Vision's (both > 0.5) ≥ 0.995,
  mean |difference| inside the 8 px edge band ≤ 3 levels; (4) **size** ≤ 15 MB per minute of
  30 fps source at Standard; (5) **playback** — a 1080p30 camera with its mask track over a 4K
  screen recording composes, over 20 s crossing ≥ 5 chunk boundaries, ≥ 99 % of the frames it
  composes without the mask track; (6) **build** — a 60-minute camera cut into 120 clips, every
  one cut out, builds within 100 ms more (median of 10) than without mask tracks. The chunk
  length L is the shortest of 5, 10, 30 s passing (5) and (6) whose per-chunk fixed cost adds
  under 5 % to analysis time per minute; the encoding is the smaller of the two that pass.
  Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured on (1), (2), (5), (6) and kept if it passes; if
  neither passes, CO stops after CO1 and the owner is asked.
- **CO-S3 — Whether the edge needs refinement, and which.** Candidates: r0 bilinear sampling and a
  smoothstep remap (the edge and feather controls); r1 a joint bilateral upsample in the layer
  stage (3×3 mask texels weighted by the picture's colour distance, read as `KeyReading` reads);
  r2 a guided filter in a pass before the destination at twice the mask's size. A standalone
  Metal probe over S-KEY1's frames and masks measures B on the composites and cost per frame at
  1080p and 4K (200 frames a sample, three interleaved runs, median of medians). **Rule:** the
  cheapest candidate whose B is ≤ 1.1 × the lowest B ships, if it costs ≤ 1.0 ms at 1080p and ≤
  3.0 ms at 4K above r0; if r1 and r2 both miss the cost bound, r0 ships and the better is filed
  with its numbers.

**VR.**

- **VR-S1 — People and saliency on video** (at VR1's head, after CJ-S2, on CJ-32's device). At
  what rate and frame size do `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2 and
  `VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2 run deterministically and fast enough, and do
  person boxes hold when the face is lost? Instrument `tools/proof/creator_spike/vr_subjects/`
  (synchronous VN* calls through CJ-23's reader); inputs S-TH1 (with the owner's times for the
  leave, turn-away and side-on beats), S-TH4 (HLG) and the moving-still fixture. **Rules:** (1) the
  rate is `faces`' rate if both requests together, at `faces`' frame size, run at ≥ 4× realtime;
  else every other `faces` sample; (2) the frame size is `faces`' unless person recall there is
  more than 1 point under recall at a long side of 1440 on S-TH1, then 1440; (3) three runs on the
  pinned device give byte-identical files, else **STOP**: the kind's stamp carries a tolerance
  instead, amended before VR1's code; (4) people stay if the person box is found in ≥ 90 % of
  S-TH1's turned-away and side-on samples, else `people` leave `subjects` and VR-21's person tier
  is removed by amendment before VR1's code; (5) with S-TH4, person recall through the converted
  path is recorded (no rule). VR1 also re-runs CJ-S2 rules 1–3 and 5 and CJ-S3 (b) with a
  `subjects` job.
- **VR-S2 — The planner's first numbers** (with VR2a, over cached analyses, no video). The core's
  planner from a test binary over S-TH1's cached `faces` and `subjects`, T1's and T2's, and the
  canned fixtures; grid dead zone {6, 10, 15} % × speed {0.3, 0.5, 0.8} windows/s × headroom {33,
  38, 42} %; measured containment (the face centre inside the window's central 60 %) and moves per
  minute. **Rule:** the setting with the highest containment at no more than 6 moves per minute;
  if none reaches 97 % containment, the dead zone shrinks one step and the cap rises to 8. JOB-31
  judges the feel.
- **VR-S3 — Face-to-mic agreement** (at VR6's head). Over S-PC3 (a two-shot with a microphone
  each) and the two-face moving still with synthetic turns, the agreement between each face's
  mouth opening and each mic's turns, for the true pairing and the swapped one. **Rule:** the
  threshold is the midpoint between the lowest true-pair agreement and the highest swapped-pair
  agreement when they separate; if they do not, VR6 always asks (VR-61) and the guide says so.
- **VR-S4 — A framing switch in the preview** (before VR7a's code, only on the owner's yes). How
  long does the preview take to rebuild on a canvas-size change on a 300-clip project (measured by
  toggling `set_canvas`), and does a per-framing plan fit the decoder budget? **Rule:** under 1 s
  on the owner's Mac, the preview rebuilds on switch; otherwise it keeps the last two framings'
  compositions. A framing whose plan warns past 8 decoders is named in the export sheet.

**FC** (paid runs behind `--live --cap`, held to P-6's ledger; an Anthropic key is read only by
`assistant_prompt_eval.py`'s `anthropic_key()`; an AssemblyAI request goes through
`tools/proof/cloud_spike/`'s client with `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` supplied by the owner for that run and
`cloud_live_ledger.py` with its cap; only the owner's own speech is sent, a guest's only with the
guest's agreement, recorded in the spike's README).

- **FC-S1 — Sound Analysis as a signal** (before FC3; verdict FC-30). On macOS 26.5.1, does
  `SNClassifySoundRequest` `.version1` find laughter, applause and cheering in the owner's
  recordings well enough to steer the pool, how fast, and at which window? Inputs: S-EV (with its
  written onset list), at least 10 minutes of speech only (S-TH1 and S-ST1), S-MU, and
  `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`. Runs: windows 1.0, 1.5 and 3.0 s at overlap 0.5, through
  `SNAudioFileAnalyzer` and through `SNAudioStreamAnalyzer` fed by `speechReader`. **Rule:** a
  group is first-class when one threshold t ∈ {0.3, 0.4, …, 0.8}, chosen on the odd-numbered
  labelled events and applied unchanged to the even-numbered ones, finds ≥ 70 % of them (onset
  within ±1 s) and calls at most one window per 10 minutes of the speech-only and music inputs; a
  group with fewer than 10 held-out events is weak by rule. The window kept has the best laughter
  recall among those at ≥ 60× real time, ties to 1.5 s; if none reaches 60×, the slowest
  acceptable is kept and its figure recorded. The stream analyzer is used if its event times
  agree with the file analyzer's within one hop; otherwise the kind's version records which ran
  and FC-31 is amended.
- **FC-S2 — The ranking's request shape and cost** (at FC5's head; cap $3.00; verdicts FC-50's
  constants, FC-51, FC-63). Questions: (a) does the helper with one app tool `submit_ranking`, no
  deferred tool and `fallbacks` off send a request the API accepts; (b) does `countTokens` of the
  request text fit FC-62's estimate; (c) does `claude-opus-5-5` submit a valid ranking first time;
  (d) what does a run cost against the estimate; (e) does the ranker's `cancel` after a valid
  submission leave no further request? Inputs: S-TH1's transcript, S-ST1's when present, two
  public-domain texts cut into timed sentences at 2.6 words a second (sources in the README); S-PC1
  or S-LONG1 only with the guest's agreement. Ten runs at counts 10, 20 and 30. **Rule:** (a)
  passes if no request is refused; if `TOOL_SEARCH` beside one non-deferred tool is refused, FC5's
  diff adds `search: false`; (b) passes if FC-S3's estimate lies within its recorded margin of
  `countTokens` on every input, else FC-S3's constants are refitted on both spikes' inputs; (c)
  passes if ≥ 9 of 10 runs submit a valid ranking (FC-63's checks) on the first call and 10 of 10
  within two, else FC5's diff adds a one-shot `rank` message using structured output and FC6 is
  designed on it; (d) passes if every run's priced cost lies in [`low`, `ceiling`] computed before
  it, and the 10th and 90th percentiles of output tokens per candidate become `output_low` and
  `output_typical`; (e) passes if each run's `cost` events number exactly its submissions.
- **FC-S3 — Sentence ends, recognition speed and transcript size** (before FC4; cap $0.50;
  verdicts FC-41's on-device rule, FC-62's constants, FC-45's accepted limit). S-TH1 (and S-ST1)
  transcribed on device and once by AssemblyAI (one request per file, with `disfluencies` and
  speakers; S-TH1's also becomes FC8a's filler fixture). **Rule:** on-device sentence ends are
  usable if ≥ 80 % of AssemblyAI's sentence ends have an on-device FC-41 end within 0.5 s and the
  sentence counts are within 30 %; otherwise FC-41's on-device arm drops punctuation and ends a
  sentence at a word followed by a non-speech run of ≥ 0.6 s on `MediaSpeech`'s 32 ms grid
  (probability under `defaultVoiceConfidence`), or at a change of track where two voice clips play
  at once, measured against AssemblyAI's ends too, and the window and `find_clips`' notes say
  "Edges are approximate without a cloud transcript." when the scope has on-device words. The
  on-device speed (cold and from TR-14's cache) is recorded as FC-45's figure beside TX-S1's;
  `fixed`, `per_word` and `per_sentence` are fitted by `countTokens` (free) with the largest
  residual as the margin; `claude-opus-5-5`'s `max_input_tokens` is recorded.

**SW.**

- **SW-S1 — What AVFoundation does with several audio tracks and many channels** (at SW3a's
  head). Fixtures: a MOV and an MP4 with video and three AAC tracks of distinct tones (440, 880,
  1320 Hz); the same with three 48 kHz LPCM tracks; one with a 44.1 kHz track; a 6-channel 48 kHz
  24-bit WAV with a tone per channel, without and with a discrete layout; a 6-channel AAC; S-IP1;
  S-MT1 when supplied. **Rules:** (a) **order:** each track k inserted alone and exported as 24-bit
  WAV through Frame Job; if `tracks(withMediaType: .audio)` lists tracks in the container's order
  and every export peaks at track k's tone ≥ 40 dB above every other, stream k is AVFoundation's
  k-th audio track (SW-30), else streams are ordered by track ID and that is recorded (recorded
  beside it, no rule: the LPCM track's export nulled against ffmpeg's `-map 0:a:k`, and the AAC and
  44.1 kHz tracks' exports nulled against an export of the same track extracted with `-c copy`);
  (b) **the tap:** the tap branch (SW-60) only if `prepare` reports six channels in AVPlayer AND
  the export's `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput`, each channel peaks at its own tone ≥ 40 dB above the
  rest in both, and a round trip (a probe tap zeroing all but k, exported through the export's own
  mix read) puts k in both sides within 0.5 dB for every k; else a channel source is a mono copy;
  (c) **the fold:** if today's export puts every tone in both sides within 1 dB of one another and
  of every other tone, AVFoundation's fold stands, else Frame Job folds (SW-61); (d) **cache
  reads:** if `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` in float, non-interleaved, with no channel-count key
  delivers all N channels for the WAV, the AAC and the iPhone's tracks, passes read a channel
  directly, else they read the copy; (e) **writing:** if `AVAssetWriter` writes a `.mov` with video
  and three LPCM tracks read back as three tracks in order, the reversed copy carries every track,
  else a reversed CAF per stream; (f) real files: record each track's codec, channels, title,
  track ID and whether one buffer decodes.
- **SW-S2 — Several 4K angles, a thousand shots, three hours** (SW0, after CJ0a's question 4 is
  answered yes; again at SW9a on the owner's files). Runs on F-4K, made once behind `--build-4k`
  (about 34 GB, 30–60 minutes of encoding; the owner is asked first); `play_preview` plays at most
  60 s a call, so a longer run is consecutive calls summed. **Rules:** (a) **cuts on one
  composition track:** two 4K30 angles of each codec (H.264 100 Mb/s as the GH5 writes, HEVC Main
  10, ProRes 422 HQ) alternating every 2–8 s, five minutes at Full, and a two-minute HEVC 59.94
  pair: ≥ 99 % of due frames composed keeps the plan's assignment, else SW2c is built and (a)
  re-measured on it; (b) **rebuild:** a two-hour timeline of four hidden angle tracks (each twelve
  placements of one ten-minute F-4K file), two microphone tracks and a 1,000-shot program track
  written as package JSON; each rebuild after a `roll`, ten times, from `playback_rebuilds`: the
  median `landed_ms` within 1,500 ms, else the figure goes in the guide and a candidate issue in
  the Performance project (no proxies in this road map); (c) **angles at once:** N = 1…4 angle
  tracks each in a cell of a 2×2 grid on a 1080p canvas, under a full-frame program track at 50 %
  opacity alternating among them every 2–8 s (N + 1 decodes), 60 s at Half and Full: the largest
  N with ≥ 98 % of due frames at Half is the viewer's live cell count (N ≥ 4: four live; 2–3: live
  up to N, the rest refreshed when paused; < 2: every cell refreshed only when paused or after a
  switch); (d) **long files:** time to first frame after seeks to 0:30, 1:00, 2:00 and 2:59 in a
  three-hour 4K file, recorded; on S-LONG1, or a generated file behind `--long` after the owner's
  yes.
- **SW-S3 — Mouth activity on a one-microphone show** (before SW8, after CJ3). On S-PC2 (one
  shared microphone, a camera on each person, a lavalier each), faces from CJ3's `faces` on each
  1080p-or-larger angle; truth is S-PC2's `turns.json`. Agreement over every second the truth
  labels as one person speaking. **Rule:** ≥ 85 % agreement and `faces` at ≥ 4× realtime per
  angle: SW8 is built as SW-81 says; 70–85 %: built with SW-82's hedge; under 70 %: SW8 is not
  built and a candidate issue records the numbers.
- **SW-S4 — The switch's numbers on real speech** (inside SW2a). Fixtures: F-TURNS at bleed −12,
  −18 and −24 dB and floors of −55 and −45 dBFS, and a five-minute excerpt of S-PC1 whose truth is
  its `turns.json` (never the loudness feature SW-21 thresholds). Measured on the excerpt:
  agreement over all single-speaker seconds, and false cuts (shots of a person silent for the
  whole shot). **Rule:** SW-21's and SW-22's defaults are the values that place every synthetic
  cut within τ (SW-27) and, among those, maximise the excerpt's agreement; SW2b ships them when
  the excerpt agrees on ≥ 90 % of single-speaker seconds with no false cut of `min_shot` or more,
  else SW2b shows the bleed row by default and the guide names the case; if NO setting places
  every synthetic cut within τ, SW2a stops, each miss is recorded, and SW-21 or SW-22 (the rule,
  never τ) is amended before SW2b's code.
