**Scope-level decisions of the bets, recorded at CJ0a (their phases' sections hold the rest).**

- **VR-1 — Auto-reframe is in, as analysis plus ordinary actions.** Subjects are found offline by
  Vision's rectangle and saliency requests on the Mac and cached in CJ2a's store; the core plans
  the framing, and the result is placement and actions on the clip. No mask, no shipped model, no
  pixel work outside the one-pass compositor.
- **VR-2 — Bet 3 needs no key.** No VR control is disabled for a missing key.
- **VR-3 — A regenerated copy first; linked versions designed and asked at VR7a.** The planner
  answers a framing path, a similarity per instant from the source canvas to the target; the copy
  composes it into each clip, and linked versions would store it per framing. With a no at VR7a,
  VR7a–VR9 are filed as one issue carrying this design.
- **VR-4 — Subjects are boxes, detected per sample, never tracked by Vision.** Faces come from
  CJ3's `faces`; people (`VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2, `upperBodyOnly` false) and salient
  regions (`VNGenerateAttentionBasedSaliencyImageRequest` r2) from VR1's `subjects`. A fresh
  `VNImageRequestHandler` per sample; no `VNTrackObjectRequest` or other stateful request. Linking
  boxes across samples is the core planner's (CJ-31); masks are out for framing (E9: they flicker).
- **VR-5 — The planner is the core's, and `reframe_clip` is an op (CJ-8 (f)).** Swift measures and
  caches; the core maps samples into clip time, chooses subjects, plans, enforces coverage and
  writes actions, because coverage (VR-7) needs (★) and `fill_scale` and composition into
  existing action ends needs the actions' own evaluation. The op is a pure function of the project
  and the samples handed to it.
- **VR-6 — No nest is made to make room for framing.** Framing is composed into the clip's own base
  and actions; a nest would cost tracks against `MAX_TRACKS` and wall the clip off from blurred
  backgrounds, filler cuts and the transcript.
- **VR-7 — A followed picture never shows the canvas, with three named exceptions.** The window
  lies inside the clip's picture (scale at least fill, offsets clamped by (★)), every key is a
  covering state, and one curve carries x, y and scale, so every frame between keys covers too
  (the covering placements are convex). Exceptions: **`fit` spans** (the whole picture, the canvas
  around it, unless `backdrop` puts a blurred copy behind; a nest clip has none); **motion** (a
  `video.motion` that moves or turns the layer keeps its motion, and the guarantee excludes its
  span — the whole clip for a During motion; `spin` counts as rotation; `fade` is not an
  exception); **opacity** (fades, transitions and opacity below 1 are the author's).

  spelled words of neighbouring phrases; it offers every strike for review and cuts nothing until
  the person removes it. Amends TR-3, AI-6 and W-9** (owner, 2026-11-01, accepting bet 1 with
  the survey's amendment). It finds a **restart** (a phrase whose words are the opening words of
  the next), a **retake** (a phrase of four or more words most of whose words recur, in order, at
  the start of one of the next few phrases, TX-71's numbers) and a **repeat** (one to four words
  said twice in a row); the earlier is struck, the last kept. It reads each word's text lowercased
  with edge punctuation trimmed (TR-8's rule, fillers left out), their order, the pauses between
  them (the voice cache) and sentence punctuation; phrases are compared only within one track and,
  where labels exist, one speaker; one take placed twice (the same media's same source ticks) is
  never a retake. No model reads the words, nothing is sent, no key is needed. A false start that
  repeats no words stays the assistant's, on the person's ask (TR-5). Amending lines: **TR-3**

  comparison of spelled words and offered struck for review; one that repeats no words is found

  person asks (TR-5)"; **AI-6** "a pipeline may strike words for review by comparing their
  spelling, order and timing with the phrases beside them; that is not picking words by meaning,

- **SW-3 — Multicam is in, as a program track over angle tracks.** Synced camera clips (angles)
  stay whole on their own tracks; a program track holds the shots, each an ordinary clip copied

#### Every spike, with its rule

Each rule is fixed here before its run (CJ-7). Instruments go in `tools/proof/creator_spike/`
(CJ, VR, SW), `transcript_spike/` and `retake_spike/` (TX), `cursor_spike/` (CU) and
`cutout_spike/` (CO), probes built through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`; each run's
`results.json` stores `rule_sha256` (CJ-7), the OS build and the compute device. A spike's
verdict is recorded in its phase's record and in the decision it feeds before the phase's code.
Runs that need power run on AC (`pmset` first).

**The analysis set (CJ-S2, CJ-S3, CJ-S4 hold the only rules for device, rate, size, log input,
playback impact and shots; VR1 and CO1 re-run their rows for their own kinds.)**

- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling** (at CJ6's head; decides CJ-9). How many clips can a project hold
  before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096, 8,192,
  16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as packages;
  N above 4,096 needs a scratch Release build with the cap raised, never committed. Measured: (1)
  `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2) `rc_project_from_json` plus
  `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times, median; (4) over MCP, one
  `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo, each from the call to its answer; (5) after
  (4), the time until the next main-thread call (`get_project`) answers; (6) after an edit, the
  time until `play_preview` composes its first frame; (7) a probe that lays out and draws a
  `TimelineView` of N clips offscreen at the fit-all and the default zoom, median of 20; (8) the
  app's resident memory after 50 undo steps of `split`. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N for
  which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms, (4) applies and undoes in ≤ 1 s each, (5) ≤ 1 s,
  (6) ≤ 2 s, (7) ≤ 33 ms at both zooms, and (8) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical memory.
  N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096 and CJ6 ends with
  the verdict and no code.
- **CJ-S2 — Vision on video** (at CJ3's head; decides CJ-30 and CJ-32). On which device, at what
  rate and size, and from which reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate?
  Inputs: the face fixtures always; S-TH1…S-TH4 when they exist. Measured: the cache bytes of
  three runs on each of CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; seconds per minute of source for decode,
  rectangles, and rectangles with landmarks, at long sides 720, 1280, 1920 and native; face recall
  (the share of samples, in spans where a face is known present, with a box overlapping it) at
  each size; recall and reader cost raw against converted on each log or HLG sample; face share
  over S-TH1's first 60 s. **Rules:** (1) **Device:** the fastest of the three whose three runs
  are byte-identical; if none is, the CPU when it meets rule 2's rate; otherwise the fastest, with
  every proof comparing against the cache only. (2) **Rate:** 10 samples a second if decode plus
  rectangles plus landmarks run at least 3× real time on 1080p30 and 1.5× on 4K30 on the chosen
  device; else 5; else 2.5. (3) **Size:** the smallest long side of 720, 1280 and 1920 whose face
  recall is at least 98 % of recall at native size, on the small-face fixture and on S-TH1 when it
  exists. (4) **Landmarks** stay in `faces` if they cost at most 2× rectangles alone; else mouth
  opening is a `mouths` kind on the same grid, built by SW8. (5) **Log and HDR input:** the
  converted reader, unless on every log or HLG sample raw recall is at least 98 % of converted
  recall AND the converted reader costs more than 1.5× the direct one per frame (CJ-S3's figure);
  then face kinds read raw. With no such sample, converted. (6) **Face share** on S-TH1's first
  60 s below 95 % stops VR1 and SW8 until CJ-30 is amended; without S-TH1 the row skips by name
  and is owed in CJ3's record. VR1 re-runs rules 1–3 and 5 for its requests; CO1 re-runs rule 1
  for its mask request.
- **CJ-S3 — The lane** (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23; replaces CO's former CO-S4).
  What does decoding for analysis cost, does a second concurrent picture job pay, and does
  analysis cost playback? On a 4K HEVC 10-bit HLG file and a 1080p H.264 file (synthetic until
  S-TH4 exists): frames a second through the direct and the converted reader at long sides 256
  and 1280; the total throughput of one job and of two; `play_preview`'s composed frames over 20 s
  of a 1080p30 timeline idle and with a `shots` job running. **Rules:** (a) **width:** 2 only if
  two jobs reach at least 1.5× one job's throughput; else 1. (b) **playback:** when composed
  frames with a job running fall by more than 2 % against idle, the picture queue pauses while
  any transport plays and resumes when none does. CJ3 (`faces`), CO1 (`masks`) and VR1
  (`subjects`) each re-run (b) with their own job at their head; the first failure turns the pause
  on for every picture kind, recorded as an amendment of CJ-21. (c) **reader:** converted for
  converting media and direct for the rest, unless CJ-S2's rule 5 says otherwise for a kind.
- **CJ-S4 — The shot signature** (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-24). Which signature, threshold T
  and neighbourhood m find hard cuts inside one flattened clip? Candidates: a 32-bin luma
  histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, and a 4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at long side 256, both by
  L1 distance. Inputs: the shots fixture; a no-cut talking head (S-TH1, else ten minutes of the
  moving-still fixture); flattened exports with known cut lists (the trial's exports when they
  exist, and always a fixture project of 40 clips cut from four `testsrc` variants, exported by
  Frame Job, its cut list read from `get_project`). **Rule:** the signature and T with the highest
  recall on the flattened exports with at most one false cut per 10 minutes on the no-cut input;
  m the largest of 4, 6, 8 and 12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It passes at
  recall ≥ 98 %. If no candidate passes, a 64 × 36 luma sum of absolute differences joins as a
  second signal and the run repeats; if that fails, CJ-24 ships with the measured recall stated in
  the guide.

**TX.**

- **TX-S1 — The fill's cost** (at TX1's head; no owner media needed). How fast does
  `SpeechEngine` recognise long speech on this Mac, can one run cover a whole file, and does a
  fill slow playback? A probe calls `SpeechEngine.transcribe` on `say` phrases joined into 10- and
  60-minute files, and on S-TH1 and S-LONG1 when they exist; it measures wall time, peak added
  memory, temporary WAV size, word count, each word's start against the same audio recognised as
  six 10-minute windows (median and p95 |Δ|), and, in the Release app over MCP, `play_preview`'s
  composed frames over 10 s of a 1080p timeline while a 60-minute fill runs at `.userInitiated`,
  then at `.utility`, each against 10 s idle. **Rules:** outcome A, one whole-file run per media
  (TX-12), if the 60-minute run finishes within 6 minutes and its peak added memory is at most
  1/32 of physical memory; otherwise outcome B, per-clip windows from the playhead outward. The
  fill keeps `.userInitiated` if `play_preview` composes at least 95 % of its idle count during
  it; else `.utility` if that reaches 95 %; else the fill pauses while the transport plays. The
  measured rate replaces "a few seconds per minute" in the guide.
- **TX-S2 — The view** (at TX2a's head). Which view holds a three-hour transcript and leaves the
  transport keys to the editor? Candidates in order: (b) a custom `NSView` laid out by TextKit 2
  (`NSTextLayoutManager` over `NSTextContentStorage`, viewport layout); (c) an `NSTableView` of
  paragraph rows; (a) a read-only `NSTextView` subclass. Fixture: 27,000 synthetic words in 900
  paragraphs with 40 collapsed cuts and 300 strikes, in the offscreen harness on the main thread.
  Measured: first layout of the visible part, a full rebuild after an edit, moving the highlight,
  hit-testing a click, a selection across paragraphs, added memory. **Rule:** take the first of
  (b), (c), (a) that meets: first layout ≤ 200 ms; rebuild ≤ 100 ms; highlight ≤ 2 ms; hit-test ≤
  1 ms; added memory ≤ 1/256 of physical memory; Space and J/K/L reach `handleEditorKey` with no
  change to a frozen file. (a) meets the last only with a change to `handleEditorKey`'s first line
  (`EditorViewController.swift:713`), so it is taken only if (b) and (c) both fail, and that one
  line is recorded as TX-21's deviation.
- **TX-S3 — Cut edges** (at TX3's head). Where should a word's cut fall, when on-device word
  ranges tile the audio and start 270 ms early? Fixtures: (1) `say` phrases joined by silences of
  60, 120, 250, 500 and 1,000 ms (every onset known); (2) the owner's o2
  (`tools/proof/media/filler-sample/`, 29.4 s); (3) S-TH1 and S-RT1 when they exist. Rules
  compared: E0 the transcript's edges; E1 E0 corrected by `CaptionPages.lead(for:)`; E2
  onset-to-onset from the voice cache as TX-30 words it, with E1 as its fallback, at guards of 0,
  32, 64 and 96 ms. Measured: per boundary on (1), a clipped onset and the error against the true
  onset; on (2) and (3), the share of edges in voice-cache non-speech and under −40 dBFS in the
  peak cache. **Rule:** E2 with the smallest guard that clips no onset on (1) and keeps at least
  95 % of real-speech edges in non-speech; else E1 if it clips none on (1); else E0, with JOB-11
  the only judge. TX-30 records which.
- **TX-S4 — The retake rule** (at TX7's head; needs S-RT1, with its `say` twin as the synthetic
  half). Which phrase split, window and similarity find planted retakes and restarts without
  striking the traps? The script and its answer key are `tools/proof/retake_spike/SCRIPT.md`: 8
  retakes, 8 restarts, 6 repeats and 6 traps (an anaphora, "that that", a refrain, a list). Both
  reads are recognised on this Mac; AssemblyAI only if the owner allows the paid run. Grid: pause
  P {0.4, 0.6, 0.8 s}; window K {2, 3}; similarity θ {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8}; one-word repeats {off,
  pause-separated}. **Rule:** among the settings that strike no trap word on either read, take the
  highest recall of retakes plus restarts on the owner's read, ties to the higher θ; if that
  recall is under 80 %, the retake kind ships off by default. If no setting strikes no trap word,
  the retake kind ships off, and restarts and repeats ship on at the setting with the fewest trap
  strikes on both reads together, ties to the higher θ. TX-71 records the setting; its strikes on
  S-TH1 go to JOB-14.

**CU** (CU-S1…CU-S4 run in CU0b; rows whose grant is held by a launched `.app` run in a scratch
hardened-runtime bundle opened with `open -a`; rows that post input skip by name without
Accessibility for the poster, and the owner's one run covers them).

- **CU-S1 — Capture APIs, grants, clocks, the cursor's image.** Rows: A1 a listen-only
  `CGEventTap` (session) for mouse down/up, dragged and scroll, no grant; A2 the same tap for keys
  with no grant, Input Monitoring only, Accessibility only; A3 `NSEvent` global and local
  monitors, the same matrix; A4 `CGEvent(source: nil)?.location` polled at 120 Hz (µs per call,
  whether `CGWarpMouseCursorPosition` moves are seen); A5 `NSCursor.currentSystem` over TextEdit's
  text, a Safari link and a resize edge (identity, hot spot, reps, ms per call with a TIFF hash,
  the safe thread, whether it answers nil); A6 event timestamp against arrival
  `mach_absolute_time`, as ns, mach units and `systemUptime`; A7 keys delivered while the probe
  holds `EnableSecureEventInput()`; A8 whether the signed bundle needs a plist key or entitlement
  for ListenEvent, and whether a tap made before the grant works without a relaunch; A9 hidden
  cursors (a helper's `NSCursor.hide()`, TextEdit's `setHiddenUntilMouseMoves`): what
  `currentSystem`, its image and `CGCursorIsVisible()` report, 10 trials each; A10 a replacement
  for `currentSystem`: two 64 × 64 pt `SCStream`s around the pointer, `showsCursor` on and off,
  differenced, the silhouette's IoU against A5's image, 10 trials over three cursors. **Rule:**
  positions are polled (A4) if a poll costs ≤ 20 µs median and sees warps and real moves, else
  they come from the click source; clicks and scrolls use the tap if it delivers ≥ 99 % of 200
  events with no grant (Frame Job's own windows included), else the monitors if they do, else
  **STOP** (clicks not captured; the owner is asked before CU1a); keys use the tap under Input
  Monitoring alone, else the monitors, and if keys need Accessibility **STOP key capture** (CU6 is
  not built; the owner is asked); the image sampler asks at most 10 times a second plus once per
  mouse-down, `cursor_image=current-system` if A5 identifies another app's I-beam and pointing hand
  in ≥ 9 of 10 trials and its median cost × 10 Hz is ≤ 1 % of one core (≤ 1 ms a call), else
  `none` (no images; the cursor draws as Frame Job's arrow); whatever the verdict, every sample is
  checked for nil at run time, a nil records no change, and a segment whose every sample was nil
  writes `cursor_image: none` and says so on landing; hidden spans are recorded if a signal from
  A9 tells hidden from shown in ≥ 9 of 10 trials in both cases, else not (Hide when idle is the
  remedy); A10 is built only if A5 fails and its IoU is ≥ 0.9 in ≥ 9 of 10 trials
  (`image_fallback=a10`), else the arrow stands and an issue is filed with A10's numbers; the
  event clock is the hypothesis whose arrival − event lies in [0, 20 ms] for ≥ 99 % of events;
  secure input's delivered keys are noted, and the recorder drops keys under
  `IsSecureEventInputEnabled()` either way. Verdict line: `VERDICT positions=<poll|events>
  clicks=<tap|monitor|STOP> keys=<tap|monitor|STOP> cursor_image=<current-system|none>
  hidden=<recorded|not-recorded> image_fallback=<a10|arrow> event_clock=<ns|mach|uptime>
  secure=<withheld|delivered> relaunch=<needed|not-needed>`.
- **CU-S2 — From global points to movie pixels, and the time anchor.** In the picture: record with
  `showsCursor = true` over a flat-colour full-screen window, the burned tip found per decoded
  frame, the cursor warped along a known path, every frame's `SCStreamFrameInfo` and the polled
  samples logged. Separate's exact configuration (`showsCursor = false`, `showMouseClicks = false`,
  420v): the truth is the instrument's own 24 pt marker moved to the warped point at each step.
  Still start: the screen held still 2 s while the cursor moves, then a full-screen colour flip at
  a logged host time, recording which anchor the segment used and its error. Sources: a display
  at Nominal and at Best (2×); the instrument's window moved and resized; a window of odd size
  (1001 × 701 pt at 1×); a picked window; a second display when attached; each in both
  configurations. Candidates: **M1** `pixel = (p − screenRect.origin) × contentScale ×
  pixelsPerPoint + contentRect.origin × pixelsPerPoint`, pixelsPerPoint the configured pixel width
  ÷ point width; **M2** M1 with `scaleFactor`; **M3** a fixed display frame from
  `SCDisplay.frame`; anchors E2, E1 and `DisplayTime` of the first complete frame. **Rule:** the
  mapping is the first of M1, M2, M3 with tip error ≤ 1.5 movie px at p95 on every source row
  (odd window included) over still frames; the anchor is the first of E2, E1, DisplayTime with time
  error ≤ one frame interval at p95 on every row of BOTH configurations (position error ÷ speed
  over moving frames); E1's still-start error over 10 runs ≤ 25 ms at p95, else the limit is
  recorded and the file still names E1. **STOP:** if no mapping passes for window sources, window
  recordings keep the burned cursor and the panel greys Separate for Window; if none passes for
  displays, the bet stops after CU1b; if a candidate passes In the picture but fails Separate,
  In the picture is the default (CU-36). The owner is told in each case.
- **CU-S3 — Do dirty rects locate typing?** Records the instrument's own `NSTextView` while text is
  inserted programmatically, beside distractors (the menu-bar clock, a spinner, a playing
  animation); per burst the median centre of the per-frame dirty-rect bounding boxes against the
  caret rect. **Rule:** pass if within 64 pt of the caret in ≥ 9 of 10 bursts: the file stores each
  complete frame's dirty bounding box and CU7 aims typing zooms at their median centre; otherwise
  nothing about dirty rects is stored and typing zooms aim at the last click before the burst,
  else the cursor's position at its start.
- **CU-S4 — The file's size and speed.** The core's reader prototype over a worst case: one hour
  at 120 Hz (432,000 samples), 3,600 clicks, 20,000 key marks, 40 images, each figure measured
  through a JSON request and answer as `rc_cursor_query` runs it. **Rule:** a JSON body
  (columnar integer µs and points × 100) if the file is ≤ 25 MB, parse and validate take ≤ 300 ms,
  and `state at t` takes ≤ 20 µs median once prepared; otherwise a binary columnar body
  (little-endian i64 arrays after a JSON header), version 1 either way. Smoothing's `prepare` at
  smoothing 1 takes ≤ 1 s on the one-hour file, else smoothing is prepared per 60 s window on
  demand, off the compositor's thread, and the verdict says which.
- **CU-S5 — Motion blur's cost** (before CU11; any time after CU0b). A probe through
  `MetalRenderer`'s pipelines draws one full-canvas layer N times at sub-frame transforms (a 2×
  zoom's middle, eased), accumulated in `rgba16Float`, N ∈ {4, 8, 16}, at 1920×1080 and
  3840×2160, measuring GPU time against the frame drawn once. **Rule:** ship zoom blur at the
  largest N in {16, 8, 4} adding ≤ 4 ms at 1080p and ≤ 8 ms at 4K on the owner's Mac, one N for
  preview and export; **STOP zoom blur** if N = 4 misses either bound (numbers recorded, an issue
  filed). Cursor blur (N sprite samples inside `layerSample`) ships either way.

**CO** (CO-S1 and CO-S2 at CO0; CO-S3 at CO0 when S-KEY1 exists, else at CO4's head; the former
CO-S4 is CJ-S3 (b), re-run by CO1).

- **CO-S1 — Which segmentation, at what rate and read size.** Candidates: person `.balanced`,
  person `.accurate`, `VNGeneratePersonInstanceMaskRequest` with `generateScaledMaskForImage`;
  each at every source frame (capped at 30 a second), at 15 and at 10 a second; frames read at the
  source's size and at a long side of 1920; on the device CJ-S2's rule 1 picks for the mask
  request (the Neural Engine until CO1 re-runs rule 1; a different pick re-measures speed). Truth:
  S-KEY1's keyed composites. Measured on every truth frame against the mask the compositor would
  show there (CO-3's nearest-hold): J = mean IoU of mask > 0.5 against truth > 0.5; B = mean
  |mask − truth| inside an 8 px band around the true edge at 1080p; B on the gesture segment;
  flicker = mean consecutive-mask difference on the still segment; realtime factor at 1080p30 and
  4K30; also S-KEY1's composite re-tagged with a 90° rotation matrix, and the first Vision call of
  a fresh process (recorded, no rule). **Rule:** (a) a candidate whose flicker exceeds 2 levels is
  out; (b) the rate is every frame, unless B on the gesture segment at 15 a second is within 5 %
  of every-frame B (then 15), and again at 10 a second within 5 % (then 10); (c) **Standard** is
  the fastest remaining candidate at ≥ 1.0× realtime at 1080p30 at that rate whose J is within
  0.02 of the best; if none reaches 1.0×, the rate steps down (every frame → 15 → 10) and (c) is
  applied again; if none reaches 1.0× at 10, Standard is the fastest within 0.02 J at 10 and its
  realtime factor is recorded as a risk; (d) **Best** is the lowest-B candidate, kept only if its
  B is ≥ 15 % below Standard's and it runs ≥ 0.25× realtime, else no Best and no Quality control;
  (e) the read size is a long side of 1920 for a larger source when J and B there are within 0.005
  and 2 % of the source size's, else the source size; (f) the rotated composite's J is within 0.01
  of the unrotated, else **STOP**: CJ-23 is amended before CO1 to read coded frames and pass the
  orientation to Vision. Without S-KEY1 at CO0: speed only, on the E9 fixtures and S-TH1 if
  present, Standard = person `.balanced` at the fastest rate (every frame, 15, 10) reaching 1.0×
  realtime; (b), (d), (e), (f) run when S-KEY1 arrives, before CO4.
- **CO-S2 — How the mask reaches the compositor.** A probe compiled from `app/Sources` takes the
  core's plan of a project built through the FFI, adds by hand a mask track whose segments copy
  the picture segments, fills both through `CompositionBuilder.fill`, and reads every frame
  through a probe compositor (a subclass of the class the project would use) that fetches both
  tracks' buffers per request; frame counts from the probe's own `AVPlayer`. Fixture: a synthetic
  movie whose frame k carries its index as a bar code, and mask chunks written from it with
  chunk-relative times by CO-3's nearest-hold rule. Tried: HEVC 8-bit 4:2:0 full range with the
  mask in luma, then ProRes 422 Proxy; chunk lengths 5, 10 and 30 s. **Rule:** the mask track is
  kept when all hold: (1) **registration** — every frame shows the mask of the nearest analysed
  source frame (ties to the earlier in the stream its segment reads), at every-frame analysis and
  at 15 a second, across a trim, ×0.5, ×2, ×1.37 with a chunk boundary inside the segment, a ramp
  across a chunk boundary, a freeze, a reverse (mirrored chunks), a split, a nest, a
  cross-dissolve and an HLG variable-frame-rate source (S-TH4, else an `ffmpeg` HLG VFR fixture);
  (2) **colour path** — the value read differs from the DECODED mask by ≤ 1/255 at every pixel in
  an SDR and an HLG composition under the class each is built with (if the plain class conforms
  the mask, a composition with a mask track is built with `ConvertingCompositor` and (2) is
  measured again); (3) **codec loss** — decoded masks' IoU against Vision's (both > 0.5) ≥ 0.995,
  mean |difference| inside the 8 px edge band ≤ 3 levels; (4) **size** ≤ 15 MB per minute of
  30 fps source at Standard; (5) **playback** — a 1080p30 camera with its mask track over a 4K
  screen recording composes, over 20 s crossing ≥ 5 chunk boundaries, ≥ 99 % of the frames it
  composes without the mask track; (6) **build** — a 60-minute camera cut into 120 clips, every
  one cut out, builds within 100 ms more (median of 10) than without mask tracks. The chunk
  length L is the shortest of 5, 10, 30 s passing (5) and (6) whose per-chunk fixed cost adds
  under 5 % to analysis time per minute; the encoding is the smaller of the two that pass.
  Otherwise the per-media mask pack is measured on (1), (2), (5), (6) and kept if it passes; if

  1080p-or-larger angle; truth is S-PC2's `turns.json`. Agreement over every second the truth

  angle: SW8 is built as SW-81 says; 70–85 %: built with SW-82's hedge; under 70 %: SW8 is not
  built and a candidate issue records the numbers.
- **SW-S4 — The switch's numbers on real speech** (inside SW2a). Fixtures: F-TURNS at bleed −12,

  agreement over all single-speaker seconds, and false cuts (shots of a person silent for the

  every synthetic cut within τ, SW2a stops, each miss is recorded, and SW-21 or SW-22 (the rule,
  never τ) is amended before SW2b's code.

### CJ2a — the analysis lane, its store and reader, and `shots`

- **What a person gets:** nothing visible yet. An agent gets `get_media_analysis` with the `shots`
  kind: the hard cuts in any media or clip.
- **Head:** CJ-S3 and CJ-S4 run; their verdicts are recorded in CJ-21, CJ-23 and CJ-24 first.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **CJ-20 — Analysis is a cache, made on demand.** It never runs at import, is never project
    state, and is never read by the composition plan or the frame recipe; a planner reads it and
    writes ordinary edits. A render drawn from it (CO's masks) is substituted by Swift, as a
    reversed file is (§5.6). No analysis kind bumps the format. The speech cache's import-time rule
    stands for speech.
  - **CJ-21 — One lane, `AnalysisLane`, process-wide, with two queues:** a picture queue (decodes
    and Vision) and a sound queue (audio decodes and Sound Analysis), so a sound job never waits
    behind a face job. Each is its own `DispatchQueue` at `.utility`, never the cooperative pool,
    never `MediaCacheLane`; the picture queue's width is CJ-S3's (1 until it earns 2), the sound
    queue's 1. A job is a source, a window and its kinds; kinds that share a reader, a size and a
    grid decode once (`faces` and `subjects`). Jobs are wanted by owners — a document's command,
    a tool call, an export — as ramp audio's renders are (SR-12): unwanted jobs are cancelled, a
    job wanted again while running is not, `wait` returns on landing, failure or cancellation, and
    an owner's `settled` runs on main. A job takes no `CachePass` and writes only through
    `CacheLedger.publish(in:for: nil)`, so an import pass and an analysis job of the same media
    never cancel or wait on each other. `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>` (`FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` only) holds
    each job before its first frame, polling cancellation every 50 ms. When CJ-S3 (b) turns it on,
    the picture queue pauses between frames while any transport plays, through a new internal
    `BackgroundRender.anyPlaying` over its `transports` (:71).
  - **CJ-22 — The store.** A kind's results for one media are a marker
    `cache/analysis/<kind>/<media id>.json` and a payload folder `cache/analysis/<kind>/<media id>/`
    holding the files the kind names (`shots` a `frames.bin`, `faces` a `samples.bin`, CO's masks
    one movie per chunk and its mirrored chunks, FC's `sound_events` a `windows.bin`). A kind whose
    variants must coexist puts the variant in its name (`masks`, `masks_best`). Every kind has a
    grid on source time — frames by presentation time (`shots`), samples at k / rate (`faces`,
    `subjects`), fixed chunks (masks), windows at k × hop (`sound_events`) — and stores per grid
    point only values that depend on that point's input and a fixed neighbourhood the kind names,
    never on where a job began or what else is cached. Thresholds over time, minimum lengths,
    smoothing and identity are applied when a request is answered, over the requested window. The
    marker holds the `AnalysisStamp`, the payload's files and the COVERAGE: the sorted, merged
    ranges of grid indices stored. A request is a hit when the coverage holds every index of its
    window plus the kind's read margin; otherwise a job runs only the missing ranges, each with the
    kind's pre-roll, and the coverage grows. Payload files are written through a `.partial` and a
    rename, the marker last, all inside `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The
    `AnalysisStamp` is the source's identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no
    path), the kind and its version (Vision request revisions inside it), a digest of the kind's
    parameters, the OS build, the compute device, and the reader's input (`raw`, or the conversion
    as `ConvertedThumbsStamp` records it). A stamp that differs in any field is a miss: the next
    store deletes the marker first, then the payload, and starts empty. Relink, consolidate and
    `set_media_color` therefore invalidate as for every cache. Coordinates are normalised 0…1 in the
    media's display orientation, origin top-left, and every answer carries the display size; times
    are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or reversal reuses them through `SourceMap` and
    `ReverseMirror`.
  - **CJ-23 — The frame reader.** `AnalysisFrames.swift` has a direct reader
    (`AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` over the first video track, 32BGRA, scaled to the kind's long edge,
    turned upright from the track's orientation codes) and a converted reader
    (`AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` over `MediaImporter.oneClip`'s composition at the kind's
    size through step 0, so analysis sees what the person sees; `oneClip`, :311, loses `private`).
    A media whose picture converts (Camera Log, HLG, PQ) is read converted unless CJ-S2's rule 5
    says otherwise for a kind; frames arrive in presentation order, and a sample at k / rate takes
    the first frame at or after it. CO-7 adds a third arm for masks (CO1).
  - **CJ-24 — `shots`: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.** Each frame's
    signature (CJ-S4's) gives two stored values, d1 (L1 distance to the frame before) and d2 (to
    the frame two before); the pre-roll is two frames. When answered, frame i is a cut when
    d1(i) ≥ T, d2(i + 1) ≥ T (a single flash frame returning to the shot is not a cut), and d1(i) is
    the largest d1 within m frames either side, ties to the earlier. A dissolve, whose distances
    stay under T, is not a cut. T and m are CJ-S4's; the read margin is m + 1 frames each side.
  - **CJ-25 — `get_media_analysis {media | clip, kind, from?, to?}` reads any kind, running or
    reusing it.** Exactly one of `media` and `clip`; with `clip` the window defaults to, and is
    clamped to, the clip's played source window, and each time is also answered in clip ticks
    through its source map and the reversal mirror. It runs off main (`creatorOffMainTools`) and
    waits with a bound fixed here from CJ-S3's throughput, refusing past it with a sentence naming
    how much is covered. It answers `kind`, the source window, the display `size`, `cached`, the
    stamp, `run` (`queued_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at` in process uptime, only when it ran a job)
    and the kind's results. An answer is capped by size; over the cap it is refused naming the
    largest window that fits. It is `get_transcript`'s counterpart for pictures and sounds; every
    kind answers through it.
  - **CJ-26 — A canned analysis is honoured only for a proof:** a marker with `"canned": true`
    carries only the source identity and is read only in a `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` build launched with
    `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`, so a planner's proof is byte-exact on any Mac and Distribution never
    reads one.

### CO0 — scope, the record, the tolls' schedule and the spikes

Bet 6 opens here. The cutout phases run in lane C on CJ2a's analysis lane; the layout phases (CO6
on) run in lane B after CU. Nothing in this bet needs a key: person segmentation is Vision on the
Mac and hide-while-silent reads Silero's spans; no CO control or tool is in `ModelKeys.keyed`.

- **What a person gets:** nothing visible; the CO record opened.
- **Decisions (CO-1…CO-9, draft):**
  - **CO-1 — Remove Background uses Vision on the Mac.** Video uses
    `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest`, a FRESH request per frame, on the device CJ-S2's rule 1
    picks for it (CO1 re-runs rule 1), never `.fast` (stateful). Pictures may use
    `VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest` (CO10); video never does (it flickers). This adopts
    #124's D5. A matting model, shipped or downloaded, is allowed by CJ-1 and not built here; it is
    filed as a candidate only if JOB-60's verdict asks for it, and Frame Job being Apache-2.0, a
    GPL-3.0 or AGPL model (Robust Video Matting, Concat's) cannot ship in it.
  - **CO-2 — The cutout is a property of the clip's own layer, not a matte track.** `video.cutout`
    on a media or still clip. A luma matte track holding a rendered mask has no link to the camera
    clip, so a trim, split, slip, speed change, ramp or reverse would slide the outline off it
    (MT-2); a per-layer mask is fetched the way the picture is and follows every edit. Closed
    vocabulary; R5-1 and G-1 stand.
  - **CO-3 — The mask reaches the compositor as a second composition track (provisional on
    CO-S2).** The plan gives each cut-out instance a MASK track whose segments copy its picture
    segments; Swift fills it from the cached chunks. Each mask frame's presentation time is chosen
    so AVFoundation's hold shows, at every source frame, the mask of the NEAREST analysed source
    frame (ties to the earlier): exact at every-frame analysis, nearest at a capped rate. A segment
    crossing a chunk boundary is cut there in source ticks, each part placed by the picture
    segment's own linear map in ticks, converted once (`fill`'s cursor rule). Mask track ids start
    at 2001, so a project with no cutout has a byte-identical plan; they count toward the
    eight-decoder warning. If CO-S2 fails, a per-media mask pack looked up through the picture
    track's own segment mapping replaces this entry before CO2a.
  - **CO-4 — Masks are an analysis kind on CJ2a's lane and store.** Kinds `masks` (Standard) and
    `masks_best` (Best, only if CO-S1 keeps it). The store is CJ-22's:
    `cache/analysis/masks/<media id>.json` with the stamp (no path; the kind's version, the request
    digest and revision, rate, read size, OS build, device). The grid is fixed CHUNKS of L seconds
    of source from 0 (L from CO-S2; 10 s until it reports), each a hit or miss on its own, each
    recording `subject_found`. A chunk's payload is its mask movie
    `cache/analysis/masks/<media id>/<k>.mov`, samples at chunk-relative source times in the source
    track's timescale. A reversed clip's mask is the forward masks mirrored, never a second
    analysis: `r<k>.mov` is chunk k read backwards with each time mirrored through `ReverseMirror`
    (D4-6), made without Vision and published beside it. Masks are in DISPLAY orientation.
    `get_media_analysis {media, kind: "masks"}` answers runs (`from`, `to`, `subject_found`, frame
    count) and the stamp, never pixels. The package carries the folder. Clarifies CJ-22 (one payload
    file per run, in the media's folder); amends CJ5b's CJ-51 (`cache/analysis/` copied whole, masks
    and mirrored chunks included).
  - **CO-5 — "No person found" is decided per clip window.** A clip whose analysed chunks found no
    subject (no mask with ≥ 0.5 % of its pixels above 127) draws uncut, its status "No person
    found"; once any chunk of its window finds one, every analysed frame honours its mask, so a
    person who walks out leaves an empty picture. Swift decides it from the runs' `subject_found`;
    the core never reads analysis (CJ-20).
  - **CO-6 — A frame without its mask draws uncut; a file waits (amends CJ-27).** Pending,
    cancelled and failed chunks draw the clip uncut, never blank and never the slate. An export
    waits for every chunk its range needs through `Exporter.withRampAudio` and fails with
    `cutoutFailed` naming the clip when one fails. `render_frame` and File ▸ Save Frame… wait up to
    30 s for their one frame's chunks, then draw uncut and say so (`render_frame` in a sentence
    before its last; Save Frame in an informational sheet after saving). The eyedropper and the
    look gallery do not wait. A render-substituted kind shows no Analyzing sheet: the person keeps
    editing and the Background section says what is happening. A command that PLANS from masks
    (CO7's centroid) reads only what is cached.
  - **CO-7 — The analysis sees the picture as SDR; the mask is not a colour (amends CJ-23).** A
    converting media is read by `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput`, every frame's presentation time kept,
    and each frame converted through step 0's own pass (`InputPass`) on the GPU — not through the
    one-clip composition, whose frames lose the source's times. The mask is a coverage 0…1
    multiplied in at step 7 like the corner radius and the matte, the same in SDR, HLG and
    linear-light projects; it never passes step 0 (mask track ids never reach `InputStage`; a mask
    buffer is wrapped raw). Which compositor class a composition with a mask track uses is CO-S2
    (2)'s verdict. Any edge refinement reads the picture as the chroma key reads it (`KeyReading`,
    HD-13 (h), HD-20).
  - **CO-8 — Where it is drawn.** The mask binds at `texture(4)` (CJ-8 (b)) on every layer,
    shadow-silhouette, reflection and matte draw, a 1×1 white placeholder when the layer has no
    cutout; sampled at the same DISPLAY-space coordinate as the picture (after the spotlight lens
    and the pixelate snap, before `orientedUV`). `LayerUniforms` gains one group of four (enabled,
    edge, feather, a spare): 132 → 136 floats, 528 → 544 bytes, or 140 and 560 if CU's group lands
    first. The shadow and reflection follow the cut outline (MT-3).
  - **CO-9 — The spikes' rules are CJ0's**; CO-S4 is retired into CJ-S3 (b), which CO1 re-runs with
    a masks job.

### CJ2a — the analysis lane, its store and reader, and `shots`

- **What a person gets:** nothing visible yet. An agent gets `get_media_analysis` with the `shots`
  kind: the hard cuts in any media or clip.
- **Head:** CJ-S3 and CJ-S4 run; their verdicts are recorded in CJ-21, CJ-23 and CJ-24 first.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **CJ-20 — Analysis is a cache, made on demand.** It never runs at import, is never project
    state, and is never read by the composition plan or the frame recipe; a planner reads it and
    writes ordinary edits. A render drawn from it (CO's masks) is substituted by Swift, as a
    reversed file is (§5.6). No analysis kind bumps the format. The speech cache's import-time rule
    stands for speech.
  - **CJ-21 — One lane, `AnalysisLane`, process-wide, with two queues:** a picture queue (decodes
    and Vision) and a sound queue (audio decodes and Sound Analysis), so a sound job never waits
    behind a face job. Each is its own `DispatchQueue` at `.utility`, never the cooperative pool,
    never `MediaCacheLane`; the picture queue's width is CJ-S3's (1 until it earns 2), the sound
    queue's 1. A job is a source, a window and its kinds; kinds that share a reader, a size and a
    grid decode once (`faces` and `subjects`). Jobs are wanted by owners — a document's command,
    a tool call, an export — as ramp audio's renders are (SR-12): unwanted jobs are cancelled, a
    job wanted again while running is not, `wait` returns on landing, failure or cancellation, and
    an owner's `settled` runs on main. A job takes no `CachePass` and writes only through
    `CacheLedger.publish(in:for: nil)`, so an import pass and an analysis job of the same media
    never cancel or wait on each other. `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>` (`FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` only) holds
    each job before its first frame, polling cancellation every 50 ms. When CJ-S3 (b) turns it on,
    the picture queue pauses between frames while any transport plays, through a new internal
    `BackgroundRender.anyPlaying` over its `transports` (:71).
  - **CJ-22 — The store.** A kind's results for one media are a marker
    `cache/analysis/<kind>/<media id>.json` and a payload folder `cache/analysis/<kind>/<media id>/`
    holding the files the kind names (`shots` a `frames.bin`, `faces` a `samples.bin`, CO's masks
    one movie per chunk and its mirrored chunks, FC's `sound_events` a `windows.bin`). A kind whose
    variants must coexist puts the variant in its name (`masks`, `masks_best`). Every kind has a
    grid on source time — frames by presentation time (`shots`), samples at k / rate (`faces`,
    `subjects`), fixed chunks (masks), windows at k × hop (`sound_events`) — and stores per grid
    point only values that depend on that point's input and a fixed neighbourhood the kind names,
    never on where a job began or what else is cached. Thresholds over time, minimum lengths,
    smoothing and identity are applied when a request is answered, over the requested window. The
    marker holds the `AnalysisStamp`, the payload's files and the COVERAGE: the sorted, merged
    ranges of grid indices stored. A request is a hit when the coverage holds every index of its
    window plus the kind's read margin; otherwise a job runs only the missing ranges, each with the
    kind's pre-roll, and the coverage grows. Payload files are written through a `.partial` and a
    rename, the marker last, all inside `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The
    `AnalysisStamp` is the source's identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no
    path), the kind and its version (Vision request revisions inside it), a digest of the kind's
    parameters, the OS build, the compute device, and the reader's input (`raw`, or the conversion
    as `ConvertedThumbsStamp` records it). A stamp that differs in any field is a miss: the next
    store deletes the marker first, then the payload, and starts empty. Relink, consolidate and
    `set_media_color` therefore invalidate as for every cache. Coordinates are normalised 0…1 in the
    media's display orientation, origin top-left, and every answer carries the display size; times
    are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or reversal reuses them through `SourceMap` and
    `ReverseMirror`.
  - **CJ-23 — The frame reader.** `AnalysisFrames.swift` has a direct reader
    (`AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` over the first video track, 32BGRA, scaled to the kind's long edge,
    turned upright from the track's orientation codes) and a converted reader
    (`AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` over `MediaImporter.oneClip`'s composition at the kind's
    size through step 0, so analysis sees what the person sees; `oneClip`, :311, loses `private`).
    A media whose picture converts (Camera Log, HLG, PQ) is read converted unless CJ-S2's rule 5
    says otherwise for a kind; frames arrive in presentation order, and a sample at k / rate takes
    the first frame at or after it. CO-7 adds a third arm for masks (CO1).
  - **CJ-24 — `shots`: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.** Each frame's
    signature (CJ-S4's) gives two stored values, d1 (L1 distance to the frame before) and d2 (to
    the frame two before); the pre-roll is two frames. When answered, frame i is a cut when
    d1(i) ≥ T, d2(i + 1) ≥ T (a single flash frame returning to the shot is not a cut), and d1(i) is
    the largest d1 within m frames either side, ties to the earlier. A dissolve, whose distances
    stay under T, is not a cut. T and m are CJ-S4's; the read margin is m + 1 frames each side.
  - **CJ-25 — `get_media_analysis {media | clip, kind, from?, to?}` reads any kind, running or
    reusing it.** Exactly one of `media` and `clip`; with `clip` the window defaults to, and is
    clamped to, the clip's played source window, and each time is also answered in clip ticks
    through its source map and the reversal mirror. It runs off main (`creatorOffMainTools`) and
    waits with a bound fixed here from CJ-S3's throughput, refusing past it with a sentence naming
    how much is covered. It answers `kind`, the source window, the display `size`, `cached`, the
    stamp, `run` (`queued_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at` in process uptime, only when it ran a job)
    and the kind's results. An answer is capped by size; over the cap it is refused naming the
    largest window that fits. It is `get_transcript`'s counterpart for pictures and sounds; every
    kind answers through it.
  - **CJ-26 — A canned analysis is honoured only for a proof:** a marker with `"canned": true`
    carries only the source identity and is read only in a `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` build launched with
    `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`, so a planner's proof is byte-exact on any Mac and Distribution never
    reads one.
- **Core, FFI:** none.

  `creatorOffMainTools` name), `ProjectDocument+Analysis.swift` (the document's wants, so

### TX3 — delete words

- **What a person gets:** select words by drag, ⇧-click or ⇧-arrows; the timeline shades the cut as

  as one step "Delete Words", from the first word's onset to the next kept word's onset, so the
  pause before the cut stays and the one after it goes (up to 1 s). Words of other clips the cut
  would take are added to the selection first. A selection with a word that cannot be cut, one
  that would leave a locked track's words behind, or one that would pass the clip ceiling is
  refused in its own sentence. A pause token can be selected and deleted (it shortens to 0.2 s
  each end).
- **Head:** TX-S3 runs; TX-30 records its verdict; then TX-31…TX-33.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **TX-30 — A word's cut runs from its onset to the next kept word's onset.** A word's onset is
    the end of the latest voice-cache non-speech run (probability under 0.5, at least two 32 ms
    cells) lying between the previous word's midpoint and this word's midpoint, less a guard G
    (64 ms until TX-S3). Midpoints are lead-corrected (`CaptionPages.lead(for:)`: +270 ms on this
    Mac, −60 ms for AssemblyAI); the previous word is the previous word of the same instance (same
    nest path and clip) and media; a clip's first word's window opens at the clip's start; the
    onset is never before the previous word's lead-corrected end; with no such run (continuous
    speech) or no voice cache, the onset is the corrected transcript start. A run w_i…w_j cuts
    `[onset(w_i), min(onset(w_next), end(w_j) + 1 s))`, w_next the next shown word in timeline
    order (none: `end(w_j) + G`). A word's own `cut_start`/`cut_end` are its run of one, so cutting
    words one at a time and together make the same timeline (except across a pause over 1 s, the
    pause pass's). Snapping is `ripple_delete_ranges`' own. A pause token cuts `[end of the speech
    before + 0.2 s, next onset − 0.2 s)`. TX-S3 may replace E2 by E1 or E0. Risk accepted: in
    continuous speech a fragment of a deleted word can remain.
  - **TX-31 — A word selection is the in/out range, and ⌫ in the transcript ripples.** Selecting
    words sets the document's range to the selection's cut range (`set_range`'s door), so the
    timeline shades what will go and Loop plays it. ⌫, ⌦, Edit ▸ Delete and Edit ▸ Ripple Delete,
    with the view first responder and words selected, send one `ripple_delete_ranges`, step name
    "Delete Words"; the range then clears and the playhead lands at the cut. (⌫ lifts on the
    timeline; deleting text closes the gap.)
  - **TX-32 — The tab refuses a cut before sending it**, in this order: a word that is not editable
    (TX-11's reason); locked words left behind ("Track <name> is locked and has words in this cut:
    unlock it to cut here."); the clip ceiling — the tab counts the clips the cut would leave as
    `check_caps` counts them (the current count, plus one per unlocked-track clip running from
    before a merged range's start to after its end, less one per unlocked-track clip wholly inside
    one), and past `RC_MAX_CLIPS` says "This cut would make <N> clips; a project holds at most
    <RC_MAX_CLIPS>. Lock a track that needs no cut, such as a music bed, or cut less." and sends

### TX4 — cuts the core can list and put back

- **What a person gets:** an agent can put back any cut a ripple made, or any part of one, as one
  undo step. The tab's button is TX5.
- **Room first:** `ReelCore.swift`'s next free ledger block, a doc-only cut gated alone, for
  `ReelProject.cuts()`. `ffi_query.rs` (392 of 400) takes nothing: the export gets its own module.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **TX-40 — A cut is where two clips of one file meet on a track with source skipped between
    them:** A ends exactly where B starts (no overlap; a transition is not a meeting); both are
    `media` sources of one media with the same `reversed`; equal speeds and neither ramped
    (`speed_map::is_ramped`; a ramp's source past its end is not what the cut removed); and
    `B.in > A.in + content_length_in_source(A)`. Its source is `[A.in + content_length(A), B.in)`.
    Its length `D` is the largest `t` with `at + t` on the canvas's frame grid for which
    `timeline_to_source(A.duration + t, speed) ≤ B.in − A.in` — the core's own rounding of the
    product a split makes, so for a ripple `D` is the removed span exactly at any speed and rate
    (29.97 fps's 20,020-tick frame and 7 fps's uneven grid included). `at` is A's end. Nothing is
    stored. Risk accepted: a cut that removed a whole clip, or where two different files met, is not
    a cut; undo brings it back, restore does not.
  - **TX-41 — `restore_cut {at, length, offset?}` puts back `length` of the cut material at `at`,
    starting `offset` into it (0 by default), as one op.** Snapped as `insert_time` snaps
    (`edit_time.rs:454–462`): a negative `length` or `offset` after snapping is an error, a zero
    `length` an identity. Per track, never rippling the timeline: (1) every clip on an unlocked
    track starting at or after `at` shifts right by `length` with its linked partner
    (`shift_clips`), and a clip straddling `at` stays put and whole; (2) on each unlocked track with
    a cut at `at` and `D_t > offset`, the piece is `L_t = min(length, D_t − offset)` long — with
    `offset` 0, A is extended into its handle by `L_t`; with `offset` above 0, a scratch copy of A
    is extended by `offset + L_t`, cut at `at + offset` by `split_clip`, and its second half (a
    fresh id) moved to start at `at`, so its `in`, base props and rebased actions are exactly what a
    ripple of the original's outer parts leaves; (3) when A and its linked partner both gain a
    piece, the pieces are linked by `pair_split_halves`' rule. The result equals the original with
    `[at, at + offset)` and `[at + offset + length, at + D)` rippled out, to the tick. Markers do
    not move. Locked tracks get nothing. A track with no cut at `at` gets a gap of `length` and its

### TX3 — delete words

- **What a person gets:** select words by drag, ⇧-click or ⇧-arrows; the timeline shades the cut as
  the in/out range. ⌫, Edit ▸ Delete or Edit ▸ Ripple Delete takes them out on every unlocked track
  as one step "Delete Words", from the first word's onset to the next kept word's onset, so the
  pause before the cut stays and the one after it goes (up to 1 s). Words of other clips the cut
  would take are added to the selection first. A selection with a word that cannot be cut, one
  that would leave a locked track's words behind, or one that would pass the clip ceiling is
  refused in its own sentence. A pause token can be selected and deleted (it shortens to 0.2 s
  each end).
- **Head:** TX-S3 runs; TX-30 records its verdict; then TX-31…TX-33.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **TX-30 — A word's cut runs from its onset to the next kept word's onset.** A word's onset is
    the end of the latest voice-cache non-speech run (probability under 0.5, at least two 32 ms
    cells) lying between the previous word's midpoint and this word's midpoint, less a guard G
    (64 ms until TX-S3). Midpoints are lead-corrected (`CaptionPages.lead(for:)`: +270 ms on this
    Mac, −60 ms for AssemblyAI); the previous word is the previous word of the same instance (same
    nest path and clip) and media; a clip's first word's window opens at the clip's start; the
    onset is never before the previous word's lead-corrected end; with no such run (continuous
    speech) or no voice cache, the onset is the corrected transcript start. A run w_i…w_j cuts
    `[onset(w_i), min(onset(w_next), end(w_j) + 1 s))`, w_next the next shown word in timeline
    order (none: `end(w_j) + G`). A word's own `cut_start`/`cut_end` are its run of one, so cutting
    words one at a time and together make the same timeline (except across a pause over 1 s, the
    pause pass's). Snapping is `ripple_delete_ranges`' own. A pause token cuts `[end of the speech
    before + 0.2 s, next onset − 0.2 s)`. TX-S3 may replace E2 by E1 or E0. Risk accepted: in
    continuous speech a fragment of a deleted word can remain.
  - **TX-31 — A word selection is the in/out range, and ⌫ in the transcript ripples.** Selecting
    words sets the document's range to the selection's cut range (`set_range`'s door), so the
    timeline shades what will go and Loop plays it. ⌫, ⌦, Edit ▸ Delete and Edit ▸ Ripple Delete,
    with the view first responder and words selected, send one `ripple_delete_ranges`, step name
    "Delete Words"; the range then clears and the playhead lands at the cut. (⌫ lifts on the
    timeline; deleting text closes the gap.)
  - **TX-32 — The tab refuses a cut before sending it**, in this order: a word that is not editable
    (TX-11's reason); locked words left behind ("Track <name> is locked and has words in this cut:
    unlock it to cut here."); the clip ceiling — the tab counts the clips the cut would leave as
    `check_caps` counts them (the current count, plus one per unlocked-track clip running from
    before a merged range's start to after its end, less one per unlocked-track clip wholly inside
    one), and past `RC_MAX_CLIPS` says "This cut would make <N> clips; a project holds at most
    <RC_MAX_CLIPS>. Lock a track that needs no cut, such as a music bed, or cut less." and sends
    nothing (the core's check stays the backstop; `CaptionLayout.swift:288` is the precedent). Any
    shown word the range partly covers is added to the selection first, until nothing is added.
    This bet never raises `MAX_CLIPS` (CJ-9).
  - **TX-33 — An agent cuts words with `ripple_delete_ranges`**, one range from the first word's
    `cut_start` to the last's `cut_end`; no new edit tool; the step is "Ripple Delete" (TR-12).
    Amends TR-11's prompt bullet: "Cutting words: `get_timeline_transcript` answers the timeline's
    words in order, each with the `cut_start` and `cut_end` the Transcript tab cuts it by; cut a run
    of words with one `ripple_delete_ranges` range from its first word's `cut_start` to its last
    word's `cut_end`. `detect_fillers` answers the filler words as ranges. A false start that
    repeats no words is a judgement of meaning, so cut one only when the person asks: say which
    words you will cut, then cut them in one `ripple_delete_ranges` call." TX5, TX6 and TX7 extend
    it, each with its own Amended line.
- **Core, FFI:** none.
- **Swift:** new `TranscriptCut.swift` (pure: onset, `cut_start`/`cut_end`, a run's range, a
  pause's range), `TranscriptCut+Plan.swift` (selection to ranges, the widening, TX-32's refusals,
  the clip count), `TranscriptView+Delete.swift`. Changed: `EditorViewController+Timeline.swift`
  (489; the delete family forwards to the view when it is first responder with words selected);
  `AgentServer+TimelineTranscript.swift` (`cut_start`, `cut_end`, and `pauses[]` with their
  ranges); `AssistantPrompt.swift` (TX-33's paragraph).
- **MCP mirror:** the words' `cut_start`/`cut_end` and one `ripple_delete_ranges` (TX-33).
- **Docs:** `transcript.md` (selecting, deleting, where a cut falls); `editing.md` (⌫ in the
  transcript ripples); `menus-and-shortcuts.md` (the tab's keys); spec §4.3e; §11 TX-30…TX-33 and
  TR-11's line; `app/CLAUDE.md`.
- **Acceptance:** TX-S3's verdict holds on the proof's fixture; one at a time and together give the
  same project.
- **Proof** (`transcript_cut_probe.swift`, `transcript_cut_proof.py`, Release): C1 on the `say`
  fixture every edge in the silence before a kept word, no clipped onset; C2 one at a time and as
  one selection give byte-identical placements; C3 the 1 s cap (a cut before 20 s of B-roll takes
  1 s of it); C4 crosstalk: the other track's overlapping word is selected and cut; C5 a locked
  track's words give TX-32's sentence and no step; C6 a cut past `RC_MAX_CLIPS` gives the cap
  sentence with the predicted count and no step, and one clip under applies with the count equal to
  the prediction; C7 the tab's Delete (`transcript_view` selects, `perform_menu_item` Edit ▸
  Delete) is one step "Undo Delete Words" whose placements equal `ripple_delete_ranges` of the
  read's ranges; C8 two WAV exports decoded to PCM are equal sample for sample — after the tab's
  Delete Words, and after `ripple_delete_ranges` of the read's ranges on the original — both
  through the always-on master limiter.
- **Mutants** (8): guard 0; the 1 s cap removed; start and end snapped in different directions;
  the widening off; the locked refusal off; the fallback without the lead correction; the cap check
  skipped; the count missing the clips spanning a whole range (C6).
- **Manual check:** **JOB-11** — word cuts on S-TH1: no word's start clipped, no fragment of a
  deleted word left, and the pause after a cut sounds natural.
- **Depends on:** TX2a; TX-S3 at its head. **Lane** A.
- **Questions for the owner:** (1) ⌫ ripples in the transcript and lifts on the timeline: right?
  *Recommended: yes* (lifting words would leave black holes). (2) A word selection sets the
  timeline's in/out range? *Recommended: yes.*

### TX4 — cuts the core can list and put back

- **What a person gets:** an agent can put back any cut a ripple made, or any part of one, as one
  undo step. The tab's button is TX5.
- **Room first:** `ReelCore.swift`'s next free ledger block, a doc-only cut gated alone, for
  `ReelProject.cuts()`. `ffi_query.rs` (392 of 400) takes nothing: the export gets its own module.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **TX-40 — A cut is where two clips of one file meet on a track with source skipped between
    them:** A ends exactly where B starts (no overlap; a transition is not a meeting); both are
    `media` sources of one media with the same `reversed`; equal speeds and neither ramped
    (`speed_map::is_ramped`; a ramp's source past its end is not what the cut removed); and
    `B.in > A.in + content_length_in_source(A)`. Its source is `[A.in + content_length(A), B.in)`.
    Its length `D` is the largest `t` with `at + t` on the canvas's frame grid for which
    `timeline_to_source(A.duration + t, speed) ≤ B.in − A.in` — the core's own rounding of the
    product a split makes, so for a ripple `D` is the removed span exactly at any speed and rate
    (29.97 fps's 20,020-tick frame and 7 fps's uneven grid included). `at` is A's end. Nothing is
    stored. Risk accepted: a cut that removed a whole clip, or where two different files met, is not
    a cut; undo brings it back, restore does not.
  - **TX-41 — `restore_cut {at, length, offset?}` puts back `length` of the cut material at `at`,
    starting `offset` into it (0 by default), as one op.** Snapped as `insert_time` snaps
    (`edit_time.rs:454–462`): a negative `length` or `offset` after snapping is an error, a zero
    `length` an identity. Per track, never rippling the timeline: (1) every clip on an unlocked
    track starting at or after `at` shifts right by `length` with its linked partner
    (`shift_clips`), and a clip straddling `at` stays put and whole; (2) on each unlocked track with
    a cut at `at` and `D_t > offset`, the piece is `L_t = min(length, D_t − offset)` long — with
    `offset` 0, A is extended into its handle by `L_t`; with `offset` above 0, a scratch copy of A
    is extended by `offset + L_t`, cut at `at + offset` by `split_clip`, and its second half (a
    fresh id) moved to start at `at`, so its `in`, base props and rebased actions are exactly what a
    ripple of the original's outer parts leaves; (3) when A and its linked partner both gain a
    piece, the pieces are linked by `pair_split_halves`' rule. The result equals the original with
    `[at, at + offset)` and `[at + offset + length, at + D)` rippled out, to the tick. Markers do

- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **CJ-51 — The derived document.** `ProjectDocument+Derived.swift`'s
    `derived(from:handle:range:path:display:)` answers a new untitled document built from a handle:
    `keep_range` applied when a range is given, the handle unchanged when none (VR3's copy). It
    carries the graphics its clips draw plus `fonts/` and `assets/`, through the started
    `GraphicStore` (G-14), and each kept media's caches: peaks, loudness, sync, speech, device
    transcripts, `cache/analysis/` whole (masks and mirrored chunks included, CO-4), a cloud
    transcript with its marker only when its file records `remote_deleted: true` (one still owed a
    DELETE stays in the source, so R6-11 and R6-3 hold, N4), and `cache/reversed/<media id>-<digest>.mov`
    for each kept reversed clip (the digest is over the same media file, so it stays valid, and
    nothing renders a reverse for a windowless document, N5). It never copies media files (a
    derived project points at the source's media; a consolidated source's shorts point into its
    package) nor ramp, isolated or voiced renders (the export waits for and makes them). Copies
    are APFS clones where the volume allows (`clonefile`, `COPYFILE_CLONE`), else copies. With
    `path`, the package is written first so `cache/` lands once; the order is caches through
    `CacheLedger.publish`, then `makeWindowControllers()` (so `startCaches()` finds them current
    and starts no pass), then graphics through the started store (N6). `display: false` makes the
    window controllers (so caches and the graphic store start) and shows no window (N7). (SW-44
    later adds every per-source cache key.)

### VR2b — framing composed into existing actions, and Clip ▸ Follow Subject…

- **What a person gets:** select clips, choose Clip ▸ Follow Subject…, and each picture is framed on
  its subject with eased moves on its action lane, around its zooms and volume points, as one undo
  step. A nudge is an ordinary edit of an action's end on the canvas (CI-13).
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **VR-27 — Compose, or replace.** Compose (the default): the framing path F (scale and offset from
    the source canvas to this one) is composed into the clip's base and into the x, y and scale of
    every action end; holds over an existing action are exact (F is affine in (x, y, scale) and
    commutes with the lerp); the planner schedules its own moves in the gaps between existing
    actions, and a move that cannot fit in a gap is carried by the action it overlaps, approximated
    by that action's curve and still covering. A cut inside an existing action A splits A around the
    cut's one-frame action as `split` narrows a straddled action (`edit_split.rs`'s `state_patch` and
    `narrow_to`, made `pub(crate)`): each head ends at the full evaluated state over every key A
    names, composed with the framing; the tail keeps A's end and curve. A linear A plays unchanged,
    volume included; an eased A is re-eased on each side (counted); an action naming `speed`, or one
    a trim left running past the clip's end, is not split, the cut carried approximately (counted).
    `replace: true` removes every x, y and scale key from the clip's action ends first (an action
    left empty is removed), sets the base to the source canvas's Fit placement, then composes F.
    Follow Subject replaces; Make Vertical composes. The op answers only applied, identity or
    refused, so the counts are recomputed by the command from the two handles.
  - **VR-29 — Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** applies `reframe_clip` with `replace: true` to each selected
    clip with a picture, one undo step "Follow Subject": an `add_track` "Backgrounds" at index 0
    applied first on a pure handle (a refusal stops the command with its sentence, since the grouped
    fold runs on after a refusal), each `reframe_clip` with that track as `backdrop`, and a
    `remove_track` of it when no backdrop was needed. CJ-27's Analyzing sheet shows while VR-12's
    kinds run. The sheet: Follow (Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region, Center), Zoom (100–400 %;
    100 % when the canvas's shape differs from the picture's, 125 % when it matches), Where Empty
    (Show Whole, Center); it remembers Follow and Where Empty (`FrameJobFollow*` keys); the tool reads
    no `UserDefaults` (AU-68 (f)). `-RCDevFollowAccept YES` presses Follow (AU-128's precedent).

### VR4 — captions re-paged and graphics re-laid

- **What a person gets:** the vertical version's word captions fit the narrow frame with every
  correction kept; subtitles and text presets take the narrow frame's measure on any portrait
  project; full-frame graphics (lower thirds, title cards, charts) lay themselves out at 9:16,
  including those inserted before this phase.
- **Toll first:** `CaptionLayout.swift` (581) gives up `// MARK: - Words into cues` (420–581) to
  `CaptionCues.swift`, a pure move gated alone.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **VR-40 — Word caption pages are re-paged from their own words.** A caption track's pages give
    their timed words (tokens, `text.words`, the clip's start); their style is recognised by face and
    `word_style` against `CaptionStyle`, their looks by `word_style`'s keys; the words are paged
    again by the measuring builder through `CaptionLayout.place` with `replacing`, on the new canvas,
    in the same undo step (W-7 and W-10 stand). `place(replacing:)` removes each replaced track with
    its clips first (`CaptionLayout.swift:296`), so a track holding any page whose words are untimed
    or whose style is not recognised is NOT replaced: its pages are `keep` and it is listed.
    `captions: false` leaves captions to the caller (FC9).
  - **VR-41 — Text presets measure by `min(W, H)`, and the Caption preset sits higher on a tall canvas;
    one function, three callers.** `TextPreset.size(on:)` is `sizeFraction × min(W, H)`;
    `position(on:)` is `(xFraction × W, yFraction × H)`, the Caption row using 0.25 of H on a canvas
    taller than wide; the wrap stays 80 % of W. `CaptionLayout`'s Subtitles path (:327, :363),
    `TextPane.apply` (:453, :457) and `TranscribeSheetController+Style.swift` (:213) call them. On a
    canvas at least as wide as tall `min(W, H)` is H, so landscape and square output is
    byte-identical; on a portrait canvas Subtitles from Generate Captions and Import Captions, Text ▸
    Presets and the sheet's preview change. A cue that now measures over two lines is counted.
    Amends **W-7** ("on a canvas taller than wide, the Subtitles cue builder's size is 3.5 % of the
    short side and its line 25 % of H below centre, through `TextPreset`'s functions; landscape and
    square output is byte-identical") and spec §4.3d's text Presets row ("sizes are fractions of the
    canvas's short side, positions of its width and height (§11 VR-41)").
  - **VR-42 — A graphic the size of the old canvas becomes the size of the new one:** `set_graphic
    {width, height}` with its base x and y 0 and scale 1; placement keys in its action ends composed
    by `keep`; every other graphic `keep`. Amends **G-7** ("Make Vertical re-sizes a graphic whose
    size is the old canvas to the new canvas, as an explicit `set_graphic`; `set_canvas` still never
    re-lays out a graphic").

- **What a person gets:** with an In–Out range set, File ▸ New Project from Range… opens a new

  carried, so it opens with waveforms, transcripts and analysis already made. VR3's vertical copy
  and FC's shorts are built on the same door.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **CJ-51 — The derived document.** `ProjectDocument+Derived.swift`'s
    `derived(from:handle:range:path:display:)` answers a new untitled document built from a handle:
    `keep_range` applied when a range is given, the handle unchanged when none (VR3's copy). It
    carries the graphics its clips draw plus `fonts/` and `assets/`, through the started
    `GraphicStore` (G-14), and each kept media's caches: peaks, loudness, sync, speech, device
    transcripts, `cache/analysis/` whole (masks and mirrored chunks included, CO-4), a cloud
    transcript with its marker only when its file records `remote_deleted: true` (one still owed a
    DELETE stays in the source, so R6-11 and R6-3 hold, N4), and `cache/reversed/<media id>-<digest>.mov`
    for each kept reversed clip (the digest is over the same media file, so it stays valid, and
    nothing renders a reverse for a windowless document, N5). It never copies media files (a
    derived project points at the source's media; a consolidated source's shorts point into its
    package) nor ramp, isolated or voiced renders (the export waits for and makes them). Copies
    are APFS clones where the volume allows (`clonefile`, `COPYFILE_CLONE`), else copies. With
    `path`, the package is written first so `cache/` lands once; the order is caches through
    `CacheLedger.publish`, then `makeWindowControllers()` (so `startCaches()` finds them current
    and starts no pass), then graphics through the started store (N6). `display: false` makes the
    window controllers (so caches and the graphic store start) and shows no window (N7). (SW-44
    later adds every per-source cache key.)
  - **CJ-52 — File ▸ New Project from Range… and `new_project_from_range {from, to, path?}`.** The
    menu item needs an In–Out range on the top-level timeline (off inside a nest). The new document
    opens with the range as its first state, with no undo step, named "<source name> (range)" until
    saved; the source document never changes. The tool mirrors it off main, opens the document
    (saved at `path` when given, as `new_project` does) and answers its project and path; it is
    ask-first for the assistant when it names `path` (an AI-7 row: a package written where the
    model chose).

    most 1 s, each track split at every `shots` cut. The primary track has the highest presence ×
    median area × centrality; faces outrank people; a person track containing a face track (the
    face's centre inside the person box in ≥ 80 % of shared samples) is that face's body and yields;

    scoring 25 % higher for 2 s.

    point leaves a dead zone (±10 % of the window's width, ±8 % of its height); a move eases in and

    one's end unless the subject would leave the window; a still subject makes no move (first

### VR2b — framing composed into existing actions, and Clip ▸ Follow Subject…

- **What a person gets:** select clips, choose Clip ▸ Follow Subject…, and each picture is framed on
  its subject with eased moves on its action lane, around its zooms and volume points, as one undo
  step. A nudge is an ordinary edit of an action's end on the canvas (CI-13).
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **VR-27 — Compose, or replace.** Compose (the default): the framing path F (scale and offset from
    the source canvas to this one) is composed into the clip's base and into the x, y and scale of
    every action end; holds over an existing action are exact (F is affine in (x, y, scale) and
    commutes with the lerp); the planner schedules its own moves in the gaps between existing
    actions, and a move that cannot fit in a gap is carried by the action it overlaps, approximated
    by that action's curve and still covering. A cut inside an existing action A splits A around the
    cut's one-frame action as `split` narrows a straddled action (`edit_split.rs`'s `state_patch` and
    `narrow_to`, made `pub(crate)`): each head ends at the full evaluated state over every key A
    names, composed with the framing; the tail keeps A's end and curve. A linear A plays unchanged,
    volume included; an eased A is re-eased on each side (counted); an action naming `speed`, or one
    a trim left running past the clip's end, is not split, the cut carried approximately (counted).
    `replace: true` removes every x, y and scale key from the clip's action ends first (an action
    left empty is removed), sets the base to the source canvas's Fit placement, then composes F.
    Follow Subject replaces; Make Vertical composes. The op answers only applied, identity or
    refused, so the counts are recomputed by the command from the two handles.
  - **VR-29 — Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** applies `reframe_clip` with `replace: true` to each selected
    clip with a picture, one undo step "Follow Subject": an `add_track` "Backgrounds" at index 0
    applied first on a pure handle (a refusal stops the command with its sentence, since the grouped
    fold runs on after a refusal), each `reframe_clip` with that track as `backdrop`, and a
    `remove_track` of it when no backdrop was needed. CJ-27's Analyzing sheet shows while VR-12's

### VR4 — captions re-paged and graphics re-laid

- **What a person gets:** the vertical version's word captions fit the narrow frame with every
  correction kept; subtitles and text presets take the narrow frame's measure on any portrait
  project; full-frame graphics (lower thirds, title cards, charts) lay themselves out at 9:16,
  including those inserted before this phase.
- **Toll first:** `CaptionLayout.swift` (581) gives up `// MARK: - Words into cues` (420–581) to
  `CaptionCues.swift`, a pure move gated alone.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **VR-40 — Word caption pages are re-paged from their own words.** A caption track's pages give
    their timed words (tokens, `text.words`, the clip's start); their style is recognised by face and
    `word_style` against `CaptionStyle`, their looks by `word_style`'s keys; the words are paged
    again by the measuring builder through `CaptionLayout.place` with `replacing`, on the new canvas,
    in the same undo step (W-7 and W-10 stand). `place(replacing:)` removes each replaced track with
    its clips first (`CaptionLayout.swift:296`), so a track holding any page whose words are untimed
    or whose style is not recognised is NOT replaced: its pages are `keep` and it is listed.
    `captions: false` leaves captions to the caller (FC9).
  - **VR-41 — Text presets measure by `min(W, H)`, and the Caption preset sits higher on a tall canvas;
    one function, three callers.** `TextPreset.size(on:)` is `sizeFraction × min(W, H)`;
    `position(on:)` is `(xFraction × W, yFraction × H)`, the Caption row using 0.25 of H on a canvas
    taller than wide; the wrap stays 80 % of W. `CaptionLayout`'s Subtitles path (:327, :363),
    `TextPane.apply` (:453, :457) and `TranscribeSheetController+Style.swift` (:213) call them. On a
    canvas at least as wide as tall `min(W, H)` is H, so landscape and square output is
    byte-identical; on a portrait canvas Subtitles from Generate Captions and Import Captions, Text ▸
    Presets and the sheet's preview change. A cue that now measures over two lines is counted.
    Amends **W-7** ("on a canvas taller than wide, the Subtitles cue builder's size is 3.5 % of the
    short side and its line 25 % of H below centre, through `TextPreset`'s functions; landscape and
    square output is byte-identical") and spec §4.3d's text Presets row ("sizes are fractions of the
    canvas's short side, positions of its width and height (§11 VR-41)").
  - **VR-42 — A graphic the size of the old canvas becomes the size of the new one:** `set_graphic
    {width, height}` with its base x and y 0 and scale 1; placement keys in its action ends composed
    by `keep`; every other graphic `keep`. Amends **G-7** ("Make Vertical re-sizes a graphic whose
    size is the old canvas to the new canvas, as an explicit `set_graphic`; `set_canvas` still never
    re-lays out a graphic").
  - **VR-43 — A bundled template lays itself out inside any canvas:** the six that measure by
    `ctx.height / 1080` (`lower-third`, `title-card`, `callout`, `bar-chart`, `counter`,

    cuts on the stacked cameras make two to three clips per shot where the program track makes one (a

    at a time.

    each range's ends onto `track` at the same times, with fresh ids. `ranges` are project times,
