### SW2a — the switch's planner and its numbers

- **What a person gets:** nothing visible: the planner that decides the cuts, its readings off the
  document, and defaults tuned on real speech.
- **Head (inside the phase, once the planner exists):** SW-S4 runs; SW-21's and SW-22's defaults
  recorded.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **SW-20 — The inputs.** Angles are tracks (SW-13): each track holding a selected media clip with
    pictures, two to nine. A microphone is a track: by default each track holding a selected sound
    clip whose MEDIA has no pictures; a camera's own sound counts only when no picture-less sound clip
    is selected (then each angle whose clips play sound is its own microphone); a camera's detached
    sound only when picked in the sheet's Microphone popup or named by the tool. Speakers are pairs of
    a microphone and an angle; by default a microphone that is itself an angle pairs with itself and
    the others pair, front to back, with the remaining angles; the wide is the one angle no microphone
    names, when exactly one is left. The range is the In/Out range, else the first selected angle
    clip's start to the last one's end. A microphone's steps outside its clips are silent. The switch
    trusts the placement and does not check sync (the guide says to run Synchronize Audio first).
  - **SW-21 — A microphone is active when its voice is its own.** On a 10 ms grid, for each microphone
    m: its level ℓ_m(k) is 10·log10 of the loudness cache's K-weighted mean square through the clip's
    channel matrix (AU-35) and source map, averaged over a CENTRED 100 ms window (k − 5 to k + 4); its
    voice v_m(k) the speech cache's probability for the 32 ms chunk at that step; P_m the 90th
    percentile of ℓ_m over v_m ≥ 0.5; F_m the 10th percentile over v_m < 0.5. m is active when
    v_m(k) ≥ 0.5, ℓ_m(k) ≥ P_m − `bleed_db` (15 dB) and ℓ_m(k) ≥ F_m + 6 dB; when two or more are
    active and one's ℓ − P exceeds every other's by `dominance_db` (8 dB), only it is. Provisional
    until SW-S4.
  - **SW-22 — Turns become shots.** One active microphone is that person, two or more crosstalk, none
    nobody. A turn bridges gaps under 0.5 s; a turn under `min_turn` (1.0 s) starts no shot; crosstalk
    of `crosstalk_min` (1.0 s) or more shows the wide, or holds the current shot without a wide or with
    `crosstalk: hold`; nobody holds the current shot; a shot starts `lead` (0.2 s) before the turn's
    first active step, frame-snapped; a shot whose angle does not cover its span goes to the wide when
    it covers, else extends the shot before; a shot under `min_shot` (2.0 s) merges into the one before
    (the first into the one after); the range opens on the wide when there is one; optional
    `wide_after` (off) cuts to the wide for `min_shot` once one person has held the screen that long.
  - **SW-24 — It refuses, naming every reason at once (SY-1's form):** fewer than two angles; a speaker
    without a microphone; one microphone for two or more speakers ("each person needs their own
    microphone" until SW8); a microphone whose loudness or speech is still being analysed; one with no
    speech found; a stretch no angle covers ("no angle has a picture between A and B"); a result past
    the clip ceiling ("Switch by Speaker would add N clips to M; the most is {RC_MAX_CLIPS} — raise the
    minimum shot", read from the header's define).
  - **SW-25 — The switch reads caches and computes nothing else;** the planner is a pure function in
    `SpeakerSwitch.swift`, probe-callable.
  - **SW-27 — The proof's speech is made on the Mac, its truth measured.** Samantha and Daniel (`say
    -v`) read a scripted turn table (skips by name without either); each voice's SOLO stem is written
    before mixing; each microphone is its speaker at 0 dB plus the other at a set bleed plus pink
    noise; a turn's onset is the first sample of its solo stem above −40 dBFS; a cut passes when on
    the frame grid and within τ of onset − `lead`, τ = 64 ms (two VAD chunks) + 50 ms (half the window)
    + one frame (about 147 ms at 30 fps).
- **Swift:** new `SpeakerSwitch.swift` (pure: SW-20's defaults and pairing, SW-21, SW-22, SW-24),
  `SpeakerSwitch+Read.swift` (readings off the document, AudioSync's `read`), `ClipLevelSeries.swift`
  (a clip's 10 ms level series through `ClipLoudness.ChannelMatrix` and its source map, the centred
  window); the generator `tools/proof/creator_spike/f_turns.py` (F-TURNS).
- **MCP:** none yet.
- **Docs:** SW-21's and SW-22's defaults and SW-S4's record here.
- **Acceptance:** `make gate`; SW-S4 recorded; the probe PASS.
- **Proof** (`switch_speaker_probe.swift`, scored by `switch_speaker_probe.py`): R1 SW-21 over synthetic
  series, each threshold at its edge, the centred window; R2 SW-22's turns, merges, lead and the

  - **CO-60 — A layout is a placement of the camera and the screen, solved by the core.** Five:
    `corner` (shape `square`, `rounded` or `circle`; corner `bottom_right` by default; the box is
    CAM-10 (3)'s — a quarter of the canvas wide, a third tall, inset 5 % of each axis; `square` and
    `rounded` fit the camera's aspect in it, `circle` a square crop with the radius half its side,
    `rounded`'s radius 8 % of the box's shorter side); `side_by_side` (the camera in the right third,
    the screen fitted in the left two-thirds, a margin of 4 % of the canvas's shorter side round and
    between them, a 2 % radius on each); `stacked` (the screen fitted to the full width less the
    margins at the top, the camera filling the rest below, cropped to it); `camera_full` (the camera
    at `fill_scale`); `screen_only` (the camera's opacity 0). In every layout but `side_by_side` and
    `stacked` the screen takes its FULL placement — the one `add_clip` gives a new clip of its media:
    centred, `fit_scale`'s scale (honouring `canvas.fit_new_clips`, never scaling up), uncropped,
    square-cornered, opaque. A layout writes x, y, scale, crop, corner radius and opacity on each
    role, all six always, and nothing else. Every number is in `core/src/layout.rs`.
  - **CO-61 — A switch is a layout action, and it holds until the next one.** `switch_layout`
    writes, per role, one LAYOUT ACTION on the clip of that role under `at`, of `duration` (0.5 s,
    `ease_in_out`, at least one frame) from `at`; or, when `at` is the clip's first frame, the layout
    as the clip's base props plus a one-frame layout action at its start whose end equals them (a
    cut, recognisable by content). The REACH runs from `at` to the start of the first later layout
    action on that role's track, or to `through` when given and earlier, or to the track's end;
    every role clip STARTING inside the reach takes the layout as its base props; a clip whose own
    layout action starts after its first frame takes the new base for its head and keeps that action.
    One op, one undo step, "Camera Layout".
  - **CO-62 — A switch never fights a zoom.** Inside the reach and at or after `at`, a role clip
    holding a zoom action or another action that MOVES it (an end naming any of the six keys that is
    not a layout action) is refused by name: "The screen clip at 1:02 zooms (action 2); nest the
    screen's clips so the layout moves the nest and the zoom stays inside it." `switch_layout {nest:
    true}` nests each such role's clips in the reach first, in the same step (R5-3's precedent: a
    structural change only when a person said yes or an agent named it). An earlier layout action is
    never a reason to refuse. A nest-clip camera refuses `circle` and `rounded` (a nest clip cannot
    draw a radius, `nest.rs:382–394`); `side_by_side` and `stacked` write their 2 % radius on a nest
    clip, which draws square corners (a recorded limit).
  - **CO-63 — Actions are classed by content, with no tag** (CU-5): `action_class.rs` (CJ-8 (i), CU7

    group or `speed`; a LAYOUT ACTION names all six; an action MOVES its clip when its `video` names
    any of the six. A layout action is never a zoom, so Auto Zoom's Replace never removes one.

- **What a person gets:** Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ on a shot lists the camera tracks that cover it and

- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **SW-10 — The switch writes a program track; it does not cut the cameras in place.** Picture-only
    cuts on the stacked cameras make two to three clips per shot where the program track makes one (a
    four-camera three-hour show at 8 s shots is about 5,400 against 1,350, past `MAX_CLIPS`); moving
    one cut there is trimming pieces on several tracks, here an ordinary roll; both decode one camera
    at a time.
  - **SW-11 — `copy_pieces {clip, track, ranges, video?, audio?}`** copies the pieces of `clip` between
    each range's ends onto `track` at the same times, with fresh ids. `ranges` are project times,
    each end snapped as `split` snaps; sorted, not overlapping, inside the clip. `video` and `audio`,
    when given, set each piece's `enabled` switches. Refused in its own sentence: a nest clip ("clip N
    is a nest: a piece of it would replay the nest from its first frame"); a range outside the clip;
    overlapping ranges; a locked destination; a destination holding a clip over a range ("track T
    holds clip C between A and B"). `Err` for an unknown clip or track; an empty `ranges` an
    identity. A copy has no transition and its link is cleared. Allowed inside a nest.
  - **SW-12 — A piece is exactly the middle a `split` at its two ends would leave:** source window,
    a ramp's map and rate (SR-18), its actions clipped, a graphic's `in` and `length` (G-9), its words
    rebased (W-3), all from `split_clip`'s own arithmetic on a scratch copy (`edit_split.rs:95`).
  - **SW-13 — An angle is a TRACK; Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ re-picks one shot.** A track COVERS a span
    when its media clips with pictures together leave no part of it uncovered (a clip with its
    picture off or on a hidden track still counts). The submenu lists, for the one selected clip,
    every other track of its container covering the clip's whole span, front first, by name, up to

    crosses, as one step "Switch Angle". `switch_angle {clip, angle}` does the same and refuses an

### SW2a — the switch's planner and its numbers

- **What a person gets:** nothing visible: the planner that decides the cuts, its readings off the
  document, and defaults tuned on real speech.
- **Head (inside the phase, once the planner exists):** SW-S4 runs; SW-21's and SW-22's defaults
  recorded.
- **Decisions (draft):**
  - **SW-20 — The inputs.** Angles are tracks (SW-13): each track holding a selected media clip with
    pictures, two to nine. A microphone is a track: by default each track holding a selected sound
    clip whose MEDIA has no pictures; a camera's own sound counts only when no picture-less sound clip
    is selected (then each angle whose clips play sound is its own microphone); a camera's detached
    sound only when picked in the sheet's Microphone popup or named by the tool. Speakers are pairs of
    a microphone and an angle; by default a microphone that is itself an angle pairs with itself and
    the others pair, front to back, with the remaining angles; the wide is the one angle no microphone
    names, when exactly one is left. The range is the In/Out range, else the first selected angle
    clip's start to the last one's end. A microphone's steps outside its clips are silent. The switch
    trusts the placement and does not check sync (the guide says to run Synchronize Audio first).
  - **SW-21 — A microphone is active when its voice is its own.** On a 10 ms grid, for each microphone
    m: its level ℓ_m(k) is 10·log10 of the loudness cache's K-weighted mean square through the clip's
    channel matrix (AU-35) and source map, averaged over a CENTRED 100 ms window (k − 5 to k + 4); its
    voice v_m(k) the speech cache's probability for the 32 ms chunk at that step; P_m the 90th
    percentile of ℓ_m over v_m ≥ 0.5; F_m the 10th percentile over v_m < 0.5. m is active when
    v_m(k) ≥ 0.5, ℓ_m(k) ≥ P_m − `bleed_db` (15 dB) and ℓ_m(k) ≥ F_m + 6 dB; when two or more are
    active and one's ℓ − P exceeds every other's by `dominance_db` (8 dB), only it is. Provisional
    until SW-S4.
  - **SW-22 — Turns become shots.** One active microphone is that person, two or more crosstalk, none
    nobody. A turn bridges gaps under 0.5 s; a turn under `min_turn` (1.0 s) starts no shot; crosstalk
    of `crosstalk_min` (1.0 s) or more shows the wide, or holds the current shot without a wide or with
    `crosstalk: hold`; nobody holds the current shot; a shot starts `lead` (0.2 s) before the turn's
    first active step, frame-snapped; a shot whose angle does not cover its span goes to the wide when
    it covers, else extends the shot before; a shot under `min_shot` (2.0 s) merges into the one before
    (the first into the one after); the range opens on the wide when there is one; optional
    `wide_after` (off) cuts to the wide for `min_shot` once one person has held the screen that long.
  - **SW-24 — It refuses, naming every reason at once (SY-1's form):** fewer than two angles; a speaker
    without a microphone; one microphone for two or more speakers ("each person needs their own
    microphone" until SW8); a microphone whose loudness or speech is still being analysed; one with no
    speech found; a stretch no angle covers ("no angle has a picture between A and B"); a result past
    the clip ceiling ("Switch by Speaker would add N clips to M; the most is {RC_MAX_CLIPS} — raise the
    minimum shot", read from the header's define).
  - **SW-25 — The switch reads caches and computes nothing else;** the planner is a pure function in
    `SpeakerSwitch.swift`, probe-callable.
  - **SW-27 — The proof's speech is made on the Mac, its truth measured.** Samantha and Daniel (`say
    -v`) read a scripted turn table (skips by name without either); each voice's SOLO stem is written
    before mixing; each microphone is its speaker at 0 dB plus the other at a set bleed plus pink
    noise; a turn's onset is the first sample of its solo stem above −40 dBFS; a cut passes when on
    the frame grid and within τ of onset − `lead`, τ = 64 ms (two VAD chunks) + 50 ms (half the window)
    + one frame (about 147 ms at 30 fps).
- **Swift:** new `SpeakerSwitch.swift` (pure: SW-20's defaults and pairing, SW-21, SW-22, SW-24),
  `SpeakerSwitch+Read.swift` (readings off the document, AudioSync's `read`), `ClipLevelSeries.swift`
  (a clip's 10 ms level series through `ClipLoudness.ChannelMatrix` and its source map, the centred
  window); the generator `tools/proof/creator_spike/f_turns.py` (F-TURNS).
- **MCP:** none yet.
- **Docs:** SW-21's and SW-22's defaults and SW-S4's record here.
- **Acceptance:** `make gate`; SW-S4 recorded; the probe PASS.
- **Proof** (`switch_speaker_probe.swift`, scored by `switch_speaker_probe.py`): R1 SW-21 over synthetic
  series, each threshold at its edge, the centred window; R2 SW-22's turns, merges, lead and the
  hand-off to the wide; R3 SW-24's refusals as one list, the ceiling from `RC_MAX_CLIPS`; R4 SW-20's
  defaults (picture-less files are the microphones; with none, each camera its own; a detached camera
  sound never a default); R5 a two-file angle covers its join, and a gap in every angle is refused
  naming it; R6 over F-TURNS' readings every cut within τ.
- **Mutants** (5): the bleed test removed (R1); the dominance test removed (R1); a trailing window
  (R6); a short shot merged into the next (R2); a camera's own sound taken beside picture-less files
  (R4).
- **Manual checks:** none. **Depends on:** SW1. **Lane** C.

  of crosstalk) as SW-S4 tunes them? *Recommended: yes.*

## Risks

- **Vision moves under the app.** An OS update or another compute device changes Vision's answers; the
  stamp makes that a re-analysis rather than a mix, a request revision is a kind-version bump, and
  proofs read caches. The fixture faces ship with macOS and could change; their hashes fail by name.
- **Analysis competes with playback, export and `AUSoundIsolation`'s renders.** The picture queue runs
  at width 1 and `.utility` until CJ-S3 earns more, and pauses while playing if CJ-S3 (b) fails for any
  kind; an export waiting on masks is slower, accepted.
- **Real speech defeats word timing.** On-device ranges tile the audio and start 270 ms early, and
  continuous speech has no non-speech to cut in; TX-S3 decides the edge rule and JOB-11 judges it, a
  fragment of a deleted word can remain, and on-device sentence ends may fail FC-S3 (then edges come
  from pauses and are labelled approximate).
- **The first fill and the first analysis take minutes.** A multi-hour, multi-microphone project is
  read whole once per media (TX-12), a long file barely used is read whole, a macOS update re-runs every
  fill, and `find_clips` and `get_timeline_transcript` hold the agent lane meanwhile (AI-2); masks of an
  hour of camera may be an hour of background work (CO-S1).
- **The clip ceiling and undo memory.** Every word cut adds a clip per unlocked track; a long show
  switched every few seconds approaches 4,096; each edit keeps a whole project handle. TX and SW count
  against `RC_MAX_CLIPS` and refuse first; CJ-S1 measures whether the ceiling can rise. Remove Struck of
  hundreds of ranges may be slow (V8 records it; a slow figure is filed, not fixed).
- **What restore cannot bring back.** Only material where one file's clip meets itself across a cut: a
  title or caption page wholly inside the cut is gone, a ramped clip's cut is not a cut, halves are never
  re-merged; undo is the exact path.
- **Retake and auto-cut distrust.** Deliberate repetition is struck (every strike is reviewed, TX-S4's
  traps bound it); generated zooms, framings and switches are subjective (survey D16, D17). Every result
  is ordinary edits the person can change, Replace is off by default, and the trials set the defaults.
- **Ranking quality is the whole of Find Clips**, and prompt changes after FC9's trial cost paid runs.

  `xfade` dissolve and one single white frame; a 40-clip fixture project exported by Frame Job as a
  flattened clip, its cut list from `get_project` (CJ-S4, CJ2a, CJ2b).
- **Faces:** frames from `/System/Library/Photos/Resources/FlexAudio/` (the album covers macOS ships),
  read in place at proof time, each source's SHA-256 recorded and a missing one a scored failure naming
  its path: the moving still (a frontal face moved across 1920 × 1080 at a known speed), the small face
  (an eighth of the frame's height), the two-face fixture (the two-person cover, then one face leaving)
  and a portrait-rotated copy (CJ-S2, CJ3, VR1); the moving still with a Camera Log set (the converting
  fixture).
- **Canned analyses** (CJ-26): `faces` and `subjects` with known motion — a face panned for 20 s, leaving
  for 2 s and returning, two faces 400 px then 1,400 px apart, a still face, known cuts, a no-subject
  screen (VR2a–VR6, SW8); `masks` chunks carrying CO-S2's bar code (CO2a–CO5).
- **Masks:** a moving disc as a mask sequence; CO-S2's bar-code movie; the E9 fixtures
  (`vision_fixtures.sh`, the slow push-in, the no-person UI scroll, a rotation-tagged push-in); Apple
  Log, HLG and HLG VFR `ffmpeg` fixtures.
- **Cursor:** hand-written cursor files in `core/tests/fixtures/cursor/` (paths, clicks in visits, scroll
  bursts, shortcuts, repeats and near pairs, typing around shortcuts, hidden spans, a newer version, a

  `testsrc2` movie at 2880×1800, 60 fps, no cursor, with its cursor file and a 48 kHz speech
  microphone, and a twin with the sprite burned in at the file's positions (L8).
- **Words:** `say` phrases joined by known silences (TX-S3, TX3, TX6); 10 and 60 minutes of joined `say`
  speech (TX-S1); S-RT1's script read by `say` (TX-S4, TX7); a 27,000-word transcript injected as a
  device cache (TX-S2, TX2a); `say` speech with known sentences, gaps, two voices on two tracks and one
  voice duplicated on two tracks (FC4); public-domain texts as timed transcripts (FC-S2).
- **Stand-ins:** `assemblyai_fake.py` (punctuation, speakers, disfluencies, both `remote_deleted`
  values) and `anthropic_fake.py` (scripted submissions, a refusal, a hostile title, a chosen or failing
  model window); key states — an empty and a dummy-key `-RCSecretFolder` (CJ1, TX6, TX7, FC7a, FC7b).
- **Audio streams:** F-TURNS (Samantha and Daniel on a scripted turn table, solo stems and measured
  onsets, bleed at −12/−18/−24 dB and pink noise at −55/−45 dBFS, three 1080p colour-card cameras with a
  16-block binary frame code, one camera as two abutting files); F-MULTITRACK (MOV, MP4 and MKV with
  three audio tracks of distinct tones and speech placements, 48 kHz LPCM, 44.1 kHz, one undecodable);
  F-POLY (a 6-channel 48 kHz 24-bit WAV with and without a layout, and a 6-channel AAC); F-SPLIT (one
  voice per side with bleed); F-4K (about 34 GB, only behind `--build-4k`).
- **Projects built over MCP:** a duplicated track, a nest, a nest shown twice and one trimmed short, a
  transition, a locked track, a ramp, a reversed clip, a detached pair, a music bed and a caption clip
  across a cut, a project one cut short of `RC_MAX_CLIPS`, generated packages of N clips (CJ-S1).

**How Vision-dependent proofs stay deterministic:** (1) a planner's rows run on canned analyses and
assert bytes; (2) Vision's rows on fixtures and samples assert tolerances fixed before the run, never
exact numbers; (3) a determinism row compares two runs on the pinned device byte for byte; (4) a proof
compares against the cache, never a recomputation; (5) every stamp and results file carries the OS
build, the compute device and the reader's input; (6) stored values depend on one grid point, so an
answer never depends on call order (CJ2a's A9); (7) what only a person can judge — whether a reframe, a
cutout or a switch looks right on real footage — is a JOB row.

## Risks

- **Vision moves under the app.** An OS update or another compute device changes Vision's answers; the
  stamp makes that a re-analysis rather than a mix, a request revision is a kind-version bump, and
  proofs read caches. The fixture faces ship with macOS and could change; their hashes fail by name.
- **Analysis competes with playback, export and `AUSoundIsolation`'s renders.** The picture queue runs
  at width 1 and `.utility` until CJ-S3 earns more, and pauses while playing if CJ-S3 (b) fails for any
  kind; an export waiting on masks is slower, accepted.
- **Real speech defeats word timing.** On-device ranges tile the audio and start 270 ms early, and
  continuous speech has no non-speech to cut in; TX-S3 decides the edge rule and JOB-11 judges it, a
  fragment of a deleted word can remain, and on-device sentence ends may fail FC-S3 (then edges come
  from pauses and are labelled approximate).
- **The first fill and the first analysis take minutes.** A multi-hour, multi-microphone project is
  read whole once per media (TX-12), a long file barely used is read whole, a macOS update re-runs every
  fill, and `find_clips` and `get_timeline_transcript` hold the agent lane meanwhile (AI-2); masks of an
  hour of camera may be an hour of background work (CO-S1).
- **The clip ceiling and undo memory.** Every word cut adds a clip per unlocked track; a long show
  switched every few seconds approaches 4,096; each edit keeps a whole project handle. TX and SW count
  against `RC_MAX_CLIPS` and refuse first; CJ-S1 measures whether the ceiling can rise. Remove Struck of
  hundreds of ranges may be slow (V8 records it; a slow figure is filed, not fixed).
- **What restore cannot bring back.** Only material where one file's clip meets itself across a cut: a
  title or caption page wholly inside the cut is gone, a ramped clip's cut is not a cut, halves are never
  re-merged; undo is the exact path.
- **Retake and auto-cut distrust.** Deliberate repetition is struck (every strike is reviewed, TX-S4's
  traps bound it); generated zooms, framings and switches are subjective (survey D16, D17). Every result
  is ordinary edits the person can change, Replace is off by default, and the trials set the defaults.
- **Ranking quality is the whole of Find Clips**, and prompt changes after FC9's trial cost paid runs.
  Sound Analysis may be weak on real podcasts and music beds (FC-30 can demote a group to weak); a
  classifier refusal ends a run with its cost; an eight-hour VOD passes FC-62's limit and is refused.
- **Text leaves the Mac at Rank** (and only then), and a guest's recording may still need the guest's
  consent; the window and the guide say so.
- **The key rule may surprise.** With neither a key nor a cached transcript, Remove Filler Words is
  greyed with a tooltip where a sheet once explained itself; whether macOS shows a disabled menu item's
  tooltip is checked at CJ1's head.
- **Input Monitoring and key data.** The grant is attributed to the terminal for a shell launch and may
  need a relaunch (CU-S1, JOB-23); keystroke times leak from a password field that does not enable secure
  input (no character is stored; JOB-24 shows it); an ad-hoc build loses the grant at every `make app`,
  so granted proof tiers skip by name and every mutant has an ungranted killer.
- **`NSCursor.currentSystem` will answer nil in a future macOS.** A nil is checked per sample and the
  arrow drawn; CU-S1 measures a replacement, built only if needed.
- **A lost cursor file leaves a Separate recording with no pointer.** Consolidate, Relink, the Media
  tab, `cursor_warnings` and In the picture mitigate it. E1's fallback timing (about 21 ms) is used for
  still-start Separate segments; window occlusion is not sampled; hidden cursors may not be detectable.
- **Mask edges, misses and size.** Vision's 512×384 masks may look cut with scissors on hair and fast
  hands (JOB-60 decides whether a matting-model candidate is filed, which must carry a licence an
  Apache-2.0 app can ship); backlit, from-behind and small figures are missed; a composition must not
  colour-manage a mask frame (CO-S2 (2)); each cut-out instance adds a decode and each chunk an asset per
  build (CO-S2 (5), (6)); GPU and Neural Engine masks differ by up to 25 levels across Macs.
- **Layouts against existing placement.** A switch rewrites the base placement of role clips up to the
  next layout action; hand placement there is overwritten unless `through` bounds the reach; zooms in
  the reach are refused and nested, and a nested screen or camera loses rounded corners; CU's Auto Zoom
  on a side-by-side screen fills the canvas (the remedy is a nest; CU-75 refuses it).
- **Vertical versions.** A 1080p source upscaled ×1.78 looks soft (the guide says shoot 4K); the wrong
  subject can win (a poster, a monitor face); composition inside existing actions is approximate and
  re-eases split actions (counted); a moving motion preset is kept and excluded from coverage; the
  decoder budget warns past 8; VR-41 changes Subtitles and Text ▸ Presets on every portrait project
  (landscape and square byte-identical); graphics written by people or agents may overflow a tall frame;
  the copy drifts from the master until linked versions.
- **Several 4K angles and multi-hour files are unmeasured** until SW-S2: cuts between long-GOP files may
  hitch (SW2c), a thousand-shot rebuild may be slow, four live 4K decodes beside the program may exceed
  the decoders; SW-S2 costs about 34 GB and up to an hour of encoding. A shortfall is a recorded limit
  and a Performance issue; no proxies are built.
- **Audio streams.** AVFoundation's handling of many-channel streams is unmeasured (SW-S1 picks the tap
  or a mono copy at about 0.5 GB an hour per channel); its stream order may differ from the container's;
  iPhone Spatial Audio may add undecodable tracks; media imported before SW3a need a relink to the same
  file; per-source caches multiply sync and speech files; link groups rewrite every link rule.
- **The switch trusts the placement;** a slipped or moved shot falls out of sync, and one bleed margin
  will not suit every room (SW-S4 tunes it; the sheet exposes it). Mouth activity fails on profiles,
  small faces, beards and hands (SW-S3 gates SW8).
- **Shared files across three lanes.** The layer stage, the recipe, `LayerUniforms`, the recorder panel,
  `op_rows.rs`, `edit.rs`, `scope.rs`, `ReelOps.swift`, the menus, `UIMenuTable.swift`,
  `inventory.json`, the decision file, the spec index and the pinned counts take rows from several
  lanes; the integrator resolves them one landing at a time (CJ-6, CJ-8), and T8 moves the busiest two
  out of a frozen file. Provisional format numbers (ten, eleven with VR7a) are renumbered at landing.
- **`ReelCore.swift`'s room runs out.** Only four doc blocks are left to cut and the wrappers need more
  (CJ0a's question 6).
- **The helper is shared with Rasterize.** FC5's diff must land in both, or `agent/src` stops being one
  file set.
- **The assistant's search guide** is at 1,498 of 1,500 characters; FC's clips row must take words from
  other rows (F6 checks it).
- **Samples may not come.** Quality claims then rest on JOB rows, and CJ-S2's face share, S-KEY1's
  ground truth and S-EV's recall stay owed. The samples are personal and are never committed or sent
  without a spike's flags and the month's budget.
- **The trials may reorder the road map** (an amendment of CJ-2).
- **API drift.** Apple may deprecate the `VN*` classes for the `async`-only Swift API; W-8 confines
  `async`, so that would need a decision.

## Questions asked at phase time

Each with its recommendation; the phase asks before its code, and the answer is recorded with its
decisions.

## Not in this road map

- **The survey's next tier**, neither in nor out: Proposals (an agent's multi-step edit played before it
  lands; amends AI-10) and Recipes; Punch in on cuts (it would read TX-42's cuts); source ranges on
  `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip`, skimming, In and Out on media and favourite ranges (no
  bet needs them: TX-41 composes its own primitives and FC places by `keep_range`); caption styles, a
  brand kit and project templates (W-10); the publish polish slice (a 00:00 chapter list, safe-zone
  overlays, named platform export rows); `search_media` over cached transcripts; merging the in-app
  tutorials after TU4; optical-flow slow motion; WebVTT import and translated captions.
- **The survey's "Not worth chasing"**, unchanged: generative media and dubbing; direct upload,
  scheduling and analytics; stock libraries and a template marketplace; eye contact and retouching;
  cloud sync, collaboration, mobile and Windows; remote guests and live multi-camera capture; a
  virality score (FC-67 forbids one); a standalone footage index; script-to-cut; translated subtitle
  tracks as a bet; a publish kit; more MCP surface as a headline; stabilisation for now; live-compositor
  motion blur beyond CU11; a plugin system; pro finishing; analytics-driven features.
- **Lifted by CJ-1 and not built here:** other platforms, a plugin system and scripting beyond graphics
  (G-1 stands), third-party Audio Unit hosting (AU-2 stands), stabilisation, optical-flow retiming,
  proxies (only after a measured shortfall, as a Performance issue), and GR-20 and GR-27…GR-30.
- **Language models:** Apple FoundationModels, any on-device language-model fallback, an on-device filler
  pass (TR-7 stands), a Frame Job relay or account (C2, #125 stays iced), the Keychain for keys (R6-5's
  measured reason stands).
- **Put out by the bets** (filed as candidates at the close where useful): editing a word's text;
  background fills on import; a detachable transcript window and Find (⌘F) unless chosen; a merge op
  rejoining restored halves; diarisation without AssemblyAI; script-first recording, a teleprompter,
  regenerated speech, translation (TX). Reconstructing a cursor for older or imported recordings;
  typed text as overlays (an "all keys" mode); click sounds, cursor packs and styles beyond As recorded
  and Arrow; other callouts (arrows, highlights); a global record hotkey; frame interpolation for
  sped-up typing; live auto zoom while recording; recording an iOS device's screen (CU). Masks or any

content.text:
I wrote the road map to `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/designs/creator-jobs.md` (5,888 lines; no other file in the repo was touched). It folds in all seven sections with the challenge notes left out, and prose is wrapped at 100 columns. Rewrapping changed no words, bullets, tables or headings. Nothing was gated, since the file isn't in a worktree yet.

**Phase order with lanes.** CJ0a runs alone first. Then CJ0b, CJ0c and CJ0d run at once in A, B and C.
- **Lane A (words):** CJ0b → CJ1 → TX1 → TX2a → TX2b → TX3 → **CP1**, the owner's checkpoint, cutting T1 by deleting words. TX4 waits for CP1's verdict; CJ5a is built meanwhile. Then TX4 → TX5 → TX6 → TX7 → CJ5b (TX8, the closing trial, runs beside it) → FC3 → FC4 → FC5 → FC6 → FC7a → FC7b → FC8a → FC8b → FC9 → SW3a → SW3b → SW4a → SW4b → SW5 → SW6 → SW7b.
- **Lane B (recorder and placement):** CJ0c → CU0a → CU0b → CU1a → CU1b → CU2 → CU3a → CU3b → CU3c → CU4 → CU5 → CU6 → CU7 → CU8 → CU9a → CU9b → CU10 → CU11 → CO6 → CO7 → CO8 → CO9 → SW7a. CU12, the owner's screen-tutorial trial, runs beside it.
- **Lane C (pictures):** CJ0d → CJ2a → CJ2b → CO0 → CO1 → CO2a → CO2b → CO3 → CO4 → CO5 → CO10 → CJ3 → VR1 → VR2a → VR2b → VR3 → VR4 → VR5 → CJ6 → SW0 → SW1 → SW2a → SW2b → SW2c (only if SW-S2 (a) earns it) → SW8 → VR6 → SW9a → SW9b. VR7a → VR7b → VR8 → VR9 follow only on the owner's yes at VR7a, in whichever lane is free.

**Format bumps.** Ten are planned: CU3a, CO2a, CO5, CO10, CU11, SW3a, CO9, SW7a, SW4b and SW6. VR7a would make eleven. All are provisional from 38 and renumbered at landing.

**Questions for the owner at CJ0a, before any code:**
1. Merge into main per phase or at the close? *Recommended: per phase.*
2. Lift §2's "Left out" list along with §1's? *Recommended: yes.*
3. Where do real samples live, and which will you record when? *Recommended: `tools/proof/media/creator/`.*
4. Survey decision 8 — measure several 4K angles and multi-hour files (about 34 GB of fixtures) as SW0? *Recommended: yes.*
5. "Remove all explicit non-goals" read literally also lifts GR-20, GR-27…GR-30 and §1's AU-2 and G-1 clauses. Read it that way? *Recommended: yes; nothing on that list is built.*
6. Once `ReelCore.swift`'s doc cuts are spent, may a `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` file call `rc_*`? *Recommended: yes.*

About 70 more questions are listed by phase under "Questions asked at phase time", each with a recommendation.

**What I could not reconcile cleanly, and how I settled it:**
- **`keep_range` and New Project from Range.** cj.md retired CJ5, but fc.md and vr.md both depend on CJ5. I kept it as two shared phases, CJ5a and CJ5b. No CJ-50/CJ-51 text existed anywhere, so I wrote CJ-50…CJ-52 from FC's N1–N7. Two points are left for CJ5a's design pass: a nest clip straddling a range edge (drafted as a refusal), and what else a range leaves unused.
- **SW's lane request is not adopted.** SW asked for its audio-track phases between TX and FC. I put them after FC to follow the lead-segment order, so SW4b moves FC's and TX's per-media readers too. The owner can swap them.
- **`ReelCore.swift` room.** The four remaining doc blocks free less than the planned wrappers need (CU's three cursor exports, TX4, SW9a). This is why question 6 exists.
- **Two composition-plan options exports.** VR7b's `rc_project_composition_plan_opts` and SW9a's `rc_project_composition_plan_with` are now one export, `_opts`, built by SW9a; VR7b adds a `framing` key.
- **Samples.**
  - S-TH1 is the GH5 in Rec. 709, as in cj.md; TX, VR and CO said iPhone.
  - VR's S-VR1 is folded into S-TH4 (iPhone HLG).
  - S-PC2 stays SW's one-microphone, camera-each recording. A new S-PC3 (a two-shot with a microphone each) covers VR6, VR-S3 and CO's two-person masks.
  - CO's S-TH3 hard cases are S-TH5, and S-GS1 is S-KEY1.
- **Spikes and identity.**
  - CO-S4 is merged into CJ-S3 (b).
  - CO-1's compute device comes from CJ-S2's rule 1.
  - No face or person ids are stored (CJ-31). VR's planner links tracks in the core, so VR1's id proof row moved to VR2a's core tests, and SW-81 takes each sample's largest face.
- **IDs and numbers.**
  - Manual checks are renumbered into blocks: TX 10–15, CU 20–28, FC 40–44. CJ's JOB-1 and JOB-2 are not trial rows.
  - The multicam scope decision is SW-3, because SW-1 and SW-2 are taken by SW0.
  - CO8's recorder keys come after CU's sixteen.
  - TX-70 is recorded at CJ0a, per cj.md, rather than at TX7's head.
  - CJ-4's "third grant" is corrected to "fourth".
- **Worktree.** I used the task's `.claude/worktrees/creator-jobs` rather than cj.md's `~/devel/framejob-creator-jobs`.
- **Unchecked facts the plan depends on.**
  - Whether macOS shows a tooltip on a disabled menu item: a check at CJ1's head, with a fallback question.
  - Whether five tab titles fit at 280 pt: TX2a's T1 measures it.
